- Yazelix/anima
- Yazelix/yazi-bistro
- Yazelix/auto-layout.yazi
- Yazelix/zjstatus
- Yazelix/starcompass

Resolve this inventory again before final closure.

## Verified Public State — 2026-08-10

A remote read-only audit checked canonical repository HEADs or Nova's selected branch at exact revisions:

| Repository | Audited revision | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mars | `21109e3ebc24b63da11bae644dfb9bab28ce0e18` | Canonical URLs published; no live unclassified stale identity found |
| Cursors | `2383c2e6a5484379414434f9d572421f440722c7` | URLs published, but README still calls the repository `yazelix-cursors` at lines 120 and 141 |
| Nova Zellij | `bbccdea6eda81f314151160f9b3f8882a26478ec` | Selected Nova branch clean |
| Nova Helix | `2c3701a30c0d4abf893689ef5a8ef9e2929f67c7` | Canonical fork name and contributor URL published |
| Zellij Pane Orchestrator | `e76ae565f0dc25844293544bf9b58a6dcf127947` | Canonical URLs published |
| Zellij Popup | `2e75b1f409b2f9668a1eac6c81f99f64007c0dfd` | Canonical URLs published |
| Zellij Status Kit | `0908737a19d22c9d8d12946dbbd82f6b3a170837` | Canonical repository name and URLs published; legacy package/artifact names explicitly preserved |
| Ratconfig | `675a21f17900df47585b2a8290c5436204d120e4` | Canonical URLs published |
| Anima | `d22d091d427af0be307056c65e475802b602d386` | Canonical product/repository name and URLs published; `yzs` remains stable |
| Yazi Bistro | `eef407e9eae250ff73b0ff9852d4ed41e14ef73b` | Contributor policy points to Nova; no stale identity found |
| auto-layout.yazi | `df562160ea1d86d16c83af632d0d5bb9c0a927b7` | Remote tree and README clean |
| zjstatus | `a9859a94aaa745339a3e7933d97bd9d2777855d4` | Nova-selected branch clean |
| Starcompass | `621bc6fcec916521c116e89d1ae8b146973145d5` | Source identity and self-adoption output point to Yazelix |

The original sample inspected local checkouts that were one or two commits behind their public branches. Those stale local files are not evidence of remaining public defects.

The original claim that several child `AGENTS.md` files are generated was wrong. The child files inspected here are direct repository instructions. Nova and Starcompass root `AGENTS.md` files are generated and must still be changed through their declared sources/renderers.

## Remaining Work

1. Correct Cursors README repository-name prose while preserving the Yazelix Cursors product name and existing package/crate identifiers.
2. After that child publishes, update only the Nova child pins whose delivered Nix or Cargo metadata still comes from pre-canonicalization revisions: Mars, Cursors, Zellij Pane Orchestrator, Zellij Popup, Zellij Status Kit, Ratconfig, and Anima.
3. Re-run the public inventory and record intentional compatibility or historical occurrences explicitly.

## Scope

In scope:

- Live README prose, manifests, Nix metadata, contributor instructions, badges, install examples, and source URLs.
- Exact published child revisions and the minimum Nova lock/Cargo pin transaction needed to consume corrected delivered metadata.
- One child Bead per remaining independently reviewable repository cleanup; use Nova's tracker with explicit source metadata when a child has no repository-local tracker.

Out of scope:

- Renaming crates, binaries, flake outputs, installed paths, plugin identifiers, configuration keys, or stable artifact names solely for branding.
- Rewriting history, Beads history, changelog history, archived planning evidence, lockfile provenance strings that name immutable old sources, or third-party/private links that remain canonical.
- Updating Nova pins for children whose only published change is contributor prose or CI and whose delivered metadata is already canonical.
- Creating new Beads trackers in child repositories that do not already own one.

## Verification

- Search every current public audited revision for personal namespaces and retired repository URLs, excluding Beads state, historical changelogs/archives, vendored sources, and immutable lock provenance.
- `git ls-remote` must resolve every canonical repository and exact selected branch.
- Each implementation child must pass its repository-specific instructions plus `git diff --check`.
- Metadata edits must pass `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1` and/or `nix flake metadata --no-write-lock-file` as applicable.
- Nova's final pin transaction must pass its runtime-flake verification and installed-artifact checks.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before replacing a URL when the canonical target or referenced object cannot be verified.
- Stop and request a compatibility decision if cleanup would rename a public non-repository surface.
- Stop before editing a generated file without its declared source and renderer.
- Stop a repository when its required branch, authority, or publication path is unavailable.

## Maintenance Notes

Use verified replacements, not a global search-and-replace. Public Git redirects are migration aids, not canonical metadata. Local checkout lag is operational state and does not justify a repository cleanup Bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every current first-party child, fork, and Starcompass has an exact audited public revision and a classified result.
- No live public README, manifest, Nix metadata, contributor instruction, badge, install example, or source link carries an unclassified personal namespace or retired repository URL.
- Cursors distinguishes the Yazelix Cursors product and stable package identifiers from the canonical `Yazelix/cursors` repository.
- Nova consumes published canonical metadata revisions only where its delivered package or Cargo metadata otherwise remains stale.
- Stable crate, command, flake-output, plugin, artifact, path, and configuration names are unchanged unless separately approved.
- Historical/immutable occurrences and intentional compatibility names are recorded rather than rewritten.
- Repository-specific checks and Nova's final runtime-flake and installed-artifact gates pass at the exact accepted revisions.
notes:
Planning reconciliation on 2026-08-10 replaced the stale-local-checkout sample with exact public-remote evidence.

Remaining sequence:

1. `yazelix-5vl-469.1` — finish two Cursors README repository-name statements and publish the child.
2. `yazelix-5vl-469.2` — consume only the published child identity/metadata revisions in Nova; blocked by .1.

No implementation Beads were created for Mars, Nova Zellij, Nova Helix, Zellij Pane Orchestrator, Zellij Popup, Zellij Status Kit, Ratconfig, Anima, Yazi Bistro, auto-layout.yazi, zjstatus, or Starcompass because their audited public revisions are already clean. Their lagging local checkouts were intentionally left untouched. The direct child AGENTS.md files are not generated; only repositories whose own manifest says so, including Nova and Starcompass, use generated root instructions.

title: Finish Cursors repository-name canonicalization
description:
## Why

Cursors published the canonical repository move in `2383c2e6a5484379414434f9d572421f440722c7`, but two README sentences still identify the repository itself as `yazelix-cursors`. The canonical repository is `Yazelix/cursors`; the Yazelix Cursors product name and existing crate, package, and flake-output identifiers remain valid compatibility surfaces.

## Evidence

- Public `main` revision `2383c2e6a5484379414434f9d572421f440722c7` updates AGENTS.md, Cargo.toml, install examples, and flake homepage to `Yazelix/cursors`.
- `README.md:120` says the repository is named `yazelix-cursors`.
- `README.md:141` says `Product/repository: yazelix-cursors`.
- The repository has no local Beads tracker, so Nova's cross-repository epic owns this implementation issue with explicit Cursors source metadata.

## Contract

Public Cursors documentation distinguishes:

- product: Yazelix Cursors;
- canonical repository: `Yazelix/cursors`;
- stable implementation/package names such as `yazelix-cursors`, `yazelix_cursors`, and `yzc` where the current crate, Nix, artifact, or command contract uses them.

## Scope

In scope:

- Fast-forward or otherwise begin from the exact published canonicalization revision.
- Correct the two README repository-identity statements.
- Re-run the live tracked-content identity search and classify any remaining retired terms as product/package compatibility or historical evidence.

Out of scope:

- Renaming the crate, package, flake output, source derivation, command, config paths, registry schema, or shader assets.
- Editing AGENTS.md again unless its already-published canonical Nova URL has regressed.
- Rewriting changelog history, lock provenance, or third-party references.

## Implementation Notes

1. Read the Cursors AGENTS.md and start from public main at or after `2383c2e6a5484379414434f9d572421f440722c7`.
2. Change only repository-name prose; keep product and stable package identifiers explicit.
3. Publish the child commit before Nova consumes it.

## Verification

- `rg -n -i 'github\\.com/luccahuguet|github:luccahuguet|luccahuguet/yazelix|Product/repository: yazelix-cursors|repository is named .yazelix-cursors' . --hidden --glob '!.git/**' --glob '!.beads/**' --glob '!target/**' --glob '!Cargo.lock' --glob '!flake.lock'` should find no live unclassified occurrence.
- `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1` should exit 0 and report `https://github.com/Yazelix/cursors` as repository metadata.
- `nix flake metadata --no-write-lock-file` should exit 0.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the canonical public main revision no longer contains the cited statements.
- Stop and request a compatibility decision if a proposed edit would rename a package, crate, command, flake output, artifact, or config path.
- Stop before publication if the local branch cannot fast-forward safely because of user-owned changes.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort S. Risk LOW. Confidence HIGH. Rejected: global replacement of every `yazelix-cursors` token, because most remaining tokens are stable implementation/package names rather than repository identity.
acceptance_criteria:
- README names `Yazelix/cursors` as the canonical repository while preserving Yazelix Cursors as the product name.
- Existing `yzc`, `yazelix-cursors`, `yazelix_cursors`, flake-output, config, and shader contracts remain unchanged.
- The live identity search has no unclassified personal-namespace or retired-repository occurrence.
- Cargo metadata and Nix flake metadata resolve successfully and advertise the canonical repository.
- The child commit is published before the Nova consumer issue starts.

README distinguishes the Yazelix Cursors product from the canonical Yazelix/cursors repository while preserving yzc, yazelix-cursors, yazelix_cursors, flake-output, config, and shader identifiers. Verified on Linux at that exact clean revision: identity rg scan returned no live unclassified occurrence; cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 reported https://github.com/Yazelix/cursors; nix flake metadata --no-write-lock-file resolved revision e0f8bc9492dbfaaf498cef47d543010f4abb2b8f; git diff --check passed; origin/main resolved to the same revision.

title: Audit and retire stale Yazelix worktrees
description:
## Why

Yazelix currently registers three secondary worktrees in addition to the primary checkout. They include one known disposable repin worktree, one worktree whose `.git` file points at a moved/nonexistent administrative directory, and one clean but historically divergent audit branch. Blind deletion could discard untracked files or branch-only work, while leaving all of them indefinitely creates workspace and branch ambiguity.

## Evidence

- `git worktree list --porcelain` on 2026-07-16 listed the primary checkout plus `yazelix_light_mode`, `yazelix_rust_loc_audit`, and detached `yazelix-mars-repin-20260716`.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix` is the primary `main` checkout at `79a18c0a`, two commits behind `origin/main`, with unrelated tracked modifications. It must not be deleted or reset as part of this cleanup.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix-mars-repin-20260716` is detached at `dc197a1a`, clean, fully contained in `origin/main`, and was created only for the Mars repin transaction.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/worktrees/yazelix_light_mode/.git` points to nonexistent `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix/.git/worktrees/yazelix_light_mode`, so ordinary `git -C ... status` fails. Its branch tip is `67371615` (`feat: add yzxterm appearance handling`), it has no remote branch, and it has no merge base with current `origin/main`.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/worktrees/yazelix_rust_loc_audit` is clean at `b05ea629` (`Refresh Rust LOC ownership audit`), has no remote branch, and has no merge base with current `origin/main`.

## Scope

In scope:
- Inventory every registered Yazelix worktree, its administrative metadata, status, branch/ref, remote publication, reachability, and unique work.
- Treat all secondary worktrees as removal candidates, but preserve any dirty, untracked, or still-useful branch-only work before removal.
- Repair the stale `yazelix_light_mode` worktree pointer temporarily if needed to obtain a trustworthy status, or make a filesystem-level backup before any manual cleanup.
- Decide whether the two old branch tips contain anything worth porting to current Nova; preserve selected work as explicit beads/commits rather than keeping ambiguous worktrees indefinitely.
- Remove safe secondary worktrees with `git worktree remove`, then prune stale administrative entries and optionally delete obsolete local branches only after their tips are preserved or explicitly rejected.
- Leave the primary checkout and its current uncommitted changes intact; after secondary cleanup, report how its local `main` should be advanced safely.

Out of scope:
- Do not reset, clean, stash, commit, or delete files from the primary dirty checkout without separate maintainer approval.
- Do not force-delete an uninspectable or unmerged worktree merely to reduce the count.
- Do not port light-mode or Rust-audit code in this bead; create focused follow-ups for anything deliberately retained.
- Do not delete remote branches or rewrite repository history.

## Implementation Notes

1. Fetch `origin/main` and capture `git worktree list --porcelain`, `git branch -vv`, and `git worktree prune --dry-run --verbose`.
2. For every secondary path, record `git status --porcelain=v1`, HEAD, branch, upstream, remote branch existence, and reachability from `origin/main`.
3. For `yazelix_light_mode`, first preserve the directory, then use `git worktree repair` or the main repository metadata to restore inspection. If status still cannot be trusted, stop before deletion and present the backup/recovery choice.
4. For branch-only histories with no merge base, inspect the tip tree and a bounded set of relevant commits rather than assuming thousands of historical commits are intentional unique work.
5. Remove only worktrees classified as clean and disposable, using normal `git worktree remove`; use `--force` only with explicit maintainer approval after preservation evidence.
6. Run `git worktree prune`, verify the final list, and record retained branches/worktrees and their reasons.

## Verification

- `git worktree list --porcelain` should show only the primary checkout plus any explicitly retained worktrees.
- `git worktree prune --dry-run --verbose` should report no stale administrative entries after cleanup.
- `git status --porcelain=v1` in the primary checkout should show the same pre-existing user changes; cleanup must not alter them.
- Every removed branch tip must either be reachable from a retained ref, recorded in an explicit backup ref, or documented as intentionally discarded with maintainer approval.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before deletion if a worktree is dirty, contains untracked files, cannot be inspected reliably, or has useful work not preserved elsewhere.
- Stop before deleting any local branch whose tip is not reachable from a retained ref unless the maintainer explicitly rejects that work.
- Stop if repairing worktree metadata would overwrite the primary checkout metadata or working files.

## Maintenance Notes

- Effort: S-M. Risk: MED because two old branches are unrelated to current Nova history. Confidence: HIGH that the temporary repin worktree is disposable; LOW until inspection for the stale light-mode directory; MED for retiring the Rust LOC audit worktree.
- Rejected alternative: delete every secondary directory immediately. Worktree count is less important than preserving unmerged or untracked work.
- Prefer a final state with one authoritative primary checkout and short-lived task worktrees that are removed after their commits are published.
close_reason: Removed all three secondary worktrees: detached Mars repin, clean Rust LOC audit, and repaired/forced stale light-mode. Preserved local branch refs yazelix_light_mode at 67371615 and yazelix_rust_loc_audit at b05ea629, so committed history remains recoverable. Explicit maintainer stale designation authorized discarding the light-mode worktree's sole uncommitted change: the obsolete in-progress Restore Linux Foot terminal variant planning line. Primary dirty checkout was not reset or otherwise altered. Final worktree list contains only the primary checkout and prune dry-run is empty.

title: Enable native Nushell clipboard commands
description:
## Contract

Consumer: a Nova user running the packaged managed Nushell.

Trigger: start Nushell through the existing yzx-nu launcher and invoke `clip copy`, `clip paste`, `clc`, or `clp`.

Observable result: the pinned native clipboard commands are available, including structured pipeline input such as `pwd | clip copy`. Managed Nushell also provides the documented convenience aliases `clc = clip copy` and `clp = clip paste`, so `pwd | clc` copies and `clp` pastes. Nova adds no external clipboard package, new configuration setting, or change to host Nushell and other shells.

Failure behavior: the exact packaged Nushell pin and delivered-shell check fail if the opt-in flag, native commands, or aliases disappear. Clipboard access failures remain native Nushell errors; Nova does not promise a local desktop clipboard in headless or remote environments.

## Ownership

yzx-nu owns the exact managed Nushell invocation and enables the pinned native-clip option. Nova's existing packaged Nu config owns the two managed aliases. Nushell owns clipboard serialization, platform APIs, command behavior, and errors.

## Scope

Add the single startup option and two direct aliases, extend the existing delivered-artifact check, add concise documentation and changelog coverage, keep exact LOC accounting, prove isolated package delivery, and obtain fresh-session Edge dogfood. Do not add wl-clipboard, OSC52 wrappers, a clipboard abstraction, another setting, or host-Nushell mutation.
notes:
Accepted native-command dogfood on 2026-08-24: a fresh installed Edge session successfully used `pwd | clip copy` and `clip paste`. The user then chose the documented `clc`/`clp` convenience aliases for the same managed Nushell surface.

Implemented candidate: yzx-nu enables Nushell 0.113.1's native-clip option; Nova's packaged Nu config directly aliases `clc = clip copy` and `clp = clip paste`; and the existing delivered-package contract resolves the configured shell, requires `help clip copy`, and checks both exact alias expansions. No external clipboard package, setting, wrapper, or host-shell mutation was added.

Proof on x86_64-linux (2026-08-24): `git diff --check`, Rust formatting, and exact 26,385-line accounting passed. The focused alias contract failed before the aliases and passed after them, including after its final environment simplification. `nix flake check` passed all 74 compatible checks; `nix flake show --all-systems` evaluated Linux and Darwin outputs; `nix build .#yazelix-edge` produced `/nix/store/5ji0if31i127b5f25xalgipr3hwf7qaq-yazelix`; isolated profile `/tmp/tmp.uq1kmVXWOn/profile` installed that path and its delivered shell reported `clc=clip copy` and `clp=clip paste`.

Acceptance: the user's installed Edge profile resolved the candidate at `/nix/store/5ji0if31i127b5f25xalgipr3hwf7qaq-yazelix` with both exact alias expansions, after which the user explicitly instructed commit and push.
close_reason: Native Nushell clipboard commands and documented clc/clp aliases implemented, verified, installed, and accepted

title: Document macOS XDG opt-in and declarative config source reuse
description:
## Why

A macOS Home Manager or nix-darwin user may prefer Linux-style XDG locations and one declarative source for configuration used both inside and outside Yazelix. Nova intentionally keeps its managed runtime under a Yazelix-owned namespaced tree and does not adopt ambient Helix, Yazi, Zellij, terminal, Starship, or shell files automatically. The supported answer needs concise documentation rather than another runtime integration mode.

## Outcome

Document two independent opt-in patterns:

1. How macOS users can deliberately export Linux-style XDG base directories through their own Home Manager or nix-darwin launchd configuration so GUI-launched and shell-launched tools see a consistent environment.
2. How Home Manager users can reuse the same source files for a normal host tool and the corresponding programs.yazelix.config native text/source option while installing them at separate owned destinations.

State clearly that XDG_CONFIG_HOME changes the base directory but Yazelix still uses its own yazelix subdirectory, and that declarative source reuse is not ambient-config adoption.

## Scope

- Provide one concise, current Home Manager or nix-darwin example for propagating appropriate XDG variables on macOS.
- Avoid prescribing an unsafe persistent XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; explain its lifecycle requirements or omit it from the general example.
- Provide representative shared-source examples for a safe native file such as Helix languages.toml or a Yazi override.
- Explain which Yazelix integration-owned configuration cannot be replaced wholesale, especially managed Zellij nodes and required Yazi or Helix bindings.
- Link the canonical Nova Home Manager text/source options and ownership diagnostics.
- Keep the documentation platform-aware and use public Yazelix Nova names after canonical cutover.

## Guardrails

- Add no runtime setting, global launchctl mutation, ambient-config reader, import side effect, or compatibility mode.
- Do not tell Yazelix to move, overwrite, or take ownership of native tool configuration.
- Do not imply that setting XDG_CONFIG_HOME makes ambient tool files control the managed runtime.

## Verification

- The documented Nix example evaluates on the intended macOS Home Manager or nix-darwin surface, or the untestable platform gap is stated explicitly.
- Paths and option names match the canonical Nova Home Manager module.
- The shared-source example installs the same immutable source at two explicit destinations without duplicate file content.
- Documentation clearly distinguishes XDG base selection, Yazelix namespacing, declarative source reuse, and ambient configuration.

title: Make Nova sponsorship prominent in the repository
description:
## Why

Nova exposes its funding link only at the end of a 442-line README. Readers can understand, install, or leave the project without seeing how to fund continued work. GitHub also has no repository-native funding configuration.

## Evidence

- `README.md:434-435`: the sole README funding CTA links to `https://github.com/sponsors/luccahuguet` near the bottom of the file.
- `README.md:442`: the README ends seven lines after the funding link.
- `runtime/yzx/cli.rs:383`: `yzx help` already treats the same GitHub Sponsors URL as canonical.
- `.github/FUNDING.yml`: absent, so GitHub cannot expose its native Sponsor button from repository configuration.

## Scope

In scope:
- Make sponsorship visible in the README introduction or another above-the-fold repository surface.
- Add the native GitHub Sponsors configuration for `luccahuguet` if GitHub still supports that syntax.
- Keep one canonical destination: `https://github.com/sponsors/luccahuguet`.
- Move or consolidate the existing bottom CTA so the README does not accumulate competing funding copy.
- Update the README LOC scorecard after the tracked documentation change.

Out of scope:
- Sponsor tiers, funding goals, payment processing, supporter lists, badges from third-party services, or runtime command changes.
- Reworking the README structure beyond the smallest placement change.
- Changing the canonical sponsor account.

## Implementation Notes

1. Verify the current official GitHub `.github/FUNDING.yml` syntax before editing.
2. Add one short, direct funding CTA near the project introduction or primary install path.
3. Reuse the canonical URL already present in `yzx help`; do not introduce a redirect or link service.
4. Remove or relocate redundant bottom copy rather than showing the same appeal twice.
5. Recalculate the README LOC scorecard using the repository command in `docs/development.md`.

## Verification

- `rg -n "github.com/sponsors/luccahuguet" README.md runtime/yzx/cli.rs .github/FUNDING.yml` should show the canonical account on each intended surface and no alternate funding destination.
- Inspect the rendered GitHub README and confirm the CTA appears before the first long reference section.
- GitHub should show the native Sponsor action after the funding configuration reaches the default branch.
- Run the LOC scorecard command in `docs/development.md`; its total should match the updated README scorecard.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if GitHub no longer supports the proposed funding-file syntax or the account is not enabled for Sponsors.
- Stop if a prominent placement requires restructuring unrelated README content.
- Stop if the canonical funding account changes.

## Maintenance Notes

- Effort: S. Risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH.
- Use GitHub native funding metadata and a plain README link; add no dependency or service.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A direct sponsor CTA appears near the top of the README before long reference material.
- [ ] The CTA points to `https://github.com/sponsors/luccahuguet`.
- [ ] `.github/FUNDING.yml` enables the native GitHub Sponsor surface, if supported.
- [ ] Redundant bottom funding copy is moved or consolidated.
- [ ] The README LOC scorecard matches the tracked tree.

title: Apply appearance mode coherently through Rio capability
description:
## Contract

Consumer: a user changing root appearance.mode from Ratconfig inside a managed Nova session.

Trigger: save appearance.mode as dark or light.

Observable result: Nova preserves one integrated appearance across Rio, Ratconfig, the addressed Zellij session and bar, and newly opened managed Yazi processes. A session whose Rio config projected successfully at launch changes live through Rio native config watcher plus the native Zellij action. A session whose Rio config is Home Manager-owned, read-only, or failed projection keeps its captured appearance and applies the saved root mode everywhere in the next session.

Failure behavior: Nova does not switch Zellij or Ratconfig unless Rio projection succeeds. A session launched with live capability refuses an appearance save if Rio becomes read-only mid-session, preserving coherence. Projection failure during launch selects the next-session capability and keeps Rio --theme-mode. A failed Zellij action rolls the root and Rio projection back.

## Ownership

Root appearance.mode is the integrated policy owner. Nova owns only Rio top-level force-theme field and capability selection. Every other Rio field remains native and user-owned. Rio owns file watching, palette selection, route updates, and redraw. Zellij owns its native theme action and bar mode event.

## Scope

Nova-only projection, launch selection, session environment, Ratconfig coordination, Yazi selection, focused contracts, current-state docs, changelog, and LOC scorecard. No Rio watcher, IPC, polling, relaunch, source patch, split appearance settings, compatibility aliases, or additional mirrored Rio fields.
design: The installed yzx-config helper projects force-theme with Ratconfig formatting-preserving TOML editing and returns live or next-launch. yzx launch and yzx enter project before starting a new session. Live launch omits Rio --theme-mode; fallback launch retains it. The launcher captures YZX_APPEARANCE_MODE and YZX_APPEARANCE_LIVE for Ratconfig and later Yazi opens. Ratconfig performs Rio projection, sparse root save, and the exact-session Zellij action as one coordinated update with rollback. Fallback sessions resolve Ratconfig and Yazi from the captured mode while persisting the desired root mode for the next session.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Writable projection changes only Rio force-theme and preserves surrounding native TOML.
2. Writable launch omits Rio --theme-mode and captures live capability.
3. Read-only or failed projection launch retains Rio --theme-mode and freezes the session appearance.
4. Live Ratconfig save updates Rio, Ratconfig, the addressed Zellij session and bar, and later Yazi opens; failures do not leave a mixed saved state.
5. Fallback Ratconfig save persists the desired root mode without repainting the current session; later Yazi opens stay captured.
6. Nova checks, package build, isolated activation, and fresh-session dogfood support acceptance.
notes: Accepted on 2026-08-22. Mechanically verified on x86_64-linux from the edge candidate: nix flake check passed; nix flake show --all-systems evaluated all advertised outputs; nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs passed; disposable profile activation identified Yazelix Nova 1.1.0. Installed contract coverage proves writable and read-only projection, both Rio launch argument shapes, captured environment markers, and Yazi fallback precedence. Fresh-session dogfood through the isolated Yazelix Nova (Rio Appearance Candidate) confirmed that integrated appearance switching works.
close_reason: Accepted after packaged fresh-session dogfood

title: Add a persistent per-tab Yazi workspace popup
description:
## Why

The managed sidebar is useful as a compact editor companion, but it is not a comfortable full-screen browser for exploratory navigation. Yazelix needs one persistent Yazi popup before global zoxide and workspace-selection behavior can be designed without treating Yazi as a one-shot fzf wrapper.

## User-visible contract

- `Alt Shift Y` toggles one managed Yazi popup in the active tab from any unlocked focus state.
- The popup launches at the orchestrator-owned canonical workspace root.
- Toggling or displacing the popup hides it instead of terminating it. Reopening at the same canonical root preserves the live Yazi process, cwd, cursor, and in-memory navigation state.
- If the canonical root changes while the popup is hidden, the existing popup lifecycle may discard the stale process and launch a fresh Yazi at the new requested root.
- The popup uses the same managed Yazi package, layered user configuration, themes, plugins, preview tools, and ordinary editor opener as the sidebar.
- The popup has an explicit workspace-popup role and never registers itself as the managed sidebar. Popup navigation must not replace sidebar identity, move the tiled sidebar, or redefine the tab workspace.
- Ordinary file opens retain the existing `yzx-open` contract: requested targets reach the editor while ordinary navigation does not retarget the canonical workspace.

## Scope

- Add one packaged `yazi` popup specification using the existing popup plugin and pane orchestrator.
- Add the fixed, documented `Alt Shift Y` key and reserve the packaged popup id/title and key collision.
- Reuse the existing `yzx-yazi` launcher with the smallest private role marker needed to omit sidebar-only registration and presentation behavior.
- Use the existing hide-on-toggle lifecycle; do not add disk persistence or a second state store.
- Update current-state docs, changelog, key inventory, generated-config contract, and README LOC scorecard.

## Out of scope

- Moving global `Alt z`, launching zoxide automatically, choosing a workspace commit key, retargeting, or resynchronizing the sidebar after a commit. The dependent Alt-z bead owns that workflow.
- A configurable Yazi-popup key, general popup settings, multiple Yazi popup roles, general file picking, search, layout redesign, or sidebar hide-on-open behavior.
- Child-repository changes unless a focused failing contract proves the existing generic popup/orchestrator capabilities insufficient.

## Verification

- Generated config contains one hide-policy Yazi popup launched through the managed Yazi role at canonical workspace cwd and one global `Alt Shift Y` orchestrator binding.
- The popup id/title and key cannot be shadowed by a custom popup.
- The popup role does not register `YAZI_ID` as sidebar state; the ordinary tiled Yazi still does.
- Existing sidebar `Alt z`, ordinary Yazi opens, sidebar registration, and all other popup lifecycles remain unchanged.
- Focused Rust and contract checks, `nix flake check`, `nix flake show --all-systems`, `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs`, and a clean temporary-profile install pass.
- Manual dogfood, when explicitly requested, verifies hide/show state preservation from editor, shell, sidebar, and sidebar-hidden focus states.

## Rejected alternatives

A one-shot Yazi process that immediately runs fzf and exits was rejected because it prevents navigation and uses Yazi only as a wrapper. Reusing the tiled sidebar was rejected because workspace browsing should not require sidebar focus or mutate sidebar-local state.
acceptance_criteria: A fixed global `Alt Shift Y` toggles one per-tab managed Yazi popup at the canonical workspace root. The popup uses the existing managed Yazi configuration and hide lifecycle, preserves live navigation state while the root is unchanged, restarts when its requested canonical root becomes stale, and cannot register as or mutate the tiled sidebar. Ordinary navigation and opens retain existing workspace semantics. This bead does not change `Alt z`, launch zoxide, or add a workspace commit action.
notes: Implemented the first split slice only. Alt Shift Y now toggles one per-tab managed Yazi popup through the pane orchestrator at the canonical workspace root. The packaged popup uses hide-on-toggle persistence and the existing managed Yazi launcher/config/opener. A private workspace-popup role prevents sidebar-state and sidebar-status registration, so popup navigation does not replace or move the tiled sidebar. Existing sidebar Alt z remains unchanged for the dependent bead. Verification passed: focused launcher tests (2), yzx-tutor tests (12), pinned yzx-config tests (48), pinned materialization/contracts builds, nix flake check, nix flake show --all-systems, nix build .#yazelix, temporary-profile installation, crate-specific rustfmt checks, git diff --check, and nix profile upgrade --refresh yazelix. GUI dogfood was not launched because repository instructions require an explicit request.
close_reason: Persistent per-tab Yazi popup implemented and verified; Alt-z intentionally remains in the dependent bead.

title: Bound Zellij discovery when a session server is wedged
description:
Contract ZELLIJ-SESSION-PROBE-TIMEOUT-001.

Consumer: any Zellij command that discovers sessions, including a fresh Nova launch, list-sessions, attach, and generated-name startup.

Trigger: on Unix, a session socket accepts ConnStatus but its wedged server never replies.

Observable result: discovery stops waiting after five seconds, treats that socket as unavailable, and continues. One wedged session cannot block all Nova launches indefinitely; healthy discovery remains unchanged.

Failure behavior: do not kill or delete the wedged session automatically, do not alter Windows discovery, and do not add Nova-side watchdogs or process management.

Implement the smallest mechanism proposed upstream in zellij-org/zellij#5481, retain issue #5440 and PR provenance, publish the isolated fork revision, pin Nova to it, and verify the delivered package. Remove this fork delta when upstream ships equivalent behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The fork formats and passes zellij-utils tests. A Unix fixture that accepts the session status request but never replies proves discovery returns after roughly five seconds without deleting the socket. Nova pins the published fork revision, Linux flake checks pass, all declared systems evaluate, the default and edge packages build, and an isolated profile contains the exact candidate. The default and dogfood profiles are refreshed. Before publication, the exact committed Nova revision must also pass Linux CI, Darwin Package Smoke, and fresh-session manual dogfood.
notes:
Implemented in Nova Zellij commit 11708fc49cf85671011f81401ed48d3df0c1ebfe, published on candidate/v0.45.0 and pinned by the current Nova candidate. The change sets only a five-second Unix receive timeout after a successful session-socket connection. Windows is untouched; Nova adds no watchdog, stale-session deletion, or process killer. Provenance: upstream issue https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij/issues/5440 and proposed upstream fix https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij/pull/5481.

Verified on x86_64-linux: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo test -p zellij-utils (439 passed, 2 ignored); exact pinned Nix build; a silent-socket contract fixture returned No active zellij sessions found after about 5.3 seconds; nix flake check; nix flake show --all-systems; nix build .#yazelix; and an isolated profile install. The default and dedicated dogfood profiles resolve to /nix/store/0f3dy9g7qp7px8803jmz5pbbgglfcvli-yazelix, which contains /nix/store/ma736gxcqqbj8a2i6h0qdf253ayzf5ia-zellij-0.45.0. Real Darwin and a newly launched GUI dogfood session remain pending because the Nova candidate is not yet committed.

title: Consume synchronized Anima frames in the Nova welcome
description:
## Contract

Consumer: users invoking `yzx anima` or starting Nova through packaged `yzx launch` with the welcome enabled.

Trigger: Nova selects an Anima style directly, through `random`, or through the pre-Zellij welcome.

Result: Nova resolves `yzx-welcome` and `yzx anima` to exact published Anima commit `7ef0ec33378874bdf95b2f8fa156d5fb641017ac`. That accepted child delta adds the public `matrix` style, includes Matrix as an equally represented random animation family, hardens existing Game of Life, Kitty-frame, Mandelbrot, help/error-output, packaging, and renderer paths, adds typed truecolor half-block rendering with stricter terminal color resets, and encloses each complete native frame in one synchronized-output update. Nova's welcome enable/style/duration settings, failure continuation, and pre-Zellij ordering remain unchanged.

Important failures: a missing or failed welcome keeps the existing bounded diagnostic and continuation behavior. If the accepted child revision does not remove the reported progressive bottom flicker on the real Eonova launch path, keep this bead open and return the renderer defect to Anima; Nova must not mask it by disabling the welcome, lowering frame rate, changing art, sleeping, buffering ANSI, or moving the welcome after Zellij.

## Evidence and decision

The user observed on 2026-08-12 that the direct Eonova Game of Life welcome flickers progressively more toward the bottom, while the same animation launched after Zellij is stable.

- Inspected Nova identity: `5a673c059c454042085b191d5e8ec15c01b3d121` on `edge`.
- `flake.nix:46` owns the `yazelixScreen` input; `flake.nix:279-291` builds `yzx-welcome`; `runtime/yzx/cli.rs:197-233` inserts it only for `yzx launch`, before Zellij.
- Nova locks Anima `d22d091d427af0be307056c65e475802b602d386`.
- Published Anima `7ef0ec33378874bdf95b2f8fa156d5fb641017ac` descends through synchronized-frame commit `58396ac3c6649f035e04c6b22b19c2accc818a02`, which descends through `188c2618d7ad4115d7c23f4715f4d93ec4296f7c`. The first commit adds Matrix and the accepted hardening; the second closes Anima issue `yzs-emit-synchronized-frames-2tg` with synchronized frames.
- Nova subsequently advanced to exact descendant `7ef0ec33378874bdf95b2f8fa156d5fb641017ac`, adding the child-owned truecolor renderer without changing Nova welcome policy.
- On 2026-08-12 the user explicitly accepted both Matrix and the complete hardening delta rather than requiring a synchronization-only child revision.
- Zellij's stable nested rendering is comparison evidence, not a reason to make Zellij own the pre-Zellij welcome.

Impact: MED. Effort: S. Risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH.

## Scope

In scope:
- Advance only `yazelixScreen` to exact Anima commit `7ef0ec33378874bdf95b2f8fa156d5fb641017ac` and refresh only mechanically required lock metadata.
- Prove `yzx-welcome` and `yzx anima` resolve to that same package.
- Expose and document `matrix`, including its accepted participation in `random`.
- Accept the child-owned hardening without copying or reconstructing it in Nova.
- Obtain fresh maintainer dogfood of the packaged pre-Zellij Game of Life welcome on the reported Eonova path.
- Update current-state docs, changelog, command contracts, and the README LOC scorecard where repository policy requires them.

Out of scope:
- Nova-owned Anima source changes, Eon/Eonova/Orbit/Venus changes, Zellij changes, new Nova settings, capability detection, renderer forks, compatibility aliases, or unrelated input refreshes.

## Dependency and ownership decision

The existing Anima input remains the sole owner of animation styles, random-family selection, frame construction, terminal output, and cleanup. Nova owns exact child selection, public integration, and installed/fresh-session acceptance. No dependency or local Beads edge is added; the completed cross-repository prerequisite remains recorded by `external_ref`.

Rejected: a hidden Nova fork, source patch, ANSI wrapper, second renderer, disabled welcome, output-buffer heuristic, or unrelated input update.

## Acceptance

1. Nova's `yazelixScreen` lock node resolves exactly to `7ef0ec33378874bdf95b2f8fa156d5fb641017ac`; no unrelated input node changes.
2. Built `yzx-welcome` and `yzx anima` resolve to the same updated Anima package.
3. `yzx anima --help` exposes `matrix`; a bounded packaged Matrix run succeeds; the child-owned random pool includes Matrix with the accepted equal-family weighting.
4. Existing welcome enable/style/duration, failure continuation, and pre-Zellij ordering remain unchanged. Existing styles retain bounded resize, input-exit, terminal cleanup, and error behavior under the accepted child hardening.
5. Full mechanical, flake, package, and isolated-profile checks pass.
6. Fresh maintainer dogfood of the packaged pre-Zellij Game of Life welcome on the reported Eonova path no longer reproduces progressive bottom flicker. This bead owns rollout acceptance.
7. No Nova renderer code, new setting, compatibility promise, or unrelated input update is introduced.

## Verification

- Inspect the lock diff and prove only the intended Anima node closure changed.
- Extend the installed command contract to require `matrix` in Anima help.
- `nix flake check`
- `nix flake show --all-systems`
- `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs`
- Install the exact candidate into a disposable profile; exercise `yzx anima --help`, a bounded `matrix` run, and packaged `yzx-welcome`/Game of Life without launching a GUI.
- Refresh installed `yazelix-edge`; obtain fresh-session Eonova welcome dogfood from the maintainer.
- `git diff --check`; recompute the README LOC scorecard when handwritten files change.

## Stop conditions

Stop if the accepted child commit becomes unreachable, the lock update changes an unrelated input, either helper resolves to a different package, Matrix or existing bounded execution fails, or Eonova still flickers. Return renderer defects to Anima rather than adding a Nova workaround.
notes:
## Accepted state

Nova pins Anima `7ef0ec33378874bdf95b2f8fa156d5fb641017ac`, including Matrix, truecolor half-block rendering, stricter terminal resets, and synchronized native frames. Matrix remains in the welcome allowlist and installed help. Nova adds no renderer, adapter, setting, or compatibility path.

## Mechanical evidence

Refreshed at Nova Edge `5bc2306fd7ef46ea71dcf294d2dd33448a511a27` on x86_64-linux. The original verified candidate `9ef7f6530bac3b4296adbaa7b50eaef3c1716cf1` is an ancestor, and the exact Anima revision remains pinned.

title: Make Alt Shift A the default Anima key
description:
## Why

## Verification

title: Report Classic migration residue in yzx doctor
description: Add a read-only Classic-residue diagnostic to yzx doctor. Scan only the active Nova config and state roots. Report recognized Classic artifacts with their exact paths, whether Nova uses them, and whether ownership is certain or ambiguous. Never follow symlinks, never mutate, and keep residue as warnings rather than a doctor failure. Do not report current Nova yazi, zellij, helix, helix-steel, or logs state. Warn that external scripts may still reference residue. Extend the existing Classic-to-Nova README guidance. Owner: runtime/yzx/doctor.rs. Sources of truth: v17.12 generated-state contracts plus Nova paths/runtime owners. Rejected from this slice: archive or cleanup commands, automatic startup/activation work, active-session discovery, executing Classic state, compatibility aliases, public JSON/status schema changes, and classic/classic-bridge branch governance.
design: Keep detection in runtime/yzx/doctor.rs. Scan only active config/state roots. Treat configs/ and sessions/ as ambiguous because their contents are not provably Classic-owned; treat the exact regular Classic Nushell extern and fingerprint paths as certain; treat known backup filename matches and every final symlink as ambiguous. Walk fixed state paths one component at a time with symlink_metadata and stop at symlinked parents. Residue is informational and never changes doctor success. No archive command: Classic has no ownership manifest that makes whole-tree archival safe, and relevant live-session discovery is not a reliable cleanup guard.

When recognized Classic roots or migration files exist, it prints one warning per exact path with nova=unused and ownership=certain or ownership=ambiguous, followed by the external-consumer warning. Symlinks are never followed and are always ambiguous. Current Nova yazi, zellij, helix, helix-steel, and logs paths are never reported. Residue does not change the successful doctor exit status and no file is created, moved, deleted, or rewritten by the scanner. title: Clear hidden-tab agent activity without focusing it
description:
Why
Nova's base agent-tab-decoration feature needs a separate correctness boundary for activity that ends while its tab is hidden or unfocused. Classic sometimes left the busy marker visible until the user focused that tab. Focus must not be an acknowledgement mechanism for agent state.

User-visible contract
If agent activity ends on tab A while tab B is focused, tab A's activity decoration clears promptly without focusing or visiting tab A. The same rule applies when the agent popup is hidden, moved with its tab, or exits.

Dependency
This regression is meaningful only after yazelix-fix-agent-tab-rename-vo44-on5 establishes a truthful Nova activity signal and pipe-backed tab decoration.

Current sources of truth
- yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator owns per-pane activity facts, reduces them to an all-tab snapshot keyed by tab id, and publishes pipe_tab_activity.
- terminal_title_activity_state already removes activity when a spinner-prefixed title disappears.
- Classic's stale-state history showed that focus-driven refreshes and broad asynchronous polling are brittle and can cause pane walking or excess CPU.

Implementation scope
- Prove that the activity source chosen by the base feature emits an idle/end transition for an agent on an unfocused tab, including a hidden or suppressed popup.
- Feed that transition through the existing pane-activity facts and pipe snapshot; do not add a second activity owner.
- Preserve tab-id correctness when tabs move.
- Clear state on agent exit and pane close.
- Keep native tab names and rename mode independent of activity state.
- Do not use focus, tab visitation, shelling out to list-panes, process-lifetime heuristics, or broad polling/timers as the fix.

Focused verification
- Deterministic regression: mark an agent active on tab A, focus tab B, end activity on A, and assert the published snapshot becomes idle for A without a focus event for A.
- Cover tab movement, hidden popup, and process-exit/pane-close cleanup where those paths differ.
- Run focused child-repo tests, full project checks, and manually dogfood a multi-tab agent session.

Stop conditions
- If the base feature's selected signal cannot emit an end transition while hidden/unfocused, fix or split that signal source before adding refresh machinery.
- Do not approximate idle by elapsed time or require the user to visually acknowledge the marker.
acceptance_criteria:
- Agent activity ending on an unfocused tab removes its decoration without focusing that tab.
- Hidden/suppressed popup, tab movement, and agent exit or pane close do not leave stale activity.
- The fix uses the base feature's single activity owner and pipe snapshot, with no focus acknowledgement, native-name mutation, shellout polling, or timer heuristic.
- A deterministic regression test proves the unfocused end transition, and focused/full runtime checks pass.
notes:
Nova v1 decision, 2026-08-05: v1 keeps the current tab-activity owner and ships without the Forest and radar redesign. This P2 regression does not block v1.

Keep the bug blocked on Nova v2 activity reconciliation. If child .4 deletes the affected pipeline after radar becomes the sole attention owner, close this bug as superseded. If the current marker survives as the sole owner, resume the bug and prove the unfocused idle transition without polling or focus acknowledgement.

title: Keep the Codex status widget timely instead of increasingly stale
description:
## Problem

During current Edge dogfood, the Codex status widget takes far too long to reflect changed usage and becomes increasingly stale over time. A 10-second status-bar repaint does not guarantee a provider refresh: the current bar can reuse a successful value for 600 seconds and preserve stale facts through a 1800-second error or incomplete-result backoff. The visible value currently gives too little evidence about whether it is fresh, waiting, backed off, or sourced from delayed provider data.

## Existing related work

- yazelix-8u5-4-hnv.1 bounded Codex refresh CPU, workers, retries, and total subprocess time. Those safety guarantees must remain.
- yazelix-5vl-consume-tokenusage-quota-only-8mq plans quota-only collection to avoid parsing unused local history, but intentionally preserves the current 600-second successful freshness policy. It may improve refresh cost without resolving this stale-value contract.
- yazelix-zellij-bar remains the sole owner of provider invocation, cache freshness, backoff, and widget rendering. Main Yazelix should only pin and compose the child.

## Investigation scope

1. Reproduce the delay on the exact installed Edge revision and record the widget value, cache timestamps/status, provider output, repaint cadence, subprocess duration, and observed age over time.
2. Separate four possible delays: repaint scheduling, successful-cache TTL, failure or incomplete-result backoff, and stale or delayed upstream quota data.
3. Verify whether refresh failures or partial results leave the widget looking current while its age grows.
4. Measure cold, warm, and long-lived-session behavior without weakening the one-worker, shared-timeout, singleflight, and stale-value safety contract.
5. Decide the smallest user-visible freshness contract from evidence. Prefer adjusting the existing owner and status model over adding another scheduler, cache, daemon, or main-repo policy.
6. Coordinate with quota-only collection only where it directly removes measured latency; do not merge the two beads unless one implementation genuinely owns both outcomes.

## Expected outcome

The Codex widget reflects provider changes within a bounded, documented interval during healthy operation. When fresh data cannot be obtained, the widget makes stale or backed-off state distinguishable instead of silently presenting an old value as current. Resource usage remains bounded and background refresh never makes the machine busy.

## Verification

Add one focused deterministic regression for the discovered freshness failure, then run the bar formatting, test, release-build, and Nix-package checks. After publishing and pinning the child, run the normal Yazelix flake, package, isolated-profile, and installed-profile checks. Dogfood from a fresh session long enough to cross the relevant freshness and backoff boundaries.
acceptance_criteria:
- A controlled reproduction on the exact installed Edge revision records repaint times, cache age and status, provider duration and output, and the visible widget value long enough to identify where staleness accumulates.
- The investigation distinguishes healthy successful-cache latency, failed or incomplete backoff, subprocess latency, and delayed upstream quota data instead of treating every old value as one bug.
- Before implementation, the maintainer receives concrete options and accepts the healthy maximum-age contract and stale or backed-off presentation.
- The accepted fix remains in yazelix-zellij-bar as the single refresh and cache owner; it adds no daemon, second scheduler, second cache, or main-owned provider policy.
- The one-worker limit, one shared refresh deadline, filesystem singleflight, bounded retry pressure, and preservation of usable last-known facts remain proven.
- One focused regression fails on the observed freshness defect and passes after the fix without duplicating thin timer tests.
- Child formatting, tests, release build, and Nix build pass; the exact child is published and pinned; Yazelix flake, package, isolated-profile, and installed-profile checks pass.
- Fresh-session dogfood crosses the accepted freshness and backoff boundaries and confirms timely healthy updates plus clearly distinguishable stale behavior without a CPU or IO regression.
notes: V1 release gate decision, 2026-08-08: the maintainer requires this Codex widget freshness regression to be fixed and verified before Nova v1.0.0 is released. Beta 5 dogfooding continues while this issue is addressed. Reproduction on the installed Edge path found a partial cache 892 seconds old with 908 seconds of backoff remaining: local-history active-block discovery took 19.36 seconds and exceeded the existing five-second refresh budget before official quota ran. The isolated official-limits path completed in 0.47 seconds with 17 MiB peak RSS. Accepted implementation: yazelix-zellij-bar 0945a08aed9b8d068783318725299fe3c6792fc9 makes default quota display run one official-limits probe per refresh against the already-held empty lock directory with incremental history caching disabled; healthy freshness is 60 seconds, failure backoff is 120 seconds, and retained partial/error values render as codex~. Token and combined modes retain their 600-second freshness and 1800-second backoff because they still read history. The existing filesystem singleflight and five-second whole-refresh deadline remain the owners; no daemon, second cache, direct Codex protocol, fork, or dependency was added. Proof at the child revision: formatting, 56 tests, release build, Nix package build, and a live widget probe passed. Proof after the Yazelix pin: all 101 Linux flake checks, all-system evaluation, default package build, exact LOC scorecard reproduction, and isolated profile installation passed. Edge revision 369d795a91aee1d8fe81ce309e2286a31897d291 was pushed and the yazelix-edge profile was upgraded to it. The installed widget returned fresh quota in 0.53 seconds with 16.8 MiB peak RSS; a forced refresh left the 48.7 MB tokenusage history cache size and mtime unchanged. Fresh-session Edge dogfood confirmed that the v4 widget stayed timely during normal Codex use, and the maintainer accepted the result and authorized closure on 2026-08-08. Failure and backoff presentation remain covered by the deterministic regression and installed-command proof rather than a forced live provider outage.
close_reason: Fixed, published, installed, mechanically verified, and accepted in fresh-session Edge dogfood.

title: Consume COSMIC blur-capable Mars in Yazelix
description:
## Why

`yzx launch` opens the managed Yazelix workspace through the pinned Mars package. On COSMIC Wayland, the current pin accepts a sparse Mars configuration with opacity below 1 and blur enabled but cannot request compositor blur because the terminal lacks `ext-background-effect-v1` support.

The protocol implementation belongs exclusively to Mars bead `yzt-support-cosmic-wayland-blur-pnq`. This Yazelix mirror owns only consuming the accepted Mars revision and proving the packaged end-to-end behavior.

## Scope

- Remain blocked on the Mars implementation and its terminal-level verification.
- Pin the exact accepted Mars revision in the Yazelix flake inputs without copying or wrapping the Wayland protocol implementation.
- Build the normal Yazelix package and a temporary profile from the updated pin.
- Verify that `yzx launch` preserves the existing sparse `mars/config.toml` contract and starts the pinned blur-capable binary.
- Dogfood one fresh COSMIC Wayland window with opacity below 1 and blur enabled, confirming visible compositor blur and normal Yazelix startup, input, graphics, and teardown.
- Update the README LOC scorecard and `CHANGELOG.md` only if project files change, following the main repository rules.
- Upgrade the installed Yazelix profile only after the pin and live acceptance pass.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing Wayland blur in Yazelix, adding a wrapper protocol client, or duplicating Mars tests.
- Adding terminal selection, replacing Mars, changing Zellij, or introducing compositor-specific rules.
- Adding blur intensity controls or broadening the root Yazelix configuration model.
- Editing unrelated Home Manager, layout, plugin, or runtime behavior.

## Ownership Boundary

Mars owns protocol selection, capability handling, surface lifecycle, KWin fallback, and terminal regression tests. Yazelix owns the exact child revision, package composition, launch boundary, and one end-to-end COSMIC acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:

- Mars bead `yzt-support-cosmic-wayland-blur-pnq` is complete with terminal-level COSMIC and KWin-fallback evidence.
- `flake.lock` or the equivalent exact input pin resolves to the accepted Mars commit containing the protocol fix.
- `yzx status --json` and `yzx doctor` identify the expected packaged Mars runtime without changing the sparse native configuration ownership model.
- `nix flake check`, `nix flake show --all-systems`, and `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs` pass.
- A temporary profile installation from the local checkout succeeds.
- In a fresh COSMIC Wayland launch, opacity below 1 with blur enabled produces visible background blur while Yazelix opens normally.
- The live smoke covers keyboard input, link interaction, Yazi Kitty preview, resize/maximize, appearance projection, and clean session teardown without a terminal or Wayland protocol error.
- The installed Yazelix profile is upgraded only after all package and live checks pass.
- No Wayland protocol code, terminal abstraction, or duplicated Mars test is added to the Yazelix repository.
notes:
External blocker: `mars:yzt-support-cosmic-wayland-blur-pnq`. Beads cannot encode a blocking edge across repository databases, so the external reference and `external-blocker` label are the source of truth. Do not claim implementation readiness until the Mars bead is closed and its accepted commit is available to pin.

Observed failure context: COSMIC advertises `ext_background_effect_manager_v1` but not the KDE blur manager. The current packaged Mars pin therefore remains transparent without blur even though the native user config is valid.

title: Use quota-only collection for the Codex bar
description:
## Why

Nova requests `display=quota`, but `yazelix-zellij-bar` currently refreshes active-block tokens, weekly tokens, and official quota unconditionally. Even after the safety fix bounds retries and CPU, the default product would still load local Codex history for facts it never renders. Once tokenusage publishes a true official-limits-only command, the bar should collect only the capabilities requested by its display mode while remaining the sole widget/cache owner.

## Evidence

- `packaging/bar-render-request.nix:25-28` fixes Nova Codex display to `quota` with 5h and weekly periods.
- `../yazelix-zellij-bar/src/lib.rs:929-938` already carries `AgentUsageDisplay` in `CodexUsageWidgetOptions`.
- `../yazelix-zellij-bar/src/lib.rs:963-994` passes display only to rendering; cache refresh receives no requested capability.
- `../yazelix-zellij-bar/src/lib.rs:2564-2634` unconditionally runs active-block and weekly history probes, then optionally runs official quota.
- `../yazelix-zellij-bar/src/lib.rs:2333-2347` defines cache completeness as both token windows plus quota, regardless of display.
- `../yazelix-zellij-bar/src/lib.rs:2929-2960` contains separate token-history and official-limit command builders.

## User-Visible Contract

With Nova default `display=quota`, a successful refresh launches exactly one tokenusage official-limits-only command and never discovers or parses local session history. `display=token` collects only active and weekly token facts. `display=both` collects both capabilities. The single cache record identifies which requested capabilities its latest successful collection can satisfy, so refreshing quota never makes retained old token facts appear newly fresh and a quota failure does not cause local token-history rescans. Existing labels, percentages, reset countdowns, stale/unknown behavior, cache singleflight, and 600-second successful freshness remain intact.

## Scope

In scope:
- Wait for the released tokenusage quota-only contract tracked by `yazelix-5vl-tokenusage-quota-only-limits-pob`.
- Make Codex cache refresh in `yazelix-zellij-bar` capability-aware using the existing display and requested periods.
- Invoke only the tokenusage commands required by `quota`, `token`, or `both`.
- Keep one cache record and one freshness/backoff policy. Record the requested or successfully collected capability set, or an equivalent minimal discriminator, so retained facts that were not collected by the latest success cannot satisfy freshness. Prefer a cache schema bump over compatibility branches.
- Preserve one filesystem singleflight owner and stale-value rendering.
- Add one table-driven provider-command test covering quota, token, both, success, and partial failure without multiplying thin tests.
- Publish the child revision, bump the packaged tokenusage release, pin both exact revisions in Yazelix, and update `CHANGELOG.md` plus the README LOC scorecard.

Out of scope:
- No direct OAuth or Codex app-server client in Yazelix or the bar.
- No tokenusage source patch, fork, wrapper, daemon, watcher, new root config option, layout redesign, or provider framework.
- Do not broaden this slice to Claude or OpenCode.
- Do not preserve old derived cache schemas through migrations; they may be ignored and rebuilt safely.

## Implementation Notes

1. Write a command-recording provider fixture that proves exact process selection for each display mode.
2. Pass requested capability into freshness, refresh, and completeness decisions rather than only rendering.
3. Prefer one whole-request cache record with a small requested or collected capability discriminator and the existing global freshness and backoff. Do not add per-capability timestamps, per-capability backoffs, separate files, or display-specific caches unless a focused failing contract proves the single-record model insufficient.
4. In quota mode, call only the released no-history tokenusage surface.
5. In token mode, retain the one-worker and total-budget safety contract from `yazelix-8u5-4-hnv.1`.
6. Add no Rust crates. Reuse existing serde, process, cache, and test helpers.

## Verification

- `cd ../yazelix-zellij-bar && cargo fmt --all -- --check` should exit 0.
- `cd ../yazelix-zellij-bar && cargo test` should exit 0 and the mode matrix should prove quota executes one official-only command and zero history commands.
- With a sentinel tokenusage parse cache, invoking the packaged Nova quota widget should leave the cache byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `cd ../yazelix-zellij-bar && cargo build --release` and `nix build .#yazelix_zellij_bar --no-link` should exit 0.
- `nix flake check`, `nix flake show --all-systems`, `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs`, and a temporary profile install should succeed after both pins.
- Fresh-session dogfood should preserve the displayed Codex percentages/countdowns while `ps` and IO observation show no local `tu blocks --offline` or `tu weekly` process from quota rendering.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the released tokenusage command touches session history or its incremental parse cache.
- Stop if capability-aware caching starts creating multiple cache owners, per-capability timers or backoffs, display-specific files, or migration machinery; simplify to one request-keyed cache record instead.
- Stop if the safety bead is incomplete or its backoff/worker contract would be weakened.
- Stop if implementation requires adding provider logic to main Yazelix.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort M, risk MED, confidence HIGH after the upstream command exists. This is a performance/ownership follow-up rather than a Beta 4 blocker. Rejected: collecting all facts for cache completeness, per-capability cache state without a proven need, direct Codex protocol duplication, and separate long-running refresh infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria:
- Quota display launches exactly one released no-history official-limits command; token display launches only active and weekly history commands; both launches the union.
- One cache file and one global freshness and backoff policy remain. A small collected-capability discriminator prevents a quota success from making retained token facts fresh, and vice versa.
- Switching display modes either reuses a cache proven to satisfy the requested capability set or performs one bounded refresh; it never creates display-specific files or per-capability timers.
- The P1 one-worker, whole-refresh timeout, singleflight, stale-value, and incomplete-result backoff contracts remain intact.
- One table-driven fake-provider test proves exact command counts for quota, token, and both plus a mode-change and partial-failure boundary.
- A sentinel tokenusage cache remains byte-for-byte unchanged in packaged quota mode; child and main checks pass, exact releases are pinned, and fresh dogfood preserves the visible quota labels and countdowns.

title: Make packaged configuration discoverable through Overview and All
description:
## Why

Ratconfig joins locally owned finite schemas, child-published catalogs, curated native-tool fields, default documents, sparse user documents, and native-file actions. Those sources do not support one universal writable schema, and asking Yazelix to reproduce every type, default, and constraint would make it a duplicate semantic owner.

Users need one predictable overview, complete discovery where an owner can publish it, honest native escape hatches where it cannot, preserved sparse intent, and inline editing only when the source integration can validate and persist safely.

## Outcome

Every packaged configuration surface is discoverable through the strongest contract its real owner publishes.

- Overview contains optional owner/product recommendations plus every non-inherited field that needs attention: explicit, invalid, or externally managed.
- All contains the complete inventory for finite or machine-readable owner catalogs and every deliberately exposed field for curated partial-schema integrations.
- Search spans All.
- Each modeled setting distinguishes the inherited baseline, explicit or invalid intent, effective value, and origin where the host can resolve them.
- An explicit value equal to the baseline remains explicit; reset removes intent and recomputes the value.
- Generic rows and exact file actions expose dynamic or opaque native state; diagnostics explain invalid, ignored, or unsafe conditions that require attention.
- Safe owner-backed values may be edited inline; complex or unsupported values remain read-only and open their native source.
- Native configuration files remain canonical.

## Definitions

- Baseline: the value and origin that would be effective if the selected override were absent. It may combine tool fallback and lower-priority Yazelix packaged layers.
- Intent: the sparse assertion present in the user or externally managed layer, including an explicit value equal to the baseline.
- Effective: the resolved value the runtime uses, when determinable.
- Default document: evidence for packaged values, observed paths, grouping, ordering, and syntactic shapes; never proof of a complete schema or safe edit contract.
- Capability: a host-declared interaction backed by owner validation and safe persistence. Type or renderability alone does not grant it.

## Ownership rules

1. Consume a versioned machine-readable catalog when the actual configuration owner publishes one.
2. Keep finite Yazelix-owned schemas in Yazelix.
3. For native formats without a stable catalog, expose the smallest truthful curated subset plus generic document and file surfaces; do not manufacture completeness with a local mirror.
4. Ratconfig owns generic sparse-intent presentation, Overview/All, search, rendering, diagnostics, and declared-capability interaction—not child-tool semantics.
5. Yazelix owns source discovery, layer resolution, the local root schema, cross-tool integration/apply policy, optional recommendations, and host persistence routing—not copied child paths, types, defaults, constraints, or validators.
6. Inline editing is a declared capability of a source integration, never an inference from a literal default, type label, or renderability.
7. Reset removes the selected sparse override. Silent fallback or baseline materialization is not an acceptable substitute.
8. Preserve explicit and invalid user input truthfully, including explicit values equal to the current baseline.

## Scope

- Consume ratconfig-h7d through mirror child .13 and replace Core/current/default ambiguity with Overview plus sparse intent, baseline, effective value, origin, and editing capability.
- Review root/popups, Mars, Cursors, Zellij, Starship, Helix, Yazi, and Nushell using the correct owner class.
- Prove parity only for owner-published finite catalogs.
- Use default documents for observed baseline discovery without claiming supported-but-absent settings or semantic metadata they do not contain.
- For partial or dynamic surfaces, provide honest file actions and document rows where they add user value. Preserve safe opaque state without manufacturing rows or informational diagnostics; reserve diagnostics for invalid, ignored, or unsafe conditions. A wholly invalid native document remains a source-level diagnostic and exact file action unless the owner can localize the error safely.
- Keep complex or unsafe values read-only when the source cannot edit them safely.
- Preserve sparse native files, invalid input where safe, Home Manager ownership, validation, and existing runtime apply behavior.
- Update focused checks, current-state docs, CHANGELOG, and the LOC scorecard as user-visible slices land.

## Out of scope

- No copied child schema, scraped documentation inventory, universal configuration language, private config database, generic watcher, compatibility layer, config generator, or automatic migration.
- No requirement that every native format become a field editor.
- No arbitrary first-ten or alphabetical recommendation algorithm.
- No pure-text inline semantics that move parsing and serialization into every host.
- No yzx config CLI commands in this program; the user postponed that separate automation surface.

## Verification

Each child names its inventory, baseline, intent, validation, persistence, and effective-value sources and proves representative Overview, All, search, explicit-same-as-baseline, externally managed visibility, reset/unset with inherited-value provenance, localized versus document-level invalid visibility, edit capability, native-file fallback, and ownership behavior appropriate to that source.

The final gate proves the joined product contract without asserting fake field-count parity for partial or dynamic surfaces. Full flake, package, and temporary-profile checks pass before completion.

## Stop conditions

Stop if a completeness claim lacks a versioned owner. Stop if implementation copies a child schema into Yazelix without a separately chosen ownership transfer. Stop if Overview hides any non-inherited intent, including externally managed state. Stop if All claims completeness for opaque state. Stop if inferred syntax or type alone authorizes editing. Stop if reset writes a baseline value. Stop if tool fallback, packaged baseline, intent, and effective state are collapsed into ambiguous current/default fields.

## Rejected and deferred alternatives

Rejected: one umbrella schema in Yazelix, forcing every native format into field rows, a permanently read-only Ratconfig, pure-text inline editing, and a blind first-ten overview. Direct native editing remains the universal fallback rather than the whole product. CLI get/set/unset/edit/validate commands are deferred until after the TUI architecture is implemented and dogfooded.
notes:
Architecture decision refined by the sparse-intent model used by mature settings and declarative systems: absence means inherit; explicit presence means the user relies on that value, even when it currently equals the baseline. The closed root/popups slice remains valid and its existing selection becomes recommendations. Mars remains the decisive owner-catalog vertical slice. If Mars still requires per-field Yazelix schema logic, stop before propagating the architecture.

Further research supports treating Ratconfig as a workbench and Yazelix as the orchestrator. Prefer an owner-published catalog, parser, or constrained command/API as the conduit; guarded native patching is the fallback, not a new universal lens system. Keep provenance bounded: show the origin needed to explain effective state and what reset will inherit, but do not build full override history. An accepted value is not necessarily operationally correct, so apply and runtime status must remain truthful.

Zellij refinement chosen 2026-07-27: an exact native-file action plus tested preservation is the honest fallback for safe opaque KDL. Do not manufacture one field or informational diagnostic per preserved leaf. Ratconfig needs no contextual diagnostic-routing feature for that surface.
close_reason: Completed all Overview/All configuration discovery children and the final joined contract gate.

title: Consume Ratconfig Core and All settings release
description:
## Why

Yazelix must consume the generic Core/All contract from Ratconfig before per-config inventories can use one consistent view, count, toggle, and search behavior. Ratconfig v5.0.0 is published at 79999f6722d114cebae4944f104daa7683459400, so Yazelix can consume the released contract directly.

## Evidence

## User-Visible Contract

## Stop Conditions

## Maintenance Notes

Published child release: Ratconfig v5.0.0 at 79999f6722d114cebae4944f104daa7683459400. Update the existing Ratconfig pin only; add no crate, adapter, shim, or dual-version path.

Ratconfig v5 API audit handoff 2026-07-15: v5 adds required public fields ConfigUiModel::core_fields and ConfigUiApp::settings_view. Yazelix has one direct ConfigUiModel literal at crates/yzx-config/src/model.rs:103 and no direct ConfigUiApp literal, so adoption must populate core_fields and can continue using ConfigUiApp::new. Yazelix is the only consumer; add no legacy adapter, compatibility shim, or dual-version path. Consume the v5 API directly after the exact tag is published.
