title: Prove honest Overview and All configuration coverage
description:
## Why

Per-surface work can still leave inconsistent terminology, search behavior, ownership guidance, or false completeness claims. One final gate should prove the joined Ratconfig experience while respecting that finite catalogs, curated integrations, and dynamic native documents have different owners and verification boundaries.

## User-visible contract

Every packaged configuration surface is reachable and searchable through the strongest honest discovery surface it supports. Overview contains reviewed product settings plus every non-inherited value that needs attention: explicit, invalid, or externally managed. All is field-complete where a versioned owner catalog exists and contains every Yazelix-curated field where it does not. Native file actions and generic document rows cover remaining valid opaque state; read-only ownership messages and diagnostics are reserved for conditions requiring attention without pretending Yazelix owns the native schema. No UI or documentation uses guided as the category term.

## Scope

In scope:
- Consolidate a focused packaged contract over every inventory/discovery source.
- Verify owner-catalog parity only for finite machine-readable catalogs.
- Verify normal-mode Overview/All toggle, All-scope search, explicit, invalid, and externally managed non-recommended visibility, sections, file actions, and Home Manager ownership.
- Verify representative simple edits, complex read-only rows, opaque preserved state, reset previews plus unset behavior, sparse writes, owner validation, and truthful runtime/apply status.
- Verify each partial or dynamic surface documents its native escape hatch and does not claim exhaustive field coverage.
- Reconcile architecture and configuration docs with actual owners.
- Update CHANGELOG and README LOC scorecard, run full checks, and refresh the installed profile after acceptance.

Out of scope:
- No new setting, default, runtime feature, umbrella schema, adapter, or config owner.
- No literal expected list duplicating an owner catalog.
- No GUI launch unless separately requested.

## Implementation notes

Prefer owner-to-visible parity for published catalogs and representative behavior for curated/dynamic surfaces. The gate should fail if an owner-published field cannot render, a curated field lacks classification, a native surface lacks a truthful escape hatch, or docs overstate completeness. Do not compare Zellij, Helix, Nushell, or another dynamic surface to a fabricated host inventory.

## Verification

Run yzx-config tests, nix flake check, nix flake show --all-systems, the Yazelix and runtime builds, a clean temporary profile install, and git diff --check. Refresh the user profile only after acceptance.

## Stop conditions

Stop while any config-surface child remains incomplete. Stop if a completeness claim lacks owner evidence. Stop if checks become source-literal mirrors instead of behavior or owner parity contracts. Stop if unrelated dirty work cannot be preserved.

## Rejected alternatives

Rejected: a universal field-count assertion, a second umbrella schema, and treating a native-file action as insufficient merely because the native owner has no stable catalog API.


## Architecture constraint

Overview is a generic attention surface, not a second schema: it combines optional recommended identities with every non-inherited field. The configuration owner remains authoritative for paths, types, defaults, constraints, and writable semantics. Inline editing is allowed only when this integration has owner-backed validation and safe persistence; otherwise keep the value read-only and expose its exact native-file action. This child depends on the Ratconfig Overview integration in .13 unless it is already a completed focused slice.
close_reason: Completed the joined packaged discovery gate: all reduced tabs expose every modeled field in All, representative All-only fields and every native file action are searchable, sparse explicit-same-as-baseline and reset provenance remain distinct, architecture claims match owner completeness, and all Rust/Nix/package/profile checks pass.

title: Verify live apply timing for Mars settings
description:
## Why

Ratconfig currently tells users that every exposed Mars setting except mars.appearance.preset applies on the next launch. Maintainer dogfooding suggests more of these settings update the existing Mars window live. Incorrect apply timing makes users restart unnecessarily and weakens trust in the Takes effect column.

## Evidence

- crates/yzx-config/src/model.rs:55-64 assigns every MARS_FIELDS row through mars_apply_status.
- crates/yzx-config/src/model.rs:420-430 returns live only for mars.appearance.preset and next launch for every other Mars path.
- crates/yzx-config/src/catalog.rs:349-363 exposes window width, height, opacity, font size, line height, scrollbar, and audio/visual bell settings.
- ../mars/frontends/rioterm/src/watcher.rs:8-57 watches the config directory and emits a debounced reload event.
- ../mars/frontends/rioterm/src/application.rs:383-438 reloads config, updates every open route, and reconfigures each window.
- ../mars/frontends/rioterm/src/screen/mod.rs:467-555 reapplies font size, line height, renderer state, dimensions, and window opacity behavior.
- ../mars/frontends/rioterm/src/renderer/mod.rs:145-160 rebuilds scrollbar state from the reloaded enable-scroll-bar value.
- ../mars/frontends/rioterm/src/application.rs:571-580 reads audio and visual bell flags from the current in-memory config when BEL arrives.
- ../mars/frontends/rioterm/src/router/window.rs:145-163 applies width and height in the new-window builder, with no corresponding resize in configure_window, so those two may remain launch-scoped.
- ARCHITECTURE.md:395-396 and docs/configuration.md:233-234 currently claim every non-palette Mars field is next-launch only.

## User-Visible Contract

Each Mars setting displays the narrowest truthful apply timing for the exact packaged Mars revision. Settings proven to update an already-open Mars window say live. Settings consumed only when a window is created retain next launch or an equally precise new-window label. The UI and documentation do not generalize one result across unrelated fields.

## Scope

In scope:
- On the exact Mars revision pinned by flake.lock, change each exposed setting through yzx config and observe the already-open Mars window.
- Verify mars.appearance.preset, window.width, window.height, window.opacity, fonts.size, line-height, enable-scroll-bar, bell.audio, and bell.visual independently.
- Exercise the behavior needed to observe each setting: window geometry, opacity, font metrics, line spacing, scroll activity, and an explicit BEL for both bell modes.
- Distinguish watcher pickup, current-window application, and newly launched-window application.
- Replace mars_apply_status with the smallest evidence-backed per-path classification and add one focused mapping/behavior contract.
- Reconcile ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/configuration.md, CHANGELOG.md, and the README LOC scorecard if user-visible labels change.

Out of scope:
- No Ratconfig API or renderer change; Yazelix owns apply policy and product text.
- No Mars runtime behavior change in this bead.
- No claim about settings outside the exact packaged Mars inventory or untested operating systems/compositors.
- No weak test that only mirrors a newly introduced literal table without defending the user-visible grouping.

## Implementation Notes

1. Record a small evidence matrix for every field: watcher reload observed, current window changed, new window changed, and platform/session details.
2. Treat width and height as separate from visual/render settings; source inspection suggests they are startup-only.
3. If behavior differs by platform or compositor, use precise guidance instead of labeling the field universally live.
4. If a setting should apply live but the pinned Mars implementation does not, keep Yazelix truthful and create a Mars-owned follow-up rather than hiding a runtime change here.

## Verification

- Manual dogfooding against the flake-pinned Mars revision records one result for all nine exposed settings; GUI launch requires maintainer approval when this bead is implemented.
- cargo test --manifest-path crates/yzx-config/Cargo.toml exits 0 with a focused apply-status contract.
- nix flake check exits 0.
- nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs exits 0.
- git diff --check exits 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the tested Mars binary does not match flake.lock.
- Stop if a live result cannot be distinguished from a newly created window or config-UI-only palette update.
- Stop if truthful classification requires modifying Mars; create a separate Mars bead and preserve the observed Yazelix label.
- Stop if unrelated dirty flake.lock work cannot be preserved.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort S, risk LOW, confidence HIGH that the current blanket label is too broad; confidence is MEDIUM about the exact per-field result until manual dogfooding. Add no crates. This verification should block the Mars Core/All inventory bead because that bead retains Yazelix-owned apply policy.
notes:
Implementation staged against Mars revision 5a652a77aa8fe2ccc1edd9e5686d51f824053f06. Source evidence: the config watcher reloads the complete Config, update_config reapplies opacity, font size, line height, renderer/scrollbar state, and current bell flags to open routes; window width and height are read only by the new-window builder. Classification: live = mars.appearance.preset, window.opacity, fonts.size, line-height, enable-scroll-bar, bell.audio, bell.visual; new windows = window.width, window.height. Verification passed: rustfmt, the flake-pinned yzx package build with 40 yzx-config tests, nix flake check, nix flake show --all-systems, nix build .#yazelix, temporary-profile install, git diff --check, and installed profile upgrade. Direct local cargo test is temporarily incompatible with the unpublished sibling Ratconfig Core/All work; the pinned flake test lane passes. Manual COSMIC/Wayland dogfooding remains before closure.

Fresh-eyes and isomorphic simplification pass: renamed the focused test so it no longer overclaims direct binary verification, replaced two filtered summary lists with one ordered nine-field contract, and reduced Rust by 3 lines while strengthening completeness. Rejected a generic apply-status helper or timing enum because each adds a concept for negligible LOC savings and the current match remains the single clear owner. Post-pass rustfmt, full flake check, all-system flake show, package build, temporary-profile install, diff check, scorecard, and installed runtime refresh pass.

Second fresh-eyes/simplification pass: replaced eight repeated ConfigUiApplyStatus constructions and the one-caller next-launch wrapper in model.rs with one local apply_status constructor; every rendered summary, label, detail, and pending=false value is unchanged. Simplified the Mars timing test to validate the exact field set and summaries without accidentally freezing catalog row order or allocating a vector. Tightened CHANGELOG wording from the overbroad font metrics to font size and line height. Net reduction versus the previous reviewed shape: 25 Rust lines and one specialized helper concept. Rejected moving the helper across modules for the lone Yazi constructor, direct match-arm construction, and collapsing bell/render details because each increases coupling/repetition or loses useful precision. Full post-pass verification and installed runtime refresh passed; manual dogfood remains.

Third fresh-eyes/simplification pass: removed “immediately” from the live Mars detail text because the config watcher deliberately debounces reloads; “live in open windows” is the precise contract without a zero-latency claim. Revalidated the local apply_status helper against Ratconfig: all eight model call sites represent persisted, non-pending state, so the helper removes a repeated invariant rather than hiding meaningful variation. Rejected moving timing metadata into the generic field catalog, sharing the helper across modules for one Yazi call site, and merging the focused completeness test into a broader model test; each would add coupling or weaken the regression boundary without removing a concept. Full flake check, all-system show, package build, temporary-profile install/status, diff/format checks, scorecard, and installed runtime refresh pass. Manual Mars dogfood remains before closure.
close_reason: Completed: source-backed per-setting apply labels shipped, all automated gates passed, and maintainer dogfooding confirmed the live Mars behavior.

title: Expose packaged Zellij themes in Ratconfig
description:
## Why

Nova's Zellij tab cannot select a theme even though the pinned Yazelix Zellij 0.44.3 package already embeds 41 named themes. A focused picker would make a high-value native preference discoverable without copying theme files or introducing another theme owner.

## Evidence

- `crates/yzx-config/src/catalog.rs:382`: the guarded sidecar forbids integration-owned nodes, but `theme` is not forbidden.
- `crates/yzx-config/src/catalog.rs:395`: the eight editable Zellij fields do not include `theme`.
- `crates/yzx-config/src/model.rs:84`: every exposed Zellij field expects an effective packaged default.
- `defaults/zellij/config.kdl:1`: the packaged config does not currently select an explicit theme.

## Scope

2. Treat the pinned fork's embedded asset names as the availability source of truth. Keep only chooser metadata in Nova and make drift fail in the flake check.
3. Include `default` explicitly in addition to asset-derived names.
4. Add one focused contract test covering parse, choice validation, sparse save, reset, and preservation of neighboring assignments.
5. Confirm active-session behavior manually. Label it live only if the pinned watcher visibly applies it; otherwise label it next-session without adding reload machinery.
6. Preserve the runtime's existing acceptance boundary for hand-edited sidecars. If Ratconfig's exhaustive choice model would newly invalidate a previously working custom theme name, stop and record the smallest host/child capability needed instead of silently narrowing the runtime contract.

## Verification

- `nix profile add --refresh /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix --profile <tmp>` should install the changed package.
- Manual dogfood: use `yzx config` to select two visually distinct packaged themes, verify the documented current/next-session behavior, reset, and confirm the default returns.
- After runtime changes, `nix profile upgrade --refresh yazelix` should update the installed runtime.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the pinned package does not actually load all cited embedded assets.
- Stop if implementation starts copying theme contents or creating a second theme owner.
- Stop if exposing choices requires weakening Zellij integration-node guards.
- Stop if the first slice expands into cross-application theme synchronization or custom theme management.

## Maintenance Notes

The package-vs-in-house decision is settled: reuse Zellij's embedded assets and existing Rust/std sidecar owner; add no crate or package. This is a focused slice under the Overview/All config program. The broader Zellij inventory should count this completed field in its coverage rather than reimplement it. Rejected for this slice: copied theme files, a Nova theme registry, previews, and adaptive dark/light pairs. Effort S/M, risk LOW/MED, confidence HIGH.

## Architecture constraint

Overview is a generic attention surface, not a second schema: it combines optional recommended identities with every explicit or invalid field. The configuration owner remains authoritative for paths, types, defaults, constraints, and writable semantics. Inline editing is allowed only when this integration has owner-backed validation and safe persistence; otherwise keep the value read-only and expose its exact native-file action. title: Consume Ratconfig sparse-intent Overview contract
description:
## Purpose

Mirror Ratconfig bead ratconfig-h7d and make its released sparse-intent, capability-aware Overview/All contract the single generic configuration-discovery model consumed by Yazelix.

## User-visible contract

yzx config opens each settings tab on Overview when that tab has recommended fields or non-inherited fields distinct from its broader inventory. Non-inherited means explicit, invalid, or externally managed. a toggles Overview and All, and search spans All.

For every modeled setting Yazelix presents the strongest truthful state it can resolve:

- baseline: the effective value and origin with the selected user or managed override removed;
- intent: absent, explicitly present, invalid, or externally managed;
- effective: the value the runtime will use, when determinable;
- origin/owner: the layer responsible for the value;
- capability: the safe interaction available for that source.

An explicit value equal to the baseline remains explicit and visible. When known, the reset/inherit action previews the value and origin that will become effective. Reset removes the sparse override and recomputes the effective value; it never writes the current baseline into the user file. Localized invalid values remain visible with diagnostics instead of silently falling back. A wholly invalid document remains a source-level diagnostic with the exact native-file action unless the owner can localize it safely.

Safe owner-backed values retain inline controls. Complex, opaque, unsupported, or read-only values remain inspectable and open the exact native source where one exists. The completed root/popups recommendation selection remains user-visible after the terminology and state-model change.

## Sources of truth

- Root: defaults/config.toml and the local root validator define Yazelix's finite schema and lower-priority packaged baseline; the sparse user file records intent.
- Mars and other catalog owners: the exact pinned catalog or parser defines supported paths, semantic types, defaults, constraints, and writable shapes.
- Native default documents: provide packaged baseline values and observed paths/shapes only; they do not prove completeness or writability.
- User and Home Manager documents: preserve explicit intent and ownership, including explicit values equal to the baseline.
- Runtime materializers and apply paths: determine effective values and apply timing.

## Ownership

- Ratconfig owns generic intent/baseline/effective presentation, Overview/All filtering, counts, search, rendering, and declared-capability interaction.
- Yazelix owns source discovery, layer resolution, its local root schema, cross-tool integration/apply policy, optional recommendations, host validation/persistence routing, and truthful origin labels.
- Child tools own their paths, semantic types, defaults, constraints, and writable behavior.
- Native files remain canonical; Yazelix must not mirror child catalogs or create a second config store.

## Scope

- Wait for ratconfig-h7d to publish one exact revision and update the pinned dependency.
- Migrate ConfigUiModel integration from Core/current/default semantics to Overview plus sparse intent, baseline, effective value, and origin/ownership.
- Rename local recommendation constants and tests where they imply child semantic ownership.
- Map editing from explicit host capabilities, not type labels. Preserve current toggles, choices, ordered lists, free text, and reset only where the owning parser and persistence path make them safe.
- Treat inferred default-document syntax as display evidence only. Do not infer completeness, ranges, enum choices, units, apply timing, or writability from a literal default.
- Preserve All-scope search, a toggling, exact file actions, generic document rows, diagnostics, Home Manager read-only ownership, sparse writes, validation, theme behavior, and apply timing.
- Preserve invalid and unknown native input when the existing source contract can do so safely; never normalize it silently to a baseline. Do not add tolerant or error-recovering parsers solely to manufacture field rows from an unparseable document.
- Update current-state docs, CHANGELOG, and README LOC scorecard.

## Verification

Use focused behavioral contracts:

- One inherited root field follows the packaged baseline.
- One explicit root field equal to its baseline remains explicit and visible in Overview.
- Changing a test baseline affects the inherited field but not the explicitly pinned field.
- Reset previews the inherited value and origin, deletes the sparse path, and reloads inherited state without materializing the baseline.
- One localized invalid explicit value remains visible with a diagnostic and is not silently replaced; one wholly invalid document produces a source-level diagnostic and exact file action without fabricated field recovery.
- One non-recommended Home Manager-managed value remains visible in Overview, reports external ownership, and remains read-only.
- One safe owner-backed scalar uses its declared control; one boolean-looking or structured value without write capability remains read-only and opens its native file.
- Search from Overview reaches an All-only field.
- Existing root/popups behavior remains equivalent apart from corrected wording and provenance.
- cargo test --manifest-path crates/yzx-config/Cargo.toml, nix flake check, nix flake show --all-systems, nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs, and a clean temporary profile install exit 0.
- Refresh the installed user profile only after acceptance.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if consumption requires a Core or old-state compatibility adapter.
- Stop if Yazelix derives recommendations from alphabetical or arbitrary first-N order. Stop if integration requires a second error-recovering parser to infer fields from wholly invalid native text.
- Stop if a child field becomes editable from inferred syntax or a type label without owner-backed validation and safe persistence.
- Stop if reset writes a baseline value rather than removing intent.
- Stop if the implementation collapses tool default, Yazelix packaged baseline, explicit user intent, and effective runtime value into one ambiguous default/current pair.
- Stop if the integration creates a CLI, config database, watcher, universal schema, or migration not required by ratconfig-h7d.

## Deferred alternative

The user explicitly chose to postpone yzx config CLI commands. Do not add get/set/unset/edit/validate commands in this bead. Reconsider that automation surface only as a later independently approved slice after the TUI architecture is dogfooded.
design:
## Negligible Overview decision

This consumer adopts Ratconfig bead `ratconfig-h7d.9` rather than reproducing its policy.

- Yazelix continues to supply semantic, stable `recommended_fields` identities. It must not inspect terminal height, backfill arbitrary catalog rows, or change recommendations merely to occupy space.
- Ratconfig decides whether the resulting per-tab Overview/All distinction is meaningful. A distinction exists only when the effective Overview hides at least three fields and at least 25% of the tab inventory; otherwise the tab behaves as All.
- The earlier requirement that root/popups recommendations “remain user-visible” preserves recommendation identity and attention behavior, not a forced Overview mode when the generic threshold collapses it.
- After consuming the published Ratconfig revision, verify the reported 8/9 main-tab case shows all nine fields, a plain settings title, and no active/advertised `a` toggle.
- Also verify a threshold-positive Yazelix tab retains Overview/All, search still spans All, and explicit/invalid/externally managed/field-diagnosed rows remain visible.
- Do not create a downstream compatibility shim or a second threshold constant. Ratconfig is the single policy owner.

Cross-repo ordering is tracked by Ratconfig publication bead `ratconfig-h7d.7`, which depends on `ratconfig-h7d.9`. This existing consumer bead is the Yazelix implementation owner; no duplicate Yazelix bead is needed.
notes:
The first integration should prove behavior rather than invent a large provenance framework. "Baseline" means the resolved lower-priority value after removing the selected override; owner defaults may remain optional metadata if they differ. Preserve explicit-same-as-baseline because it pins intent across future packaged-default changes. Use the current native parsers and sparse patchers as write authorities.

Research refinement: Ratconfig is the workbench; Yazelix is the orchestrator and layer resolver. Overview visibility is recommended OR intent is not inherited. Provenance is intentionally minimal but must include the origin of the effective value and, when different, the baseline that reset will inherit. Prefer owner conduits and parsers; retain guarded native patchers only for bounded operations.

Release ordering correction: migrate and run focused consumer checks against the exact committed local Ratconfig 6.0 release candidate first. Only after that preflight passes, publish/tag Ratconfig, replace the temporary path dependency with the exact pushed revision/Nix pin, and verify again without local overrides.

Completed against Ratconfig v6.0.0 at ecce98710c254accede67760b41ecf3dbcd9626d. Strict Cargo formatting/Clippy and 49 focused tests pass; nix flake show, the full package build, all 68 flake checks, and a clean temporary profile install pass. Isolated runtime dogfooding covered negligible and meaningful Overview behavior, All toggling, inline validation, sparse edit/reset, localized invalid intent and diagnostics, the external field editor, and exact native-file fallback. The cursor flake pin was refreshed to e8edd45 so the Nix graph no longer retains Ratconfig 2.
close_reason: Consumed the published Ratconfig 6 sparse-intent contract and passed Cargo, Nix, installation, and isolated runtime verification.

title: Review root and popup settings for Core
description:
## Why

The Yazelix root and popup schema is finite and owned locally, but Core/All adoption still needs an explicit completeness and classification pass. Dynamic custom popup ids are valid configured values even though their names cannot be known before users create them.

## Evidence

- defaults/config.toml owns packaged semantic defaults.
- crates/yzx-config/src/catalog.rs:212 defines CONFIG_FIELDS and splits them between Main and Popups.
- crates/yzx-config/src/root_config.rs:204 rejects unsupported root paths and delegates only popups.<id> to dynamic validation.
- crates/yzx-config/src/custom_popups.rs owns dynamic popup rendering and validation.
- ARCHITECTURE.md Root schema inventory documents the current finite fields and dynamic popup namespace.

## User-Visible Contract

All contains every supported finite root setting plus every configured custom popup field. Core contains the product-essential subset selected by this review and always includes explicit or invalid non-core values. Search finds any finite or configured dynamic path. Unknown root paths remain rejected rather than appearing as editable settings.

## Scope

In scope:
- Reconcile defaults/config.toml, CONFIG_FIELDS, root validation, architecture inventory, and Ratconfig rows into one complete checked inventory.
- Review every finite root field and each custom-popup field kind for Core membership using frequency, product impact, safety, and clarity.
- Mark non-core fields without removing them from All.
- Render configured dynamic popup entries discoverably, including complex values as read-only when needed.
- Preserve sparse persistence, validation, managed keybinding collision rules, and apply statuses.
- Record graduation decisions and rejected Core candidates in the close reason or Beads notes.

Out of scope:
- No new root setting, popup feature, command, or compatibility alias.
- No weakening of unknown-path rejection.
- No automatic creation of custom popup ids.

## Verification

- cargo test --manifest-path crates/yzx-config/Cargo.toml exits 0 and proves schema/catalog parity.
- Focused tests prove representative Core and non-core root fields, all-scope search, and configured custom popup discovery.
- nix flake check exits 0 after integration.
- The README LOC scorecard is refreshed for project-file changes.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the documented root inventory and validator disagree; resolve the one owner before classification.
- Stop if dynamic popup rendering would invent entries that are not configured.
- Stop if Core classification changes defaults or runtime behavior.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: use the existing local schema and Ratconfig metadata only. The review term is Core, never guided. Effort M, risk LOW/MED, confidence HIGH.
notes: Review outcome: ROOT_CONFIG_CORE_PATHS contains shell.program, editor.command, agent.command, welcome.enabled, welcome.style, all six managed action keybindings, and bar.widgets. All-only defaults are open.log_level, agent.args, welcome.duration_seconds, popup.side_margin, and popup.vertical_margin; explicit or invalid values still surface in Core through Ratconfig. Non-root inventories remain Core until their own review beads. Configured popups use Ratconfig's generic TOML document rows for the leaves actually present under popups.<id>; every discovered leaf is explicit and therefore remains visible in Core, while All still contains it. Absent optional leaves and unconfigured ids are not synthesized. Rejected: a Yazelix-side five-field UI schema and derived defaults per popup id, because it duplicated the existing validator and underused Ratconfig's generic passthrough.
close_reason: Completed: reviewed the finite root inventory, applied the 12-path Core classification, kept five advanced defaults All-only, and exposed configured custom-popup leaves through Ratconfig's generic TOML rows without synthesizing ids or duplicating the popup schema. Unknown paths, semantic validation, sparse writes, and non-root Core behavior remain intact. Verified with 48 yzx-config tests, nix flake check, all-system flake evaluation, full Yazelix build, temporary profile install, and installed runtime upgrade.

title: Expose all Mars settings and review Overview recommendations
description:
## Why

Mars supports a broad typed configuration surface, but Yazelix still exposes only eight locally mirrored Mars fields. The exact packaged Mars revision must own completeness; Yazelix owns only product prominence and bounded persistence policy.

## User-visible contract

All exposes every public entry in the pinned Mars catalog except mars.appearance.preset, which is deliberately filtered so root appearance.mode remains the sole Ratconfig appearance control. That yields 150 Mars rows: 15 Overview recommendations and 135 All-only rows. Owner-excluded internal or derived state does not appear.

Overview combines the 15 recommendations with every explicit, invalid, or externally managed non-recommended field. Search spans All. No Mars-specific schema or renderer belongs in Ratconfig.

## Overview recommendations

- window.width
- window.height
- window.mode
- window.decorations
- window.opacity
- window.opacity-cells
- window.blur
- fonts.family
- fonts.size
- line-height
- confirm-before-quit
- copy-on-select
- hide-mouse-cursor-when-typing
- bell.audio
- bell.visual

## Deliberate All-only scope

Renderer controls, developer logging, bindings, hints, shell and editor commands, environment and working-directory overrides, detailed colors, font slots and symbol maps, platform override tables, navigation internals, background images, scrollback-history-limit, enable-scroll-bar, and other specialist controls remain All-only by default. Any non-inherited value from these groups still appears in Overview.

## Ownership and implementation

- Consume schema version 1 from docs/yazelix/config_inventory.v1.json at the exact pinned Mars revision without retaining the Mars runtime in the Mars-free package.
- Replace MARS_FIELDS as completeness owner. Keep only MARS_RECOMMENDED_PATHS and the smallest necessary Yazelix capability, apply, and display policy.
- Preserve owner shapes, choices, defaults, descriptions, and availability metadata.
- Enable inline editing only when the Mars validator accepts the value and the sparse patcher can persist it without materializing unrelated paths. Ratconfig renders unsupported unions, tables, and structured collections as read-only; do not add a Mars file action in this bead.
- Preserve sparse user overrides, packaged inheritance, atomic writes, native validation, and Home Manager ownership.
- Use conservative apply labels and update configuration docs, architecture, changelog, and LOC scorecards.

## Verification

- Assert the Mars revision and schema version at the consumption boundary.
- Prove every non-filtered catalog entry becomes exactly one Ratconfig field and no local completeness list remains.
- Prove representative Overview, All-only, explicit advanced, externally managed, searched, and platform-constrained rows behave correctly.
- Prove window.blur is discoverable and accepts false, true, macos-glass-regular, and macos-glass-clear while rejecting unknown strings.
- Exercise representative scalar, enum, union, list, table, and structured metadata plus sparse write and reset behavior.
- Prove a non-recommended Home Manager value remains visible in Overview and read-only.
- Run cargo test --manifest-path crates/yzx-config/Cargo.toml, nix flake check, nix flake show --all-systems, nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs, and a temporary profile install.
- Do not launch a GUI session unless separately requested.

## Stop conditions

Stop if consumption retains the Mars runtime, Ratconfig accepts values rejected by Mars, implementation mirrors owner semantics locally, Overview can hide explicit or invalid fields, or Mars-specific schema or rendering enters Ratconfig.
notes:
Consume Mars revision 129981b3a5b9f0a9ef1fa60d2742845cb1722db3 at docs/yazelix/config_inventory.v1.json, schema_version 1. It contains 151 unique owner entries: 133 base settings and 18 platform override groups. Filter mars.appearance.preset at the Yazelix adapter boundary, yielding 150 All rows, 15 Overview recommendations, and 135 All-only rows. Preserve macOS-only decoration, navigation, renderer, and window metadata plus the WGPU filter constraint.

The owner catalog is the sole inventory and semantic-metadata source. The sparse user TOML records intent; reset removes the override and recomputes inherited baseline and effective state. Default TOML supplies observed packaged values only and cannot discover absent settings. Ratconfig controls require explicit validator-backed persistence capability; unsupported unions, tables, and structured collections remain read-only. Current Ratconfig has no dedicated Mars file action, and this bead must not add one.

Invalid-input boundary: localize a bad field when the Mars owner parser can do so. If the sparse Mars TOML is wholly unparseable, expose a source-level diagnostic without adding a second tolerant parser. Do not reintroduce literal group counts or a local MARS_FIELDS completeness list.
close_reason: Completed the pinned Mars inventory consumer with the corrected ownership boundary: Mars remains the 151-entry catalog owner, Ratconfig remains generic, and Yazelix filters the appearance projection and owns recommendations, conservative capabilities, sparse persistence, apply labels, and Home Manager policy. Mars now shows 15 Overview recommendations and 150 All rows; search, availability metadata, finite window.blur values, malformed TOML blocking, advanced explicit values, and sparse write/reset are covered. Verification passed: 63 yzx-config tests locally and in Nix, cargo fmt, git diff check, nix flake show --all-systems, nix build .#yazelix, all 97 Linux flake checks including no_mars_contracts, isolated profile install, and installed profile refresh.

title: Expose all cursor settings and review Overview recommendations
description:
## Why

The Cursors tab exposes a small common subset and a full-file action, but users cannot discover every child-owned cursor setting from Ratconfig unless they already know cursors.toml. The complete cursor definitions and settings must remain owned by yazelix-cursors.

## Evidence

- crates/yzx-config/src/catalog.rs:115 defines six CURSOR_FIELDS.
- crates/yzx-config/src/model.rs:292 builds the common cursor fields and derives some allowed values from the loaded registry.
- crates/yzx-config/src/file_actions.rs:61 opens the complete cursors.toml.
- crates/yzx-config/src/native_config.rs routes edits through child-owned cursor parsing and preservation.
- flake.nix packages the pinned yazelix-cursors input and its default template.

## User-Visible Contract

All exposes every setting in the packaged yazelix-cursors schema and makes dynamic cursor definitions discoverable without pretending their user-defined ids are finite settings. Overview contains the common pool, selection, and effect controls selected by review. Explicit custom values remain visible. Complex definitions may be read-only with the complete-file action.

## Scope

In scope:
- Consume the complete version-locked child schema rather than expanding CURSOR_FIELDS as a duplicate owner.
- Review every child setting for an Overview recommendation.
- Distinguish schema settings from dynamic cursor definitions and surface both honestly.
- Preserve the seeded exact file, custom definitions, sparse edits where supported, Home Manager ownership, and cross-consumer apply descriptions.
- Prove schema-to-Ratconfig coverage and allowed-value discovery.
- Record which richer effects Mars consumes, stores for other consumers, or does not yet use.

Out of scope:
- No new cursor effect, schema field, definition format, or consumer behavior.
- No generated mirror of the child schema.
- No automatic rewrite of custom definitions.

## Verification

- cargo test --manifest-path crates/yzx-config/Cargo.toml exits 0 with child schema parity and custom-definition preservation tests.
- Focused tests prove one Overview setting, one non-recommended setting, one explicit non-recommended value, and a complex custom definition are discoverable.
- nix flake check exits 0.
- The LOC scorecard and current-state docs are refreshed when project files change.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the child schema and loaded registry disagree.
- Stop if full discovery requires Yazelix to own cursor validation.

title: Curate Zellij fields and expose the native config fallback
description:
## Why

Zellij owns a broad native KDL surface, while Yazelix safely edits ten curated scalar fields and reserves several top-level nodes for integration policy. Mirroring Zellij's schema or turning every preserved native leaf into a Ratconfig row would add a second owner without improving safe editing.

- Search finds typed fields across All and the exact `zellij/config.kdl` file action.
- The native file action is the escape hatch for every setting outside the curated editor.
- Safe unknown top-level leaves remain byte-for-byte preserved without one UI row or diagnostic per leaf.
- Diagnostics remain for conditions that require attention: invalid known fields, ignored legacy `theme`, malformed or structurally unsafe KDL, and guarded integration-owned nodes. Guarded diagnostics name the Yazelix owner and remain non-editable.

Yazelix does not claim that All is the complete native Zellij schema.

## Ownership

- Zellij owns native names, types, accepted values, and semantic validity.
- Yazelix owns the ten-field editable subset, six-field recommendation policy, sparse preservation, integration guards, actionable diagnostic text, and the native-file route.
- Ratconfig owns generic Overview/All, All-scope search, file-action presentation, and existing diagnostic rendering. This slice adds no Ratconfig feature.

## Scope

In scope:
- Classify the existing ten typed fields into Overview and All.
- Add the exact Zellij native-file action.
- Keep the existing sparse sidecar writer, resets, active-runtime patch, and opaque-leaf preservation.
- Make guarded diagnostics identify their Yazelix integration owner.
- Document that the native file is the discovery surface outside the curated fields.

Out of scope:
- No complete local Zellij inventory, copied schema, scraped catalog, or literal mirror test.
- No synthetic fields for unknown or guarded nodes.
- No per-leaf informational diagnostic for safe opaque state.
- No contextual diagnostic-routing feature in Ratconfig.
- No generic KDL parser/editor or relaxation of integration guards.

## Verification

A focused contract test proves one Overview field, one All-only field, All-scope search, the exact native file action, safe opaque preservation across an unrelated write, and a guarded source blocker with ownership guidance. Existing sparse write, reset, active-file patch, parser safety, and guard-parity checks remain green. Run the yzx-config test suite and `nix flake check`.

## Stop conditions

Stop if completion requires a native schema mirror, synthetic discovery fields, a Ratconfig API change, writable guarded nodes, or a second preservation owner.

## Rejected alternatives

Rejected: a full Yazelix Zellij schema, a Ratconfig KDL adapter, host-side diagnostic-to-field conversion, routed diagnostics on ordinary tabs, one informational diagnostic per safe opaque leaf, documentation scraping, and hiding the exact native file action.

Fresh-eyes simplification: shared file-action lookup between the Nushell and Zellij contracts; changed Nushell search assertions from exact singleton results to reachability, which matches the non-exclusive search contract; removed duplicate ownership and visibility assertions already proved by the native-file inventory test; and shortened the finite-schema explanation. Net result is six tracked lines removed with runtime behavior unchanged.
close_reason: Completed: kept shell.program and Starship with their existing owners, made both executable Nu source actions and their layering searchable, documented the finite-schema boundary, and added focused ownership/search coverage.

title: Keep config popup state across toggles
description:
## Why

Closing and reopening the config popup restarts Ratconfig on its first tab, making repeated configuration work unnecessarily tedious. Toggling the popup within the same workspace should resume where the user left it.

## Evidence

- Runtime dogfooding report on 2026-07-14: toggling the config popup returns to the first tab.
- `defaults/zellij/config.kdl:16-22` defines `config_popup` without `toggle_close_behavior`, so the popup plugin uses its default close policy.
- `../yazelix-zellij-popup/src/popup_contract.rs:868-872` supports `toggle_close_behavior "hide"`; `src/main.rs:380-389` suppresses the pane without terminating its process.
- `../ratconfig/src/editor.rs:98-105` initializes a new app at tab and row zero. Avoiding process restart therefore preserves the existing in-memory UI state without adding another persistence owner.
- The agent popup already uses the same keep-alive policy in `defaults/zellij/config.kdl:24-31`.

## Scope

### In scope

- Give the packaged config popup the existing hide-on-toggle policy.
- Within the same live tab/workspace and process, reopening the popup preserves at least the selected config tab and selected row.
- Keep popup restart-on-real-workspace-CWD-change behavior intact.
- Update the focused generated-config contract, CHANGELOG, and README LOC scorecard as required.

### Out of scope

- Disk persistence across Yazelix sessions, Ratconfig restarts, crashes, upgrades, or workspace-CWD changes.
- New Ratconfig state files, a generic popup-plugin behavior change, or making every popup stateful.
- Persisting unsaved configuration values beyond Ratconfig's existing process behavior.

## Implementation Notes

1. Set `toggle_close_behavior "hide"` only on the main-owned `config` popup specification.
2. Update the existing popup-spec contract in `checks/yzx-contracts.rs` to prove the generated KDL carries that policy.
3. Do not add Ratconfig serialization or modify the popup child unless the packaged policy demonstrably fails.
4. Treat the hidden process's existing in-memory state as the sole state owner.

## Verification

- The focused Yazelix contract expects hide behavior for config and preserves the existing policies for agent, git, and menu.
- In a live Nova session, navigate away from the first config tab and row, toggle the popup off, then toggle it on; the same tab and row return.
- Changing to a genuinely different workspace CWD retains the popup plugin's existing stale-process restart behavior.
- `nix flake check`, `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs`, and a temporary-profile install pass succeed.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if Zellij terminates or recreates the pane despite the existing hide policy; capture pane/process identity before changing Ratconfig.
- Stop if preserving state requires a disk format or cross-session lifecycle decision; that is separate user scope.
- Stop before changing generic popup defaults or other popup lifecycles.

## Maintenance Notes

Owner: the main-repository generated popup specification.

Effort: XS. Risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH.

Rejected alternatives: a Ratconfig state sidecar, restoring tabs from the Yazelix config TOML, changing the generic popup default, and keeping every popup alive.
close_reason: Config popup now uses the existing hide-on-toggle lifecycle, preserving Ratconfig tab and row state while its process remains alive. Generated-config regression coverage, current-state docs, changelog, LOC scorecard, flake checks, package build, temporary profile install, and installed runtime upgrade all pass; no Ratconfig or popup-child changes were needed. GUI dogfood remains for the user because agents do not launch GUI sessions implicitly.

title: Split Darwin compatibility builds into cached stages
description:
The native Darwin newer-nixpkgs compatibility gate runs as three dependent jobs: core workspace -> editor/file manager -> complete Home Manager integration. Each stage uses the exact candidate revision and the reviewed nixpkgs pin. Core/editor publish their runtime closures synchronously through the existing Yazelix Cachix cache before dependent jobs can succeed. Linux and the separate locked-input Darwin checks retain their coverage; final Home Manager fixtures and Rio tests remain authoritative.

Ownership: existing Nova package variants define the partitions. GitHub needs is the sole owner of prerequisite output paths. Native Nix restores raw outputs through configured substituters with local and remote builders disabled: nix-store --realise --max-jobs 0 --builders ''. NAR signatures remain checked. Missing/malformed outputs, unavailable cache paths, build failures and publication failures reject the stage; the aggregate gate requires success from all five native jobs. No single-cache copy or duplicated upstream binaries.

Trust and cost: trusted manual runs on the canonical repository's edge/main/stable refs only, guarded before checkout and credential use. Only core/editor receive the existing publication credential; final integration reads public caches. One Version Gate concurrency group. Five native jobs retain 90-minute caps and the aggregate gate five minutes: 455 configured runner-minutes. Only prerequisite closures are published, using existing retention/deduplication with no retention pins. No new workflow/service/secret, store archive, public package API, schedule, compatibility push/PR trigger or runtime dependency change.

The user selected this partition after the monolithic Darwin job timed out at 90 minutes. The user rejected an unchanged retry; it was cancelled. Raising the cap to 120 minutes, dropping tests or shrinking integration coverage was not accepted. Timings and cache transfers must be measured; cached success is not a cold-build guarantee. Revisit the partition if a stage approaches its finite limit.

Implemented and verified at c09419e9fedef1eb290b9f04373fc7526bc339bd with reviewed nixpkgs github:NixOS/nixpkgs/dc5d91f840324650bac8c379428c7037a416959a. Development guidance and the LOC scorecard describe the accepted workflow. This issue owns the implementation and proof only. Main/Stable promotion belongs to yazelix-5vl-promote-cache-guidance-71kp; later pins require release evidence for their own exact candidate.
notes:
Accepted native result: https://github.com/Yazelix/nova/actions/runs/34272794513 passed all five native jobs and release-gate at c09419e9. Exact Linux CI https://github.com/Yazelix/nova/actions/runs/34272793455 and Darwin Package Smoke https://github.com/Yazelix/nova/actions/runs/34272797569 passed.

Measured job times: Linux 58m19s; locked Darwin 16m32s; core 5m19s; editor 42m57s; final integration 17m19s; aggregate gate 5s. Total unweighted job time 140m31s, not billed minutes. Stage build commands took 3m1.371s / 40m29.803s / 15m30.107s. Editor restored core in 16s; integration restored both roots in 35s. These measurements reuse existing cache entries. A prior successful core build took 38m56.673s (40m31s job); no fully cold benchmark is claimed.

Exact handoff: core /nix/store/485x9vrfk27fv50x9liyvhy4rp1x5lch-yazelix-no-rio-no-helix-no-yazi (closure 2,073,839,216 bytes) and editor /nix/store/361l1jws6crfsx78gz5apzdb3lh0nyn2-yazelix-no-rio (2,689,597,848 bytes). Including the earlier successfully published core yields 391 unique paths, 84,884,402 compressed bytes / 441,217,864 NAR bytes. These are per-path metadata sums, not measured billing or net physical cache growth. Existing retention applies; no policy expansion or retention pin.

Initial staged run 34252445853 at 5acf48bc failed core after 47m34s due to timestamp-based test TempHome collisions. title: Decide Anima prebuilt releases when demanded
description:
## Why

Anima exposes the standalone native `yzs` command and already supports Cargo builds, but it has no prebuilt releases. Prebuilt downloads may reduce adoption friction, yet they create an OS/architecture support promise and must decide how the separately executed `asciiquarium-rs` dependency is delivered. There is no current user request proving that this release matrix is worth owning.

## Evidence

Audited public `Yazelix/anima` main at `d22d091d427af0be307056c65e475802b602d386`:

- `README.md:3-14`: Anima is standalone, but the first installation examples use Nix.
- `README.md:19-25`: the package includes native animations, a separately packaged aquarium, and the `yzs` binary.
- `README.md:51-73`: Cargo runs are documented; source-only runs resolve `asciiquarium-rs` from `PATH`, while Nix pins it.
- `README.md:95-99`: the aquarium remains a separate GPL-2.0-or-later process.
- `README.md:142-163`: SemVer/tag policy and repository verification already exist.
- `src/screen_runner.rs:219-233`: the runtime launches a compile-time override or `asciiquarium-rs` from `PATH` and surfaces launch/exit failures.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1-29`: CI covers Ubuntu Rust and Nix checks but has no release job.
- GitHub repository metadata at the audited revision reports zero releases.

## Decision To Make

When concrete user demand exists, decide:

- which OS/architecture pairs are supported and proved;
- whether releases contain only `yzs` or an archive with additional runtime files;
- whether `asciiquarium-rs` stays an explicit external dependency, is separately downloadable, or is bundled after license/provenance review;
- how missing aquarium support is documented without implying that native styles are unavailable;
- whether checksums and installation instructions justify the ongoing release workload.

Until that demand exists, keep this Bead deferred and do not add a release matrix.

## Scope

In scope after reactivation:

- Measure demand and record the supported target set.
- Define the archive/binary naming, checksum, install, and dependency contract.
- Preserve native Anima styles when the aquarium dependency is absent.
- Bound workflow jobs, permissions, timeouts, caches, and concurrency.

Out of scope:

- Changing animation behavior or `yzx anima` integration.
- Copying/linking the aquarium implementation into Anima.
- Claiming untested platform support.
- Adding installers, auto-update, or package-manager distribution in the first slice.

## Implementation Notes

1. Reopen only with a concrete user request or an accepted distribution goal.
2. Test the smallest target set that satisfies that demand.
3. Compare binary-only delivery with a complete archive; prefer the former if the external aquarium contract is clear.
4. Review GPL process/bundling obligations before distributing any aquarium artifact.
5. Add no Rust crate unless it removes more platform/release complexity than it introduces.

## Verification

From the child repository:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test`, and `cargo check --examples` should exit 0.
- `cargo run --bin yzs -- --help` and `cargo run --example render_once` should exit 0.
- `nix build .#yzs --no-link` should preserve the reference package.
- On every claimed release target, an extracted artifact should run `yzs --help`, one native bounded animation, and both the documented success and missing-dependency behavior for `asciiquarium`.
- Release checks must distinguish compilation from execution on the target platform.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop while there is no concrete demand or accepted release goal.
- Stop if a target cannot be executed on its claimed platform.
- Stop if aquarium redistribution or license provenance is unresolved.
- Stop if the smallest honest release requires a broad matrix disproportionate to demonstrated use.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort M. Risk MEDIUM. Confidence HIGH in the current gap and dependency boundary; confidence LOW that prebuilt releases are presently worth their lifecycle cost. This is intentionally deferred rather than actionable backlog.

title: Decide complete Cursors release archives when demanded
description:
## Why

Yazelix Cursors exposes a standalone native `yzc` command but has no prebuilt releases. A raw binary would be incomplete: the supported experience also needs the default registry, vendored and generated shader trees, and examples assembled by the Nix package. Platform archives may be useful later, but there is no current user request justifying their matrix and relocation contract.

## Evidence

Audited public `Yazelix/cursors` main at `2383c2e6a5484379414434f9d572421f440722c7`:

- `README.md:3-19`: the product is standalone and contains packaged shader assets plus the `yzc` binary, while install examples are Nix-only.
- `README.md:149-160`: Cargo and Nix verification commands exist.
- `Cargo.toml:13-15`: Cargo builds the native `yzc` binary.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:16-24`: source verification passes an explicit `--share-dir assets/ghostty` when generating Ghostty output.
- `flake.nix:45-68`: Nix builds `yzc`, copies the default registry and shader assets, then generates the final shader tree.
- `flake.nix:70-135`: the package creates an example and verifies the binary, registry, generated shaders, and effects as one output.
- `flake.nix:138-150`: package metadata names the stable share-root and shader-root contract.
- GitHub repository metadata at the audited revision reports zero releases; its only workflow is CI.

## Decision To Make

When concrete user demand exists, decide the smallest complete non-Nix release:

- supported OS/architecture pairs;
- archive layout containing `yzc` and the required share tree;
- how `yzc` discovers a relocated share directory, or the exact explicit flag users must supply;
- checksum, version, and installation instructions;
- whether pre-generated shaders are shipped, generated during packaging, or generated after install.

A raw `yzc` binary is not an acceptable complete release.

## Scope

In scope after reactivation:

- Preserve the existing command, config, package, and shader contracts.
- Reproduce the Nix package's generic standalone files in a portable archive.
- Prove extraction and Ghostty generation from an isolated location.
- Bound any release workflow by accepted target demand.

Out of scope:

- Nova per-window integration, settings wiring, or reroll policy.
- Renaming `yzc`, `yazelix_cursors`, config paths, or shader contracts.
- Publishing only the executable.
- Package-manager installers or auto-update in the first slice.
- Combining this work with repository-name canonicalization.

## Implementation Notes

1. Keep this deferred until a concrete user request or accepted distribution goal exists.
2. Complete `yazelix-5vl-469.1` before editing release documentation so canonical repository prose has one owner.
3. Inventory the exact Nix output and choose a relocatable archive root.
4. Test whether explicit `--share-dir` is sufficient; do not add discovery code unless it materially reduces user steps without creating path ambiguity.
5. Prefer standard archive/checksum tooling and add no Rust crate unless required by the accepted relocation contract.

## Verification

From the child repository:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --all-targets`, and `cargo test` should exit 0.
- `cargo run --bin yzc -- --help` and `cargo run --bin yzc -- list-targets` should exit 0.
- `nix build .#yazelix_cursors --no-link` should preserve the reference package contract.
- An archive prototype should unpack into an isolated directory; `yzc` should initialize config and generate Ghostty output using only files inside that archive plus the isolated config directory.
- The generated config, default registry, palette shaders, generated effects, example, and executable should all be non-empty.
- Every claimed platform should execute the extracted binary on that platform.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop while there is no concrete demand or accepted release goal.
- Stop until `yazelix-5vl-469.1` is complete.
- Stop if a complete archive requires changing stable identifiers or Nova-owned integration.
- Stop if share-directory relocation cannot be specified without a new public contract decision.
- Stop if the proposed matrix cannot execute its artifacts on each claimed platform.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort M. Risk MEDIUM. Confidence HIGH that binary-only distribution is incomplete; confidence LOW that a prebuilt matrix is currently worth maintaining. This is intentionally deferred rather than actionable backlog.

title: Make Atuin the default managed shell history
description:
## Why

Nova promises Nushell, Bash, Zsh, and Fish as packaged shell choices. The published Atuin slice at a705382a applies shell.atuin only to Nushell, so the default history promise is inconsistent across supported shells. The maintainer chose one product contract: Atuin is the default managed history integration for every packaged shell.

## Evidence

- runtime/yzx-shell.sh dispatches shell.program to packaged nu, bash, zsh, or fish.
- flake.nix generates the locked Atuin 18.16.1 Nushell init and packages all four shells.
- The locked atuin init command supports nu, bash, zsh, and fish plus --disable-up-arrow and --disable-ai.
- Bash supports an explicit interactive rc file, Fish supports a post-config init command, and Zsh supports a temporary ZDOTDIR startup layer.
- The published Nushell contract already proves default-on, false opt-out, user-init coexistence, ATUIN_NOBIND, native Up-arrow, Carapace completion, and packaged-artifact identity.

## User-visible contract

The consumer is a user starting any new Nova-managed shell selected by shell.program. shell.atuin defaults to true and applies to nu, bash, zsh, and fish.

When true, Nova exposes the exact locked Atuin executable and loads a build-generated integration after that shell's normal user startup file. Existing user Atuin initialization wins and is not duplicated. Ctrl-R opens Atuin search; Up-arrow remains native shell history; Atuin AI bindings are disabled. ATUIN_NOBIND retains capture without managed bindings.

When false, Nova starts the selected shell with its normal startup contract and no Nova-managed Atuin hooks or bindings. Changing the setting never imports, deletes, or rewrites either native or Atuin history.

A managed initialization failure remains visible but does not prevent the selected shell from starting. Nova does not own Atuin login, sync, daemon, pty proxy, AI, dotfiles, filters, styles, or native configuration.

## Scope

- Generate normal and ATUIN_NOBIND init artifacts for nu, bash, zsh, and fish from unmodified pkgs.atuin with Up-arrow and AI bindings disabled.
- Extend yzx-shell through each shell's native startup mechanism while preserving user startup ordering and ownership.
- Keep the existing Nushell integration and Carapace completion contract.
- Add installed-package checks for default-on, opt-out, native startup, binding policy, packaged Atuin, and user-init coexistence across Bash, Zsh, and Fish.
- Update current-state README, configuration, architecture, runtime notes, changelog, and LOC scorecard.
- Document one-time explicit imports for every supported shell.

## Out of scope

- Automatic imports, deduplication, deletion, login, sync, daemon, pty proxy, AI, or Atuin-native configuration.
- Other shells, Home Manager shell configuration, an Atuin fork, or a custom feature-pruned derivation.
- Replacing Carapace or changing shell.program semantics.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if a shell cannot preserve its normal user startup file before managed initialization.
- Stop if coexistence requires parsing or rewriting user configuration.
- Stop if Atuin changes native Up-arrow behavior, duplicates user hooks, or prevents shell startup.
design: Nix generates locked Atuin 18.16.1 init files for nu, bash, zsh, and fish, with normal and ATUIN_NOBIND variants and with Up-arrow plus AI bindings disabled. yzx-nu retains its existing composition. yzx-shell owns the other shell boundary and prepends the closed helper PATH required by the generated Atuin scripts. Bash uses a build-generated rc file that sources ~/.bashrc first; Fish uses its post-config init command; Zsh uses a temporary ZDOTDIR layer that sources the effective user .zshenv, follows its final ZDOTDIR including HOME fallback, then sources .zshrc before Atuin and restores the user ZDOTDIR. Each layer detects the shell-specific Atuin search function before sourcing managed init.
acceptance_criteria:
- shell.atuin defaults to true for nu, bash, zsh, and fish; false disables only Nova-managed initialization for every shell.
- Each shell loads its normal user startup file before the build-generated Atuin integration, and an existing user integration remains the sole hook owner.
- Every managed shell resolves the exact packaged Atuin 18.16.1, exposes Atuin Ctrl-R search and lifecycle capture, retains native Up-arrow history, and has no managed Atuin AI binding.
- ATUIN_NOBIND suppresses managed bindings while retaining capture hooks in every shell.
- Initialization failures remain visible and do not prevent shell startup.
- Nova performs no automatic import, deletion, login, sync, daemon, pty proxy, AI, or native Atuin configuration. Documentation gives explicit one-time nu, bash, zsh, and fish imports with the non-idempotence warning.
- Focused installed-shell contracts, config tests, rustfmt, Clippy, Cargo tests, nix flake check, four-system evaluation, top-level build, isolated-profile installation, installed edge refresh, protected hosted Linux CI, and the manual Linux/macOS Version Gate pass.
- The exact accepted revision identifies Yazelix Nova 1.1.0, is committed and pushed to edge, and is promoted unchanged through main and stable. The immutable nova-v1.1.0 tag and GitHub release identify that same revision.
notes:
Accepted state: Yazelix Nova 1.1.0 makes shell.atuin default true for packaged Nushell, Bash, Zsh, and Fish. Nova composes locked Atuin 18.16.1 after native user startup, preserves user-owned Atuin hooks, keeps native Up-arrow history, disables Atuin AI bindings, honors ATUIN_NOBIND, and leaves false as a managed-init-only opt-out. Nova does not import, delete, log in, sync, configure, or run Atuin services automatically.

Fresh-eyes and simplification fixed Bash option ordering, Fish block scoping, Zsh HOME fallback after a user .zshenv unsets ZDOTDIR, and the missing GNU sed dependency used by generated Bash/Zsh init. The no-bind source selection now appends one suffix instead of duplicating paths, and Nushell no longer inherits alternative-shell helper PATH. Installed contracts cover default-on, ATUIN_NOBIND, disabled, packaged-binary identity, native startup, Ctrl-R binding, generated-script helper availability, and user-owned integration for all four shells. The final feature is net +175 tracked-text lines over a705382a; the repository scorecard is 27,489 lines.

Package evidence: exact clean release revision da60dc7a855048edabe9706207d4f0721ed3c0a8 built and installed as /nix/store/cbmhjzk9sxj517qrarf758cfp9d7zfvn-yazelix, reporting Yazelix Nova (1.1.0). Local x86_64-linux proof passed 93 flake checks, four-system evaluation, top-level build, exact-revision isolated-profile activation, and the local edge profile refresh. The maintainer manually dogfooded and accepted the Atuin interaction before release.

Hosted proof passed Edge CI 31360013355, Linux and aarch64-darwin Version Gate 31360018658, Main CI 31360380522, Linux and aarch64-darwin cache publication 31360380509, and Stable CI 31360875439. edge, main, and stable all resolve to da60dc7a855048edabe9706207d4f0721ed3c0a8. Annotated tag nova-v1.1.0 resolves to that revision, and https://github.com/Yazelix/nova/releases/tag/nova-v1.1.0 is published. The maintainer explicitly requested this stable promotion on 2026-08-10 despite the normal weekly cadence.
close_reason: Released as Yazelix Nova 1.1.0 on edge, main, stable, and immutable tag nova-v1.1.0 with all required local and hosted checks passing.

title: Design complete non-Nix Status Kit distribution
description:
## Why

`zellij-status-kit` presents itself as standalone, but its documented installation path is Nix-only. Unlike a single Zellij plugin, the usable product is a coordinated bundle containing a native helper, a pinned upstream `zjstatus.wasm`, rendered/template KDL, and examples. Publishing only one file would create a misleading and incomplete non-Nix surface.

## Evidence

Audited public `Yazelix/zellij-status-kit` main at `0908737a19d22c9d8d12946dbbd82f6b3a170837`:

- `README.md:3-5`: the repository promises a standalone status-bar package.
- `README.md:7-26`: installation is Nix-only and the installed contract lists the native helper, WASM, KDL templates, examples, and documentation.
- `README.md:41`: the package rewrites the preset to the pinned `zjstatus.wasm`.
- `Cargo.toml:13-15`: Cargo builds only the native `yazelix_zellij_bar_widget` binary.
- `flake.nix:75,97-107`: Nix assembles the upstream WASM, substituted preset, templates, native helper, examples, and README.
- `flake.nix:120-138`: install checks and passthru metadata define the complete package contract.
- GitHub repository metadata at the audited revision reports zero releases and no Actions workflows.

## Decision To Make

Choose the smallest honest non-Nix distribution contract:

1. Document manual assembly from the native Cargo build, upstream WASM release, and copied templates/examples.
2. Publish complete platform-specific archives containing the helper plus the child-owned package tree.
3. Retain Nix-only installation until concrete demand justifies the archive matrix.

A raw `zjstatus.wasm` or raw helper binary is not an acceptable complete release.

## Scope

In scope:

- Define the non-Nix distribution unit, archive layout, supported OS/architecture set, checksum/provenance story, and update cadence for the pinned upstream WASM.
- Decide whether the helper is mandatory or optional for a minimal standalone preset.
- Prove that copied/substituted KDL refers to paths valid after archive extraction.
- Record the chosen design and rejected alternatives in this Bead before implementation.

Out of scope:

- Forking `zjstatus`.
- Moving Yazelix runtime-only widgets, cache paths, or session policy into the child.
- Publishing a lone WASM under the Status Kit name.
- Changing stable package, command, or artifact names.
- Editing Nova while deciding the child-owned distribution shape.

## Implementation Notes

1. Start from the audited child revision or review drift.
2. Inventory the exact Nix output and separate generic standalone files from Yazelix-runtime examples.
3. Compare manual instructions with per-target archives by user steps, owners, CI jobs, artifact count, and failure boundaries.
4. Review the pinned `zjstatus` release/license provenance before redistributing its WASM.
5. Prefer the smallest option that is complete; only create an implementation task after this decision is accepted.

## Verification

Evidence for the decision should include:

- `cargo test` should exit 0.
- `cargo build --release` should produce the native helper.
- `nix build .#yazelix_zellij_bar --no-link` should exit 0 and remain the reference package contract.
- Any archive prototype should unpack into an isolated directory, contain every chosen contract file, run the helper's help surface, and have KDL paths resolve within the extracted tree.
- Every claimed supported platform should build and execute on that platform; compilation alone is not runtime proof.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the current package contract has drifted materially.
- Stop if upstream WASM redistribution/provenance is unresolved.
- Stop if the proposal silently requires Nova runtime paths or policies.
- Stop before implementing a platform matrix until the supported targets are explicitly accepted.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort M. Risk MEDIUM. Confidence HIGH that a one-file release is incomplete; confidence MEDIUM on the best replacement until the archive/manual-install comparison is measured. No new Rust crate is expected. Do not depend on the shared Zellij WASI builder decision: this package's hard part is multi-artifact native distribution, not compiling its upstream WASM.

title: Run Rio-free contracts in hosted release checks
description:
## Contract

Consumer: maintainers promoting Nova Rio-free package variants.

title: Follow successful managed Yazi opens to the target directory
description:
## Why

The standard managed Yazi file opener invokes `yzx-open` but leaves the sidebar at its previous cwd. This is visible when a file is opened from search, flat view, or another result whose containing directory differs from the current Yazi directory. The existing Yazi `Alt z` plugin demonstrates the intended navigation: it emits `cd` to the chosen directory before opening it in the editor.

This is local sidebar navigation, not a tab-workspace retarget. The canonical workspace root and hidden-agent lifecycle must remain governed by `yazelix-5vl-f69`.

## User-visible contract

- After a successful open originating from the managed Yazi sidebar, that same Yazi instance follows the primary target: a file moves it to the file's containing directory; a directory moves it to that directory.
- The opened absolute target still reaches the managed editor unchanged.
- Following the target does not change the canonical tab workspace, rename the workspace from the target, restart the hidden agent, or move existing shell panes.
- A failed or rejected editor handoff leaves Yazi at its previous cwd and reports the existing clear error.
- Opens not originating from the managed sidebar do not move it.
- Existing `Alt z` behavior remains consistent with this contract and should reuse the same smallest reliable target-follow mechanism when practical.

## Scope

- Identify the originating managed Yazi instance reliably even when `yzx-open` focuses Helix before the open completes. Prefer the request's Yazi identity or the orchestrator's registered sidebar identity over the currently focused pane.
- Emit one targeted Yazi `cd` only after the managed open is known to have succeeded.
- For multiple targets, follow the containing directory of the primary/first target while passing every requested target to the editor.
- Preserve paths containing spaces and non-UTF-8-safe process arguments to the extent supported by the existing opener contract.
- Cover bridge reuse and new-editor fallback, plus files reached from nested search/flat-view results.
- Keep sidebar state publication and Starship/Git refresh behavior flowing through the existing Yazi `cd` subscription.

## Guardrails

- Do not treat Yazi cwd as the canonical tab workspace or feed this local move back into explicit retargeting.
- Do not broadcast `cd` to every Yazi instance or infer the recipient from whichever pane is focused after Helix opens.
- Do not change cwd before success unless the operation can reliably roll back.
- Do not add a second target parser, Git-root resolver, or workspace-state store.
- Do not fold global `Alt z`, hide-on-open policy, or general sidebar reveal behavior into this bug.
- Keep this in the main repo by default: use the existing managed opener, upstream Yazi `emit-to`/`cd`, and orchestrator sidebar registration. Do not change the Helix fork, archived Yazi fork, or popup child for this local navigation effect.

## Verification

Use a focused matrix covering a file already in the current directory, a nested file selected from search/flat view, a directory target, multiple files, a path with spaces, bridge success, new-editor fallback success, rejected open, and no registered sidebar. Observe both the sidebar cwd and the unchanged orchestrator workspace/agent identity.

## Maintenance notes

P2 main-repo runtime bug. Depends on the canonical workspace contract so local target-follow cannot accidentally become another workspace-retarget path. No Helix fork change is expected.
acceptance_criteria: A successful managed-Yazi open moves only the originating sidebar Yazi to the primary file's containing directory or the opened directory. Nested/search results, multiple targets, paths with spaces, live-bridge reuse, and new-editor fallback are covered. Failed/rejected opens and non-Yazi invocations leave the sidebar cwd unchanged. The canonical orchestrator workspace, tab/workspace label, existing shell panes, and hidden-agent PID remain unchanged by this local navigation, and the implementation reuses existing sidebar registration and Yazi cd publication rather than adding state. The fix remains in main-repo integration code and uses existing child APIs; any child-repo change requires a focused demonstrated capability gap rather than convenience.
close_reason: Implemented targeted post-success Yazi follow in yzx-open; verified bridge reuse, new-editor fallback, file/directory targets, multiple targets, spaces, non-originating calls, failure behavior, runtime contracts, full flake checks, package build, and profile install.

title: Evaluate an editor-free workspace retarget command
description:
## Question

Should Yazelix expose a command or option that changes the active tab's canonical workspace without opening or focusing Helix?

The canonical workspace contract will make the pane orchestrator the per-tab root owner. That creates a useful capability independent of editor lifecycle, but the user-facing need, command name, discoverability, and side effects are not chosen yet.

## Evaluate

- A direct command such as `yzx workspace <path>`, a menu action, or a picker result that performs only an explicit tab retarget.
- Behavior when no editor exists, when an editor exists but has local cwd drift, and when the target is Git, non-Git, a nested repository, missing, or unreadable.
- Which consumers update: orchestrator root, tab/workspace label, status, future workspace-root panes, and hidden agent stale state.
- Which consumers stay local: existing shell panes, Yazi navigation, file-local terminals, and open editor buffers.
- Whether the sidebar should navigate to the new root or remain where it is.
- Relationship to the tab-level Alt-z picker: separate command, picker mode, or rejected overlap.
- Whether the action is valuable enough to justify a new public command/config surface.

## Guardrails

- This is a decision bead, not authorization to add a command, setting, or picker mode.
- Reuse the explicit-retarget primitive; do not create another workspace owner or target resolver.
- Do not `cd` every existing pane or implicitly create an editor.
- Preserve clear failures and cancellation without partial workspace state.

## Outcome

Record one maintainer decision with the chosen user-visible contract and rejected alternatives. If approved, create the smallest implementation bead after the command/key/menu surface is explicitly chosen. If rejected, close this bead with the reason and keep retargeting behind existing workflows.
acceptance_criteria: The bead closes with an explicit accept/reject decision. An accepted design names the invocation surface, target/root policy, editor/sidebar/agent effects, failure behavior, and relationship to Alt-z, and identifies the existing retarget owner it reuses. No runtime surface is added by this decision bead.
