title: Decide Kitty graphics parity for EonTerm graduation
description:
## Accepted decision

EonTerm is Nova-worthy only after the approved Nova-relevant Kitty graphics slice works end to end. The maintainer describes this as roughly an 80 percent KGP gate. That phrase is a product heuristic, not a claim that the Kitty specification has a stable countable feature denominator and not a requirement for full protocol parity.

Consumer: Nova users running managed Yazi inside EonTerm.

Trigger: the pinned Nova Zellij and Yazi path produces a static Kitty image and resolved placement state.

Required result: exact Orbit, Venus, Eon or Eonova, and Nova revisions render managed Yazi previews correctly through the owner boundaries and lifecycle proof already specified by external epic `orb-j2i`. Until that proof exists, EonTerm cannot replace Mars as the only Nova graphical surface.

Failure behavior: unsupported graphics, missing resources, stale placements, incorrect geometry, unbounded resource pressure, or failed real-Yazi dogfood blocks graduation. Nova must not hide the loss, retain a secret Mars fallback, replay Kitty APC, parse Kitty commands in Venus, or claim Zellij support alone proves host rendering.

## Concrete graduation gate

The durable definition is the approved first slice in Orbit `orb-j2i`:

- static decoded RGB or RGBA resources transferred through a bounded resource plane;
- opaque session-epoch image identity plus libghostty generation;
- complete presentation state referring to resources without repeating pixel payloads;
- resolved placement geometry, clipping, and z-order owned by Orbit and rendered by Venus;
- bounded resource count, dimensions, bytes, chunks, outstanding transfers, queue pressure, and GPU cache;
- replacement, deletion, clear, scroll, resize, primary and alternate screens, missing-resource recovery, GPU eviction, detach, reconnect, and process exit;
- installed Linux Eonova or equivalent Nova acceptance using the real pinned Nova Zellij and managed Yazi preview path.

Full Kitty parity is not required. Animation, video, audio, Sixel, iTerm2 graphics, restart-persistent image storage, and general placeholder semantics beyond the accepted real Nova path remain outside this gate unless separately chosen.

## Ownership and sequencing

Orbit remains the sole terminal, Kitty parser, decoded-image, and placement-state owner. Venus validates bounded resource messages, owns GPU resources and caching, and draws resolved placements without parsing Kitty escapes. Eon or EonTerm composes exact accepted child revisions. Nova owns exact selection and installed end-to-end acceptance.

Nova Zellij already proves the current managed-Yazi `a=T,U=1` Unicode-placeholder translation through upstream-owned Kitty storage and placement. Open broader ID, coordinate, and separate-placement beads remain optional post-v1 compatibility work; they do not become a second graphics owner or silently expand this EonTerm graduation gate.

Update order remains Orbit contract and producer, Venus consumer, Eon or Eonova pin, then Nova dogfood. The final EonTerm comparison bead `yazelix-5vl-wmg` must consume exact accepted graphics proofs before recommending promotion. The cutover bead `yazelix-5vl-eonterm-only-graphical-surface-q5w4` remains blocked until that recommendation and its other prerequisites pass.

## Planning disposition

This decision changes no code, package, contract index, runtime, or public support claim. It does not activate implementation. Orbit `orb-j2i` remains deferred until the EonTerm cutover track is explicitly activated, at which point its existing four-slice implementation shape is the source of truth.
notes:
## Decision evidence

Maintainer decision on 2026-08-12: the existing roughly 80 percent KGP concept is sufficient in spirit as the Nova-worthiness gate for EonTerm.

The durable records distinguish two different 80 percent statements:

- Orbit graduation issue `orb-bi4.8` records GO at 80 percent advisor confidence; this is not KGP coverage.
- Deferred Orbit epic `orb-j2i` records the separately approved static Kitty resource-plane scope and exact real Nova Zellij plus Yazi acceptance path.

The accepted decision uses `orb-j2i` as the concrete testable meaning of the KGP gate. It requires the real managed Yazi preview workflow plus bounded resource and lifecycle behavior before EonTerm-only cutover, while rejecting literal full-spec parity and an untestable feature percentage.

Current Nova Zellij evidence is closed bead `yazelix-8u5-4-hnv.5`, which proves managed Yazi previews through upstream native Kitty support and the narrow current-Yazi Unicode-placeholder translation. Open beads `yazelix-5vl-kitty-u1-ids-coordinates-2h8` and `yazelix-5vl-kitty-u1-placement-ids-psu` remain later compatibility tiers rather than graduation prerequisites.

No implementation or cross-repository planning state changed. `orb-j2i` remains deferred.
close_reason: Accepted Nova-relevant static Kitty and real managed-Yazi parity as the EonTerm graduation gate; full KGP parity is not required and orb-j2i remains deferred until cutover activation.

title: Launch EonTerm with Nova native application identity
description:
## Outcome

Make every EonTerm-backed Nova package retain Nova launcher, icon, channel name, and running-window grouping through the exact EonTerm identity contract. This consumes Eon `EON-C15` from `eon-eonterm-application-identity-xwi` and Venus `VEN-C12` from `ven-caller-application-identity-dcb`; it changes no Eon or Venus contract.

## Observable contract

- Consumer: a Nova user launching an installed Edge, Main, or Stable desktop entry or `yzx launch`.
- Trigger: Nova launches exact EonTerm.
- Result: Nova supplies its canonical `yzx` native application identity while keeping channel-specific desktop names and the Nova icon. Wayland and X11/Xwayland group the running window with the selected Nova launcher. EonTerm remains visible as component lineage in diagnostics and does not rename the application to Eon, EonTerm, or Eonova.
- Failures: an incompatible EonTerm identity interface, invalid channel metadata, missing icon, or mismatched native grouping fails package/launch acceptance explicitly; Nova never falls back to an Eon identity or Mars.

## Scope and ownership

Nova owns desktop files, icons, channel labels, package metadata, the exact `yzx` identity value, and invocation. EonTerm owns validation and lifecycle compatibility. Venus owns native mapping. Orbit-authored terminal title remains independent.

Preserve the existing stable/main/edge identity rules and `yzx enter` terminal-agnostic behavior. Do not add a branding framework, copy Eon icons, mutate identity after launch, infer identity from child argv, or special-case Nova inside Eon/Venus.

## Prerequisites and references

External blockers: exact accepted Eon `eon-eonterm-application-identity-xwi` and Venus `ven-caller-application-identity-dcb`. Required: current Nova desktop constructor, channel labels, icons, `StartupWMClass`, Home Manager and package variants, status/doctor lineage, Eonova identity evidence, and the exact EON-C15 invocation/help.

## Acceptance

1. Every supported EonTerm-backed Nova package installs the correct channel desktop entry and canonical Nova icon and supplies exact `yzx` identity through EON-C15.
2. Fresh native Wayland and X11/Xwayland launches group with their Nova desktop entry and show no Eon/Eonova running-app identity.
3. Edge, Main, and Stable names remain distinct while their application grouping stays intentionally canonical; terminal-authored title updates remain functional.
4. `yzx launch` and desktop invocation agree; `yzx enter` remains usable in another capable terminal and owns no application identity.
5. `yzx status --json` and doctor report exact Nova and EonTerm lineage without treating branding as component identity.
6. Missing/mismatched identity or icon is caught by package checks before promotion; no hidden Mars/Eon fallback exists.
7. Exact package/Home Manager builds, desktop validation, temporary-profile install, fresh-session dogfood, docs/changelog where behavior changes, LOC accounting, and `git diff --check` pass.

Stop if Nova identity requires a consumer special case in Eon or Venus, a mutable identity, a compatibility alias, or a target-specific hidden terminal choice.

title: Accept upstream Rio as Nova graphical surface
description:
## Accepted outcome

The maintainer accepts exact upstream Rio `b2e7c38bdc56bb86b346ca4f37b9aeaa5151d790` plus three isolated deltas as the graphical replacement candidate for Mars:

1. Alternate-screen `CSI 2 J` removes obsolete direct Kitty placements while main-screen scrollback placements remain intact.
2. Vertical pixels left after fitting whole terminal rows are split between the top and bottom of the grid through one shared grid-origin owner.
3. The compact quit confirmation retains upstream behavior while using the accepted rounded Nova-orange/dark treatment, exact rendered-text measurement, and balanced four-sided spacing.

The candidate consumes Nova's immutable packaged terminal base for JetBrains Mono 16, line-height 1.12, transparency, and comparable geometry. It intentionally excludes split Yazelix cursors and all other Mars features.

## Maintainer decision

Fresh-session dogfood accepted Kitty graphics/redraw behavior, transparency, typography and line height, grid balance, resize/fullscreen behavior, input, rounded quit confirmation, and shutdown. The maintainer explicitly accepted dropping split Yazelix cursor support rather than preserving the broad Mars fork. Upstream Rio's native solid cursor and animated trail are sufficient.

## Failure and promotion boundary

This issue proves and accepts the isolated candidate only. It did not commit or publish the child source, change Nova's normal package/profile/desktop entry, remove Mars or Yazelix Cursors, open an upstream PR, or advance a channel.

Durable follow-through is split into:
- `yazelix-5vl-publish-minimal-rio-delta-h2m5`: publish the exact minimal Rio delta as a pinned child artifact.
- `yazelix-5vl-replace-mars-remove-cursors-j3ra`: consume that artifact in Nova and delete the Mars/Cursors integration after isolated dogfood and explicit cutover acceptance.

## Preserved evidence

The issue notes and comments retain the exact Nix artifacts, revisions, commands, negative Vulkan-loader result, ED2 regression refinement, low-memory build evidence, and successive dogfood handoffs.
acceptance_criteria:
[x] Candidate baseline is exact upstream `b2e7c38bdc56bb86b346ca4f37b9aeaa5151d790` with exactly three accepted behavioral deltas.
[x] Focused ED2 and grid-origin regressions pass; formatting, diff checks, Rio tests, low-memory build, and artifact identity checks pass.
[x] Fresh-session maintainer dogfood accepts Kitty redraws, transparency, typography/line height, balanced grid geometry, resize/fullscreen, input, quit prompt, and shutdown.
[x] Split Yazelix cursors are explicitly rejected as insufficient value for the fork cost; upstream Rio solid cursor/trail behavior is accepted.
[x] No Nova cutover, normal profile/desktop mutation, publication, PR, repository rewrite, or channel promotion occurred.
[x] Publication and Nova cutover/removal are transferred to two dependency-ordered implementation beads.
notes:
2026-08-21 candidate prepared on Linux 7.0.11-76070011-generic x86_64 from Nova edge revision 446d2e25db8a43dac8f30dc21d1e4519cb5c9526. Exact upstream Rio revision b2e7c38bdc56bb86b346ca4f37b9aeaa5151d790 built as /nix/store/m2a08rkffm4w2z139xgqccfy948fa5k4-rio and identified as rioterm 0.5.20. Current .#yazelix-no-mars built as /nix/store/936k8b7yr7pllmi1s5dl9zix4wfpbp7x-yazelix-no-mars and identified as Yazelix Nova (1.1.0). Its 626-path closure contained zero actual Mars or Rio package paths. `yzx enter --version` reached Zellij 0.45.0 under a PTY. Rio help exposed native `--app-id` and `-e/--command`.

Initial delivery proof was too narrow: desktop-file validation passed, but maintainer dogfood reported no window. Direct reproduction exited 134 at `vkCreateInstance` with `ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_DRIVER`; both the candidate and the separately installed upstream Rio binary failed bare because their Nix Vulkan loader could not discover a compatible host driver. The existing local `rio-desktop` wrapper identified the accepted mechanism: pinned Mesa ICD discovery. The minimum candidate correction pins /nix/store/bfkyl4qgipm1vpfls2cqr3kv0afgpbya-mesa-26.1.1 through /home/lucca/.local/share/yazelix-rio-candidate/mesa and sets only `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` to its Intel manifest in the desktop Exec. A probe with only that variable opened and exited 0 after its child completed. The exact corrected desktop command running `yzx enter` then stayed alive for the full eight-second verification window with no stderr and was stopped by timeout; no candidate Rio or yzx process remained. The desktop file validates and the desktop database was refreshed.

No Nova source, package, profile, or channel changed. The candidate remains isolated under app ID `yzx-rio-candidate`; Rio, Nova, and Mesa are GC-rooted under /home/lucca/.local/share/yazelix-rio-candidate. The agent launched only bounded verification instances after the maintainer reported the failed dogfood launch. Mars clears direct Kitty placements only for ClearMode::All while preserving partial clears, saved scrollback, virtual placement state, and image data. The exact upstream candidate still lacks that clear and b542e96 is not its ancestor. Historical Yazi issue 1786 assigns persistent/overlapping images to Rio; Rio issue 1530 and PR 1736 fixed a separate missing c/r virtual-placement sizing defect, so their closure does not cover this Zellij host-redraw boundary. Four targeted current Rio issue searches found no matching ED2-placement issue. Candidate remains active and unpromoted; do not remove Mars based on this revision. The smallest next candidate is exact upstream Rio plus only the b542e96 behavior/test, with split Yazelix cursor support still eligible for deletion. Agent-created rio-image-repro session was removed; maintainer adept-triceratops session was untouched.

The literal Mars b542e96 port therefore overreached by clearing placements on main-screen ED2, where `grid.clear_viewport()` intentionally moves content into history. The Zellij reproduction is the alternate-screen branch, which resets the grid without history. Test was strengthened first and failed against the broad port because the main placement disappeared; handler cleanup was moved inside the `Mode::ALT_SCREEN` branch. The revised test proves partial and saved clears preserve the placement, main-screen ED2 preserves and dirties it, alternate-screen ED2 clears and dirties it, and swapping back restores the untouched main-screen placement. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`, and `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test -p rio-vt kitty_placements_clear_only_on_alt_screen_full_erase -- --nocapture` passed (1 passed, 464 filtered; inherited teletypewriter warning only). The same single test now drives CSI ?1049h, CSI 2J, and CSI ?1049l through Processor; no production code or additional test was added. Local Zellij source confirms those exact host sequences. cargo fmt --all -- --check, git diff --check, and CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test -p rio-vt kitty_placements_clear_only_on_alt_screen_full_erase -- --nocapture passed (1 passed, 464 filtered; inherited teletypewriter warning only). No artifact build or GUI ran.

2026-08-21 patched dogfood artifact delivered. Nix derivation /nix/store/12k0f1arjr665d61jzasrlyfbvb8s8z4-rio.drv built source /nix/store/mnkb24z68bn9xi81ndsn17jdfb0isdpa-source into /nix/store/l5fb4si1bk0v2yp5vcf9jf0barl2hxmk-rio. The derivation records CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1, release LTO=false, codegen-units=16, debug=0, and split-debuginfo=off; release linking peaked at approximately 770 MiB rustc RSS. The package build and its full default test/doc-test phase passed with only the inherited rio-window and teletypewriter warnings. The realized source was inspected and contains the alternate-screen-only Kitty placement clear. The artifact identifies as rioterm 0.5.20 and is pinned at /home/lucca/.local/share/yazelix-rio-candidate/rio-ed2. The validated desktop entry /home/lucca/.local/share/applications/yzx-rio-candidate.desktop now appears as Yazelix Nova (Rio ED2 Candidate) and invokes the patched root with app ID yzx-rio-candidate, the exact pinned Yazelix Nova 1.1.0 no-Mars package, and the previously proven Mesa ICD. The desktop database was refreshed. No GUI was launched; fresh-session maintainer dogfood is the remaining acceptance gate.

2026-08-22 maintainer fresh-session dogfood passed on Yazelix Nova (Rio ED2 Candidate). The previously reproduced Yazi full-width-to-half-width Enter transition no longer leaves the old Kitty placement behind; the patched candidate is working in the real interaction path. This accepts the delivered candidate behavior only. The issue remains active and no Nova cutover, Mars removal, commit, PR, profile update, channel promotion, or stable change has occurred.

title: Refresh Nova README and website for the next Edge publication
description:
Refresh the canonical Nova README and current nova.yazelix.com product documentation only when the exact Edge candidate is being published. The publication pass must explain the unified `~/.config/yazelix/` tree as a product benefit and synchronize the website with the shipped Rio, startup picker, Forest, Radar, popup, package, and keybinding behavior. Until that publication gate, keep the current Edge implementation as the source of truth and do not make piecemeal website edits against a moving candidate.

Consumer: users evaluating or configuring the published Edge experience. Trigger: the maintainer selects an exact Edge revision for publication. Observable result: the README and current website describe that same revision without stale Mars, cursor, tiled-Yazi-sidebar, or keybinding claims. Failure behavior: if the candidate changes materially during the documentation pass, stop and rebase the documentation inventory on the newly selected revision before publishing.
design:
Use the accepted Edge revision and its `README.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/installation.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, defaults, and generated key contracts as the only current-state sources. Update the README first, then keep nova.yazelix.com downstream and record the exact Nova revision it describes.

Current website surfaces known to need reconciliation include `src/content/docs/start.md`, `src/content/docs/keybindings.md`, `src/content/docs/configure.md`, `src/content/docs/docs/runtime-model.md`, `src/content/docs/docs/customization-surfaces.md`, and `src/content/docs/docs/nova-and-zellij.md`, plus current homepage copy and smoke assertions that encode those claims. Replace Mars/`no-mars` with Rio/`no-rio`; replace the old persistent tiled Yazi sidebar model with the one-use startup Yazi picker, persistent Yazi popup, Forest editor tree, and Radar Zellij sidebar; describe the current shortcuts (`Ctrl y`, `Alt Shift A`, `Alt Shift H`, `Ctrl Alt n/p`, `Ctrl Tab`, and `Ctrl Shift Tab`) and current package names.

Present the unified config tree without stealing native ownership: `yzx config` is the normal entry point; root settings are sparse user intent; Rio, Zellij, Helix, Yazi, Nushell, and Starship keep their native schemas; generated `YAZELIX_STATE_DIR` output is not user configuration. Remove obsolete active cursor and Mars paths. Do not rewrite the historical Nova v1 article, its archived media notes, or other explicitly historical material merely because it accurately names the v1 stack. Do not document Nix-free installation or Omarchy integration before those artifacts exist.
acceptance_criteria:
- Work begins only after the maintainer selects the exact Edge revision being published; the website records that revision and the documentation pass restarts if the candidate materially changes.
- `README.md` plainly explains the benefit of gathering important Nova and component-native configuration under `~/.config/yazelix/`, names `yzx config` as the normal entry point, and documents `YAZELIX_CONFIG_HOME`, sparse overrides, packaged defaults, native-schema ownership, and generated `YAZELIX_STATE_DIR` separately.
- Current website installation and package copy says Rio and `no-rio`, not Mars or `no-mars`.
- Current workspace documentation explains the focused one-use startup Yazi picker, persistent Yazi popup, Forest inside managed Helix, and collapsible Radar pane without calling Forest or Radar the old Yazi sidebar.
- Current keybinding documentation matches the published candidate: `Ctrl y` toggles Forest/editor focus, `Alt Shift A` opens Anima, `Alt Shift H` toggles Radar, `Ctrl Alt n/p` cycles attention tabs, and `Ctrl Tab` / `Ctrl Shift Tab` cycle Radar sessions.
- Current configuration inventories contain no active cursor or Mars paths and accurately name the important Rio, Zellij, Helix, Yazi, Nushell, and Starship files under the unified root.
- Current Nova/Zellij ownership documentation names Radar and the pane orchestrator correctly and does not attribute popup, navigation, or session policy to the wrong component.
- Historical v1 article/media material remains historically accurate and is not silently rewritten as current product documentation.
- Nix-free installation and Omarchy remain absent from user-facing current-state docs until their implementation beads produce released artifacts.
- README links pass, the website check/build succeeds, and focused smoke tests assert the corrected package, navigation, keybinding, and configuration claims.
notes: Scheduling decision approved 2026-08-31: defer this documentation work and execute it as one synchronization pass when Edge is published. Do not spend maintenance effort keeping the website synchronized with intermediate Edge revisions. No publication dependency issue currently exists, so the explicit maintainer-selected Edge revision is the activation gate. The repository README/CHANGELOG/architecture already cover the current Forest and Radar runtime sufficiently; the material drift is primarily in the public website and the missing short unified-config product explanation.

title: Keep the tab workspace stable across Yazi opens and agent toggles
description:
## Why

Opening a file or directory through the managed Yazi bridge can currently change the effective workspace based on the target path or the focused pane. That is too unstable for a tab-level workspace contract and can cause the hidden agent to be treated as stale even when the user only navigated within the same project.

The reported ignored-file path `/home/lucca/pjs/science/tree-seg-unsuper/docs/text/personal_files/transcription.md` is a useful regression case. Direct Git lookup and the installed `yzx-open` resolve the parent worktree correctly, but live inspection showed Yazi at `.../personal_files` while Helix and the agent remained at the worktree root. Popup fallback then selected the focused Yazi pane cwd. The core defect is therefore divergent workspace ownership and focus-derived fallback, not ignored-file Git discovery alone.

Target-derived retargeting is also harmful outside that example: an ordinary open can enter a nested repository/submodule, and every non-Git file or directory currently promotes its own parent/path as the workspace.

## Existing source of truth

The locked pane-orchestrator child already owns versioned per-tab workspace state through `workspace_state_by_tab`, including bootstrap versus explicit provenance, `get_active_tab_session_state`, `retarget_workspace`, and `open_workspace_terminal`. The bar and screen consume that state. `yzx-open` currently bypasses it, while popup fallback and the agent derive cwd elsewhere.

Keep the pane orchestrator as the sole canonical owner. Main-repo `yzx-open` owns operation intent and sequencing: requested targets, ordinary open versus explicit retarget, Git/non-Git root policy, Helix bridge calls, and rollback/error reporting. It does not own another workspace-state map. Yazi cwd and ordinary pane cwd remain local navigation state.

The existing Helix fork bridge already exposes the required editor-local vocabulary: `helix.get_context`, `helix.set_cwd`, `helix.open_directory`, and `helix.open_files`. Reuse those actions. Avoid expanding the Helix fork; a new action, schema field, or editor-side policy is justified only by a focused failing contract showing that the current bridge cannot satisfy the user-visible behavior and that solving it outside Helix would require unsafe terminal keystrokes or duplicate editor state.

## User-visible contract

- Each managed tab has one canonical workspace root owned by the pane orchestrator.
- Before an explicit root exists, the first managed open promotes bootstrap state to an explicit root: the containing Git worktree when present, otherwise the opened directory or the file's parent.
- Once explicit, an ordinary file or directory open preserves that root, including ignored files, nested repositories/submodules, and non-Git descendants. The requested absolute file or directory still reaches Helix/picker behavior unchanged.
- An explicit workspace-retarget action is the only managed operation that changes the root. The current Yazi `Alt z` path must use this internal primitive until its separate tab-level picker bead replaces the UX.
- A successful retarget updates canonical state and the managed editor cwd as one operation. A failed or cancelled retarget leaves both unchanged.
- The hidden agent is requested with the canonical root. It survives navigation, pane focus changes, ordinary opens, and local editor cwd drift; it restarts only after a real canonical-root change.
- Raw Helix `:cd`, shell `cd`, and Yazi navigation may drift locally and do not redefine the tab workspace. The next managed open resynchronizes Helix to the canonical root without moving existing shells. A successful request originating in managed Yazi may still move that Yazi locally to the opened directory or file parent; this never changes the canonical root.
- On orchestrator restart, a pre-existing managed editor cwd may be used once as recovery evidence only when no explicit workspace state exists. It cannot continuously override explicit orchestrator state.
- Popup actions use the canonical root for workspace-scoped operations and an explicitly supplied request cwd for target-local operations. Focused-pane cwd is never a silent workspace fallback.

## Scope

- Route live bridge opens through the orchestrator's current per-tab session state and retarget action.
- Distinguish ordinary open from explicit retarget in the smallest request contract that cannot be confused by target type or focus.
- Promote bootstrap state exactly once and publish it to existing consumers.
- Route agent launch/staleness through orchestrator state rather than editor title, focused pane, or popup fallback.
- Make popup cwd choice request-specific: canonical workspace for workspace actions, explicit target cwd for target actions.
- Preserve requested absolute targets and clear errors for missing, unreadable, or rejected paths.
- Add focused regression coverage and enough diagnostics to identify tab id, root provenance, requested target, operation kind, and agent restart reason without creating another state store.
- Change the pane-orchestrator child only for canonical state/read-mutation primitives that belong to it, and the popup child only for generic explicit-request-cwd and hidden-reuse correctness if required. Neither child owns Git discovery, Yazelix workspace policy, or editor sequencing.
- Keep root policy, request coordination, Yazi integration, generated keymaps/layouts, packaging, documentation, and end-to-end checks in the main repo.
- Reuse the existing Helix bridge without changing the Helix fork unless a focused failing contract proves a missing editor-local primitive.
- Publish any required child commit before updating main-repo lock/release references, changelog, README LOC scorecard, and packaged runtime.

## Out of scope

- The speculative tab-level zoxide picker, editor-free retarget command, and `Alt m` pane policy are separate beads.
- The local managed-Yazi target-follow implementation is tracked separately; this foundation only guarantees that such navigation cannot retarget the tab workspace or restart the agent.
- General popup-framework redesign, layout expansion, Home Manager scope, or legacy compatibility.
- Automatically promoting arbitrary Helix `:cd` or pane cwd drift into workspace state.
- Replacing Helix or adding a second workspace owner.

## Implementation notes

- Main-repo `yzx-open` is the operation coordinator. Query current tab session state before deciding whether an open bootstraps, preserves, or explicitly retargets.
- Keep orchestrator mutation and existing Helix bridge calls transactional from the caller's perspective; if editor coordination fails, retain or restore the previous canonical root and return a clear error.
- Keep the orchestrator API state-oriented. Do not make it resolve Git roots or send `:cd`/`:open` text into Helix.
- If the popup child changes, keep the capability generic: compare hidden popup state with the caller's effective requested cwd. Workspace and agent policy remain outside the popup plugin.
- Derive tab/workspace labels from the canonical state already published by the orchestrator.
- The agent toggle must compare its stored launch root with canonical orchestrator state, not whichever pane is focused when the popup request arrives.
- Recovery precedence is explicit orchestrator state, then one-time managed-editor evidence, then existing bootstrap/default behavior.
- Prefer one contract-level test matrix over mirror tests for each literal/config value.

## Rejected alternatives

- Remove agent reset on cwd change: reduces visible harm but permits an agent from the old workspace to masquerade as current.
- Retarget on every target: makes file opening unexpectedly redefine the tab, especially in non-Git trees and nested repositories.
- Treat Helix cwd as the continuous source of truth: raw editor drift would silently restart agents and move other workspace-bound actions.
- Treat focused pane or Yazi cwd as canonical: navigation and focus become global state mutations.
- Freeze the initial root forever: prevents deliberate workspace switching and future tab-level picker workflows.
- Move workspace coordination into the Helix fork: increases fork delta, makes editor-local cwd a product owner, and couples non-editor workflows to Helix.

## Maintenance notes

P0 beta blocker, large integration slice. The bug spans main-repo coordination, the pane-orchestrator child, popup cwd semantics, the existing Helix bridge, and agent lifecycle. The desired result is fewer owners and no Helix fork expansion unless the current bridge is demonstrably insufficient.
acceptance_criteria:
- A normal Git worktree, the ignored `docs/text/personal_files/transcription.md` path, a nested repository/submodule, and a non-Git tree are covered for nested file and directory targets.
- With an explicit workspace, every ordinary live-bridge open preserves the orchestrator root while retaining the requested absolute file path or picker root.
- With no live editor, the first open establishes and publishes the correct Git or non-Git root and launches the editor with that cwd.
- Explicit retarget changes both orchestrator state and Helix cwd; ordinary open inside a nested repository does not.
- With Yazi focused and navigated below the workspace, toggling the hidden agent immediately before or after an ordinary open reveals the same PID at the canonical root.
- After an explicit retarget, the next agent reveal replaces the stale PID and launches at the new canonical root.
- A drift matrix with orchestrator=/repo, Helix=/repo/docs, Yazi=/repo/docs/text, and agent=/repo proves that a Yazi-originated open of `/repo/docs/text/personal_files/transcription.md` preserves the canonical root and agent PID while allowing the separate target-follow behavior to move Yazi locally to `/repo/docs/text/personal_files`.
- Orchestrator restart recovery may adopt a pre-existing managed editor cwd only when explicit workspace state is absent; later editor drift cannot overwrite explicit state.
- Orchestrator session state, Helix bridge context, workspace terminal cwd, and tab/workspace label agree after bootstrap and retarget.
- The current Yazi Alt-z path still performs a deliberate retarget through the new primitive pending its separate tab-level UX bead.
- The existing Helix bridge actions satisfy the contract without Helix fork source changes. If a focused failing test proves that impossible, the bead records the evidence, rejected main/orchestrator alternatives, and the smallest editor-local fork delta before implementation.
- Focused Rust/child checks, child WASI/Nix builds only for changed children, `nix flake check`, `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs`, and a temporary-profile install pass succeed.
notes: Live acceptance on 2026-07-15 used a disposable installed-runtime session. Bootstrap promoted the repo root, an ordinary nested-file bridge open resynchronized a deliberately drifted Helix cwd, and the hidden agent retained pane 1 / PID 2592505. Retargeting to yazelix-zellij-popup changed orchestrator and Helix roots, then replaced the stale agent with pane 3 / PID 2597519 at the new root. Direct MessageToPlugin URL/alias routing was rejected after dogfooding showed that Zellij's caller configuration could resolve a different plugin instance; the orchestrator instead finds the loaded yzpp instance in its existing pane manifest and messages its plugin ID.
close_reason: Completed and live-dogfooded

title: Track the published Mars config inventory
description:
## Purpose

Mirror Mars bead yzt-ehg, which owns the complete versioned public Mars settings inventory consumed by Yazelix config discovery.

## Published contract

Mars publishes one deterministic schema-versioned JSON catalog at docs/yazelix/config_inventory.v1.json. It covers every public base setting and Linux, macOS, and Windows override; preserves structured shapes; supplies defaults, finite choices, descriptions, and availability constraints; and explicitly excludes internal or derived state. Parser-backed checks prove advertised defaults, choices, unions, and representative structured values. The artifact is consumable from the exact Mars source revision without retaining the Mars runtime.

## Ownership

- Mars owns inventory completeness and native setting semantics.
- Yazelix filters mars.appearance.preset so root appearance.mode remains the only Ratconfig appearance control. Yazelix owns the remaining 15 Overview recommendations plus bounded apply and display policy.
- Ratconfig remains generic.

Do not copy Mars structs, derive completeness from packaged config.toml, scrape documentation, or add a compatibility adapter.

## Handoff

The mirror records the exact published Mars revision and artifact path and changes only the Mars lock node. Consumer bead yazelix-5vl-core-all-config-discovery-lsw.3 owns Ratconfig integration and proceeds from that handoff.

Unsupported structured settings may remain read-only. Current Ratconfig has no dedicated Mars native-file action; direct native editing happens outside Ratconfig unless the maintainer chooses that scope in another bead.
notes:
Owner handoff refreshed after the second fresh-eyes pass. Yazelix pins Mars 129981b3a5b9f0a9ef1fa60d2742845cb1722db3; functional inventory cleanup is 4a011de22c and the reviewed source record is 129981b3a5. Stable artifact: docs/yazelix/config_inventory.v1.json, schema_version 1. The catalog remains 151 unique entries: 133 base settings and 18 platform override groups. Yazelix filters mars.appearance.preset, yielding 150 All rows, 15 Overview recommendations, and 135 All-only rows. The second review marks transparent and buttonless decorations as macOS-only, validates feature constraints in WGPU and non-WGPU builds, and removes the hand-written JSON-to-TOML converter for a net 14-line reduction. Only the Mars lock node changed. Verified nix flake check, nix flake show --all-systems, nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs --print-out-paths -> /nix/store/g1dmjkm7cj09zmlspglgzb8mx4b29nj5-yazelix, temporary profile installation and Yazelix Nova (1.0.0-beta.3) smoke, installed-profile refresh, and git diff --check.

Mars main now points to 17a031c2a1 with test-only simplification 3b1ae0a7db and planning corrections. The inventory artifact and runtime stayed unchanged, so Yazelix keeps the reviewed 129981b3a5 pin and avoids lock churn for owner-side tests and planning text.
close_reason: Mars inventory published and pushed at 144b6d0d6ce447f61f6e491630942b908ff0214a; Yazelix Mars input pinned to that exact revision with only its lock node changed.

title: Package official Yazi flavors and render native Yazi config
description: Provide one Yazi Ratconfig tab that renders the user yazi.toml override against Nova packaged defaults, renders native theme.toml with dynamic dark/light flavor choices, and retains file actions for complex native structures. Package the five flavors physically hosted by yazi-rs/flavors at a Yazi-compatible revision. Ratconfig remains generic; yzx-config owns paths, flavor discovery, Home Manager ownership, validation, and atomic native writes; yzx-yazi-config remains the runtime materializer. Rejected: Classic catalog snapshots, a second semantic theme setting, a static flavor registry, vendoring Yazi internal defaults, random-theme machinery, and a generic create-arbitrary-key form.
acceptance_criteria: Nova packages Catppuccin Latte, Frappé, Macchiato, Mocha, and Dracula from an exact official yazi-rs/flavors revision without preview assets. Ratconfig has one Yazi tab where safe yazi.toml and theme.toml values render from their native files, dark/light flavor rows offer the packaged and user-installed flavors discovered from actual directories, complex structures remain read-only, and every native Yazi file remains openable. Writes preserve comments and unrelated keys, reset removes the user override, Home Manager-owned files are read-only with exact option guidance, and changes apply on the next Yazi launch. Focused Rust contracts, Yazi debug validation, Nix checks, temporary profile installation, documentation, changelog, and LOC scorecard pass.
notes: Fresh-eyes and simplification pass 2026-07-14: fixed two host-composition bugs. The Yazi tab no longer mixes Ratconfig's six-column TOML table with three-column file-action rows; it uses one consistent settings layout. The Advanced tab again uses Ratconfig's reserved advanced identity, restoring hidden diagnostics and status columns. Centralized Yazi source routing/ownership, deduplicated optional text loading, and reduced test scaffolding. Net first pass: 20 fewer Rust lines and 17 fewer tracked lines after the changelog note. A second independent pass rejected an ambiguous flavor package named only .yazi: it previously appeared as an empty picker choice and was accepted as installed. The end-to-end contract covers that boundary; production LOC stayed flat and the regression adds one test line. A third failure-path pass fixed dangling managed file/asset symlinks being silently treated as absent and ensured that write, replacement, or rename errors discard the staged runtime. A fourth boundary pass extended that protection to a dangling managed Yazi root, made the runtime ignore empty .yazi asset names consistently with the picker, and rejected incomplete user flavor overrides before they can replace valid packaged flavors. All failures were reproduced before their fixes and folded into the existing transaction and asset contracts. Rejected a Ratconfig cross-repo header/API change: row-specific source metadata remains a generic Ratconfig limitation, while row ownership, write rejection, and file-action details are correct; revisit only if misleading header metadata proves user-significant. Also rejected an intermediate field-container refactor because rustfmt made it larger without reducing ownership or branching, sharing the tiny symlink-aware existence helper across crates because that would add a dependency for no conceptual reduction, and materializer locking/platform-specific rename because the observed concurrent paths preserve a completed runtime and do not justify a new ownership layer. Fifth fresh-eyes pass reproduced broken runtime symlinks when the materializer received relative config or state paths; all three inputs are now resolved once at the boundary, and the existing asset contract runs on relative paths. Simplification collapsed two competing tab-level Yazi sources into one directory source while preserving exact yazi-config and yazi-theme field routing, so Ratconfig no longer chooses an arbitrary file for the multi-file tab header. Rejected post-processing synthetic empty flavor defaults because it would misstate Yazi's absence-based default and needs a generic Ratconfig reset contract before it can be represented honestly. Sixth fresh-eyes pass reproduced a destructive override alias: when the managed Yazi config was equal to or nested under generated state/yazi, replacement deleted the source config. The materializer now canonicalizes the state root and rejects both lexical and symlink-resolved config overlap before staging; the transaction contract proves the source yazi.toml survives. Kept the guard at the actual replacement boundary rather than banning all nearby config/state layouts or adding a second caller-side policy. Seventh fresh-eyes pass reproduced a descendant alias missed by the root guard: a managed passthrough file or asset symlink resolving into generated state/yazi was staged, then its target was deleted during replacement, leaving broken runtime links. One shared replacement-boundary check now protects the config root and every user-linked file, plugin, and flavor before the old runtime is touched; the transaction test proves the old source survives. Simplification removed test-only embedding and copying of the production Yazi default from yzx-config and its Nix source preparation; representative TOML remains in the focused test while the flake integration checks continue to exercise the actual packaged default. Rejected scanning and canonicalizing every managed input up front because copied TOML and Lua inputs are safe after staging, and duplicate traversal would add policy and change errors. Eighth fresh-eyes pass reproduced a semantic repair failure: native theme.toml with a numeric or boolean flavor value rendered that row as a free-form non-string editor instead of the installed-flavor picker. The Yazi owner now keeps dark and light rows typed as string choices while Ratconfig still owns dotted-path patchability; the end-to-end test starts from dark = 42 and repairs it to an installed custom flavor without losing comments or unrelated keys. Simplification hoisted the two identical yzx-yazi-config derivations into one private flake helper, removing three Nix lines and one duplicate owner without changing public outputs. Rejected forcing generic StructuredOnly rows editable because non-table parent paths cannot be patched safely, and rejected exposing the materializer through package passthru solely for check reuse because that would create a public surface.
close_reason: Implemented and verified the official five-flavor package, native Ratconfig Yazi tab, dynamic flavor discovery, safe writes/resets, Home Manager ownership, and runtime materialization.

title: Keep Anima navigation controls alive and name its pane anima
description:
Contract — ANIMA-CONTROLS-TITLE-001
Alt Shift A opens the managed popup titled anima. Native animations use h/Left for previous and l/Right for next; repeated navigation keeps the same process and pane alive. q exits successfully and returns focus to the live workspace. Preserve keybindings.screen, the internal screen popup ID, random startup, existing reservations and other-style any-key exit behavior. The separately executed aquarium is outside native browsing.

Ownership and implementation
Anima owns navigation/rendering; Nova owns pane naming and custom-popup validation. Change defaults/zellij/config.kdl to request anima and update its packaged contract check. Reserve anima in the existing custom-popup validator so another popup cannot reuse the managed pane identity; extend its existing semantic regression test. No child-source/pin change, control redesign, style-set change, identifier migration, new dependency, or unrelated popup-lifecycle work.

Evidence

title: Use Ctrl Alt T for Zellij tab mode
description:
## Contract — ZELLIJ-TAB-MODE-CHORD-001

Consumer: a Nova user entering and leaving Zellij tab mode.

Trigger: the user presses Ctrl Alt T outside locked mode, or presses it again while tab mode is active.

Observable result: Ctrl Alt T enters tab mode and the same chord returns to normal mode. Plain Ctrl T is no longer owned by Nova Zellij and remains available to the focused application. The status-bar key hint and Ratconfig key reference reflect the effective chord through their existing keymap sources.

Failure behavior: if Ctrl Alt T conflicts with Rio, Helix, another Nova Zellij binding, or a popup/agent route, stop and resolve the ownership conflict rather than layering an alias.

## Accepted implementation

Nova owns this shared Linux/macOS runtime configuration. The existing native Zellij parser applies a root keybinds unbind across all modes after merging upstream defaults, so one unbind "Ctrl t" removes the inherited chord. The tab and shared_except tab locked blocks bind Ctrl Alt t in both directions. No child fork patch or compatibility alias is needed.

Ratconfig's catalog and the tutor advertise Ctrl Alt t. The native status bar derives its grouped hint from the effective Zellij keymap. The existing packaged contract checks both directions, explicit inherited-key removal, and absence of a Ctrl t binding; the existing parity check covers the catalog and tutor.

The pinned Rio bindings, managed Helix defaults, Zellij modes, popup routes, and Radar routes contain no conflicting Ctrl Alt t assignment. Radar does not subscribe to key input. The locked-mode boundary and tab actions are unchanged.

## Scope

Replace the tab-mode entry and exit chord with Ctrl Alt T. Do not retain Ctrl T as a compatibility alias. Update the smallest existing contract and user-facing keymap documentation or generated reference needed to keep the packaged key inventory truthful. Do not change tab-mode actions, tab creation, Radar session cycling, popup chords, or unrelated mode keys.

## Acceptance criteria

- Packaged config enters tab mode with Ctrl Alt T and leaves it with Ctrl Alt T.
- Plain Ctrl T is absent from Nova-owned Zellij bindings.
- A conflict audit covers Nova Rio, managed Helix, Zellij modes, popup routes, and Radar chords.
- The packaged key contract, Ratconfig key-reference parity, and visible status hint agree.
- CHANGELOG and the README LOC scorecard are updated if implementation changes tracked project files.
- git diff --check, focused contracts, nix flake check, nix flake show --all-systems, and nix build .#yazelix pass for the candidate. Because this is shared runtime configuration, exact-revision Linux CI and Darwin Package Smoke are required before acceptance or promotion.
- Fresh-session dogfood proves the chord in both directions and confirms Ctrl T reaches the focused application.
notes:
Implemented and manually dogfooded; acceptance remains pending exact-revision Linux CI and Darwin Package Smoke. No promotion.

Linux proof: the new contract failed on the previous config (missing Ctrl t unbind), then passed with the fix. nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.contracts .#checks.x86_64-linux.key_reference_parity, nix flake show --all-systems, and nix build .#yazelix .#yazelix-edge pass. Full nix flake check and git diff --check pass. The committed revision produces the same verified store paths; README and development scorecards count 27,710 tracked lines (+15).

Isolated nix profile add --refresh .#yazelix installed /nix/store/fhlwbjjbb6m5xsdbw2f8ry4vala96jbq-yazelix; yzx --version reports Yazelix Nova (1.2.0). A newly started scripted PTY using that installed launcher proves Ctrl Alt T enters Tab from Normal and Pane, the same chord returns to Normal, n creates a tab only in Tab mode, and plain Ctrl T reaches a raw focused application before and after toggling. Captured native status output shows TAB in the Ctrl-Alt group in both modes. Proof files: /tmp/nova-fuvy-delivery/{session.py,proof.log,session.pty,keys.bin,tab-mode-hint.txt,normal-mode-hint.txt}; build/check logs /tmp/nova-fuvy-*. This is scripted Linux terminal evidence, not manual Rio GUI dogfood or Darwin proof.

Candidate: a3e484a31e526e0dc4bcd143a9872a21fa119636, pushed to origin/edge. The default yazelix-edge profile is pinned to this GitHub revision and /nix/store/ibszcr342kmqw34m97qwh64g2nlp68bi-yazelix. The local yazelix-nova-dogfood profile is pinned to this revision and the isolated-test artifact above. Both installed commands report 1.2.0.

Required hosted checks are running on this exact candidate: Linux CI https://github.com/Yazelix/nova/actions/runs/33934893354 and Darwin Package Smoke https://github.com/Yazelix/nova/actions/runs/33934902044. User confirmed "it works" in response to the requested fresh-session check after installation: Ctrl Alt T enters and leaves tab mode, and Ctrl T remains available to the focused application. Manual dogfood is satisfied; await both hosted checks before closing this bead or accepting/promoting the candidate. Main and stable remain unchanged.

title: Publish the Nova v1 article on Reddit
description:
## Why

The published Nova v1 article has not yet been introduced to a relevant Reddit community. Reddit can reach Nix and terminal-workflow users, but a useful maintainer-authored self-post must fit one community and its current rules rather than read like duplicated promotion.

## Evidence

- `../nova-site/drafts/yazelix-nova-v1.md:2-12` owns the published title, description, release identity, source revision, and preview asset.
- `../nova-site/drafts/yazelix-nova-v1.md:15-55` supplies the honest maintainer perspective and invites criticism and discussion.
- `../nova-site/drafts/yazelix-nova-v1.md:53-90` explains the Nix-packaged terminal workspace and gives concrete commands and keyboard workflow.
- Canonical article URL: `https://nova.yazelix.com/blog/yazelix-nova-v1/`.

## User-visible contract

Consumer: members of one explicitly approved, relevant Reddit community.

Trigger: Lucca approves the subreddit, final title/body, account, and publication.

Observable result: one community-appropriate Reddit post clearly identifies the author as the Nova maintainer, explains why the project may be useful, links the canonical article, and invites substantive feedback without link-spam behavior.

Important failure behavior: do not publish, cross-post, or contact moderators without explicit approval in the implementation run. If subreddit rules reject the intended format, return with the rule and an adapted draft rather than evading moderation.

## Scope

In scope:
- Re-read the live article immediately before drafting.
- Propose one primary subreddit based on audience fit, then inspect its current rules and recent accepted project posts.
- Draft a platform-native title and concise self-post in Lucca voice; disclose the maintainer relationship and include concrete Nova context before the canonical article link.
- Distinguish the historical v1 article source revision from current ongoing development where needed.
- Present the exact subreddit, account, title, body, flair, and media or link format to Lucca for approval.
- After approved publication, record the permalink and publication time in this Bead.

Out of scope:
- No multi-subreddit blast, automatic cross-posting, vote solicitation, paid promotion, moderator outreach, article rewrite, or engagement campaign.
- Do not copy the full article into Reddit or promise current behavior unsupported by the published source record.

## Verification

- The selected subreddit currently permits the approved project-post format and required flair or disclosure is present.
- The canonical article URL is exact and reachable, and all technical claims are supported by the article source record.
- Lucca approves the exact community and final submission before the external write.
- The published permalink is publicly reachable and recorded in the Bead.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if no suitable subreddit accepts the intended format or the community choice remains unapproved.
- Stop if the live article has materially drifted from its cited source or a claim cannot be supported.
- Stop before cross-posting, moderator contact, or account-level automation.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort: S. Risk: MED because subreddit culture and moderation rules materially affect reception. The X post is independent; neither issue blocks the other.

title: Design a Ghostty appearance tab and root-mode adapter
description:
## Why

A future Ratconfig Ghostty tab should follow the same backend-neutral Yazelix appearance rather than introducing another master toggle or making Mars the control plane. Ghostty configuration is user-owned, has Linux/macOS path and Home Manager boundaries, and already overlaps the optional-include/consent work planned for Yazelix cursor integration.

## Evidence

- Current official Ghostty docs support `theme = dark:<name>,light:<name>`, automatic system switching, `window-theme` values including light/dark/system/auto, runtime config reload, optional config-file includes, and light/dark notifications for terminal applications.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md:38` currently keeps Ghostty packaging out of this repository.
- Existing bead `yazelix-7fh-7mh` owns explicit consent and one optional Yazelix include in the real user Ghostty config for cursor generation.
- Root appearance epic `yazelix-5vl-0eg` establishes one desired product mode and backend-owned adapters.

## Decision contract

Design, but do not implement, the smallest Ghostty tab that can expose safe high-value native fields, separate dark/light theme names, and the mapping from root appearance to Ghostty without a second persisted active mode. Decide whether to reuse the cursor bead optional include and consent flow, how live reload works, which user/Home Manager-owned paths are supported on Linux and macOS, and what happens when `yzx enter` detects Ghostty without consent.

## Scope

In scope:
- Verify exact behavior against the installed/current official Ghostty version and documentation.
- Define field inventory ownership, theme discovery, root-mode projection, reload, diagnostics, consent, Home Manager, and unmanaged-host behavior.
- Reuse one safe Ghostty include/insertion owner with `yazelix-7fh-7mh` if both features proceed.
- Produce separate implementation beads only for maintainer-approved surfaces.

Out of scope:
- No Ghostty packaging, pinning, launching, broad config mirror, daemon, watcher, whole-file rewrite, or automatic consent.
- Do not add Ghostty-specific logic to Ratconfig itself.
- Do not make this block the initial Mars/Zellij contrast fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The decision records official supported syntax and reload behavior for the selected minimum version.
- The ownership matrix covers writable user config, Home Manager/store-backed config, absent config, macOS/XDG paths, consent declined, and conflicting existing include.
- The proposed tab contains only fields with safe parsing, validation, persistence, and truthful apply timing.
- Root mode remains the only Yazelix-persisted active appearance.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if safe integration requires rewriting arbitrary Ghostty configuration.
- Stop if cursor and appearance work would create two include patchers or consent flows.
- Stop before adding a Ghostty package/runtime dependency.
- Stop if live reload cannot be requested through a documented owner route.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort S decision, future implementation likely M. Related: `yazelix-7fh-7mh` and `yazelix-5vl-0eg`. Official references: https://ghostty.org/docs/features/theme and https://ghostty.org/docs/config.

title: Allow one custom command in Nova's sidebar slot
description:
## Contract — SIDEBAR-PROVIDER-001

Consumer: a Nova user starting a new session.

Trigger: `sidebar.command` is `radar` (the default) or one executable available to the installed Nova runtime, with optional `sidebar.args`. Nova exposes its managed Yazi wrapper explicitly as `yzx-yazi`.

Observable result: Radar preserves today’s behavior by default. A custom command occupies the same Zellij pane named `sidebar` in every managed tab and inherits Nova’s existing side, width, frame, open/collapsed layouts, focus navigation, toggle behavior, and popup margins. Arguments are passed as argv without a shell. `sidebar.command = "yzx-yazi"` launches the Yazelix-managed Yazi runtime without requiring a store path or separately installed Yazi. Selection is captured at session startup; changing it affects the next session.

Failure behavior: empty or whitespace-containing commands, non-string arguments, and arguments paired with `radar` are rejected. A missing or short-lived custom executable may fail visibly inside its pane but does not prevent the rest of the session from starting. Nova does not offer or diagnose Radar hooks, seed Radar permissions, or install Radar-only key routes for a custom provider. Existing user-installed external hooks remain user-owned.
design: The existing ownership boundary survives: yzx-config validates sidebar.command/sidebar.args and renders one KDL pane suffix; yzx reads that rendered value and substitutes it into both the base and tiled swap-layout templates. The installed Nova package exposes the already-built managed Yazi wrapper as `yzx-yazi`; no provider aliasing, PATH fallback, shell parsing, or store path enters user configuration. The orchestrator continues to target only the pane name `sidebar`, so it remains provider-neutral. Runtime config generation removes Radar command routes for custom providers, permission seeding omits Radar, and agent/doctor onboarding consumes one session environment flag. No live switching, provider registry, width setting, shell command string, or automatic restart.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Default config materializes the existing Radar plugin pane in startup, new-tab, open, and collapsed layouts. 2. The installed Nova package exposes an executable `bin/yzx-yazi`; configuring `sidebar.command = "yzx-yazi"` launches Nova’s managed Yazi without an absolute store path or separate Yazi install. 3. A custom command and escaped string arguments materialize as a terminal `sidebar` pane in all four positions without shell evaluation. 4. Invalid command/argument combinations fail config validation before layout launch. 5. Custom-provider runtime config has no Radar MessagePlugin key routes; Radar remains packaged and unchanged for the default. 6. Custom-provider sessions omit the Radar permission grant and skip Nova’s Codex Radar prompt and doctor diagnostics. 7. Sidebar toggling, dimensions, framing, focus movement, popup geometry, startup picker, and no-Helix packages retain their existing contracts. 8. README, configuration docs, runtime notes, changelog, doctor output, contract checks, and LOC scorecard describe the accepted behavior. 9. Rust formatting/tests, Nova flake checks, package build, and fresh-session dogfood pass before pushing Edge. Linux CI and Darwin Package Smoke must pass on that exact pushed revision before accepting the candidate.
notes:
Implemented SIDEBAR-PROVIDER-001: Radar remains the default; one custom direct-argv command shares the existing sidebar pane, layouts, focus, and popup margins. The public yzx-yazi command resolves to the managed wrapper. Custom providers omit Radar routes, permission seeding, onboarding, and doctor diagnostics. Documentation and the LOC scorecard describe this accepted behavior.

Published child inputs, locked together:
- Nova Zellij 796a30c44c8c4369021e7bb91e2b6c62cfc257de supplies ApplyTiledSwapLayout.
- Pane orchestrator b154a41f1234b3354c905f2bd18898cb632851fd uses exact named layouts instead of the sleeping multi-step swap sequencer.
- Popup f9424823b01e5223dadff9e6c5b87c0131a902f8 supports conditional left_margin and reflows visible popups with sidebar visibility.

Material negative evidence: the newer controller silently does nothing on a host without ApplyTiledSwapLayout. Old popup b07e7c4 rejects Nova's left_margin configuration and returns invalid_config for every popup. A partial override refresh therefore does not prove a coherent runtime; publish and lock all required children together. Compact inline generated plugin KDL is rejected by Zellij, so its multiline form remains. Literal-sidebar-only hiding (no work pane) is not a new accepted contract.

Verification, x86_64-linux, 2026-09-04:
- Child cargo fmt --all -- --check and cargo test --locked: 73 controller tests and 36 popup tests pass.
- nix flake check --no-write-lock-file, nix flake show --all-systems --no-write-lock-file, and nix build .#yazelix --no-write-lock-file --no-link --print-out-paths --print-build-logs pass without local overrides. Includes no_helix_contracts and no_rio_contracts. Logs: /tmp/nova-edge-pinned-{check,show,build}.log.
- nix profile add --refresh .#yazelix --profile /tmp/nova-edge-delivery.5yVBWr/profile installs /nix/store/8b9gbzad4i62mdv36ap6z3dazsfgmp3j-yazelix. The user dogfood profile was upgraded without overrides to the same package; its desktop entry already targets that profile.
- Pinned popup and controller WASM bytes match the manually dogfooded local versions (SHA-256 6e33dc0a186b3a7d4e3ddf55e6a0c6bf58905923ca1d70ef55116dadf01d8d96 and b7a4f02e61e3d9813cf7dcac4f06d9485423a41bd0bec68d648d738618aa0d05).
- Fresh isolated installed session nova-edge-pinned-20260904, 185x41 PTY: startup picker remains beside the sidebar; actual Alt Shift K opens config; actual Alt Shift H closes and restores the sidebar while the same focused popup changes x/width 33/151 to 1/183 and back; hiding and restoring config preserves its pane ID. Test session was removed; user sessions were not changed.
- Earlier isolated complete-candidate PTY checks also exercised menu, Git, Yazi, Anima, and agent shortcuts. The user subsequently confirmed fresh-session popup and Radar navigation behavior working. Scripted geometry checks are not a claim of visual macOS dogfood.

Shared portability boundary: no new Linux-only mechanism; Linux package variants pass and Darwin derivations evaluate. Darwin Package Smoke includes no_rio_contracts in its existing macOS job. Actual Darwin behavior remains unproved until that workflow succeeds.

Edge publication is authorized; main and stable are not. Hosted Linux CI and Darwin Package Smoke on the pushed candidate remain the acceptance gate. Keep this issue active until those results are recorded.

title: Consume scoped diagnostics without mirroring Zellij
description:
## Why

Ratconfig now routes diagnostics by all fields, one source, or one exact field. Yazelix still needs an honest policy for native Zellij sidecars whose schema is larger and faster-moving than the curated settings UI. Mirroring that schema in Yazelix would create a second owner and turn every new native scalar into a host release.

## User-visible contract

Known Yazelix-exposed Zellij fields remain typed and editable. A top-level native leaf node outside the managed and guarded token sets is preserved verbatim, remains visible as an unvalidated native entry, and does not invalidate unrelated fields. Yazelix does not claim that Zellij will accept that opaque entry. Malformed documents, unknown blocks, and integration-owned nodes block writes at source scope. Invalid known fields block only their own field and remain repairable.

## Ownership

- Ratconfig owns generic diagnostic scopes and rendering.
- Yazelix owns the guarded sidecar boundary, curated editable fields, sparse patch/reset behavior, and classification of document shapes it can preserve safely.
- Zellij owns native setting names, types, values, and semantic validation.

## Scope

In scope:
- Consume Ratconfig scoped diagnostics at the exact published revision already pinned for this work.
- Route known invalid values to exact field scope and unsafe document state to Zellij source scope.
- Treat unknown top-level leaf nodes as opaque nonblocking entries and preserve their original text across unrelated saves and resets. Do not interpret their arguments, properties, or values.
- Keep unknown blocks, malformed structure, duplicate/ambiguous known nodes, and integration-owned nodes source-blocking.
- Delete the local default_mode value inventory, its mode-specific parser branch, and the per-value Nix validation loop. default_mode is one regression example, not a special host-owned schema.
- Delete the sidecar only when reset leaves no meaningful native entries.
- Keep the native file action as the escape hatch for structured or unexposed Zellij configuration.
- Update current-state docs, CHANGELOG, and the README LOC scorecard for the resulting behavior.

Out of scope:
- No generic KDL adapter in Ratconfig.
- No complete Zellij schema, scraped catalog, compatibility shim, or Zellij fork change.
- No claim that an opaque entry is semantically valid or applies live.
- Complete Zellij discoverability and Core review remain in yazelix-5vl-core-all-config-discovery-lsw.5.

## Verification

Use a few contract tests: the reported default_mode normal case; a different future-looking leaf form; exact preservation across an unrelated known-field save and reset; a repairable invalid known field; a source blocker; an unknown block; and a second unaffected config source. Then run cargo fmt/check, strict Clippy, yzx-config tests, flake checks, package build, temporary profile install, and git diff --check.

## Stop conditions

Stop if the writer cannot identify and preserve an opaque leaf node without rewriting it. Stop if semantic Zellij validation is duplicated locally. Stop if narrowing diagnostics allows a guarded or structurally unsafe sidecar to be written.

## Rejected alternatives

Rejected: moving Zellij/KDL semantics into Ratconfig; maintaining a complete Yazelix Zellij schema; special-casing default_mode values; validating an enumerated mode list in Nix; treating unknown blocks as safe; and reducing the UI to only a native-file action. The selected boundary preserves the useful picker while keeping native semantics with Zellij.
notes:
Completed against Ratconfig commit f70bbfbc3e021fb3f51fea7399b020bc1ab91c49. Ratconfig owns generic diagnostic routing; Yazelix owns the sparse Zellij sidecar boundary and curated typed fields; Zellij owns the native schema and semantic validity. Unknown top-level leaf nodes outside managed, guarded, and colliding token sets are visible as nonblocking unvalidated diagnostics and remain unchanged across unrelated saves and resets. Invalid known scalar values affect only their exact field and remain repairable. Integration-owned nodes, unknown blocks, malformed structure, duplicate managed nodes, nested-token collisions, and multiple nodes encoded on one line remain source blockers.

The implementation has no default_mode allowlist, native value catalog, per-value Nix validation loop, generic Ratconfig KDL adapter, compatibility shim, or Zellij fork change. Reset removes the sidecar only when no meaningful native entries remain.

Fresh-eyes reviews fixed the handwritten-subset boundaries that could make the sparse writer target the wrong source text. Managed quoted strings no longer truncate at whitespace; quoted braces and comment-like text are not structure; unterminated quotes are source-blocking; quoted booleans and integers are not coerced; and same-line KDL separators or content after block closes are source-blocking. A single trailing semicolon remains supported.

The latest pass checked suspicious shapes with the packaged Zellij 0.44.3 parser. Zellij confirmed that slashdash can comment the next node across a newline, block comments can contain managed-looking lines, an unquoted backslash continues a node, and ui or pane_frames can carry extra arguments or properties. All of those shapes are native-file-only and source-block writes because a physical-line patch cannot preserve their semantics. Zellij also confirmed that managed strings require quotes and decode escapes. Yazelix accepts only quoted, escape-free managed strings; bare or escaped known strings receive exact-field diagnostics and remain repairable without poisoning unrelated settings.

The simplification leaves one lexical scan responsible for line comments, structural comments and continuations, quote balance, braces, semicolons, and safe-leaf classification. The parser no longer rescans ordinary lines after block-close handling. Exact managed block opening is centralized, scalar parsing stays pure with one diagnostic owner, and block state is a fixed depth rather than a collection of repeated names. The final scorecard is 18,970 lines: 131 above the 18,839 mode-specific prototype and 333 above the 18,637 clean baseline shared with the theme slice. This pass adds 50 lines for the confirmed structural boundaries, focused cases, and current-state documentation.

Focused contracts cover custom quoted theme names with spaces and braces, opaque quoted braces and comment-like text, typed repair, exact leaf preservation, source isolation, guarded nodes, duplicates, blocks, nested-token ambiguity, same-line separators, structural KDL comments, continuations, managed-block metadata, and bare or escaped strings. Rejected further deletion: typed scalar parsing is required for Yazelix-owned fields; lexical scanning is required to prove safe preservation; duplicate, collision, separator, comment, continuation, and block-shape guards protect sparse writes. Rejected a generic KDL parser, spawning Zellij for every UI read or write, and parsing multiple nodes per line because they add another semantic owner or runtime dependency; the native file remains the escape hatch for richer KDL.

Verification passed: direct Zellij setup checks for every newly guarded syntax family, cargo fmt check, all 45 yzx-config tests, strict Clippy, git diff check, nix flake check with 43 checks, nix flake show --all-systems, nix build .#yazelix, isolated profile installation, and installed runtime refresh. Live theme switching and reset dogfood remains owned by yazelix-5vl-core-all-config-discovery-lsw.12.
close_reason: Completed scoped diagnostics and hardened the sparse Zellij writer against native multiline and structured KDL forms.

title: Use a human fallback title for the agent pane
description:
## Why

Opening the managed agent popup can expose its full Nix store executable path as the native pane title, for example `/nix/store/...-yzx-agent/bin/yzx-agent`. That is implementation leakage and visually noisy. The stable Yazelix role is simply `agent`.

The current popup deliberately preserves terminal titles because provider spinner titles drive agent activity decorations. The fix must therefore supply a human fallback without pinning the pane title or suppressing meaningful provider updates.

## User-visible contract

When a managed agent pane has no meaningful provider-emitted terminal title, its frame shows `agent`, never a Nix store path or raw launcher command. Provider-emitted titles, including spinner titles, remain visible and continue driving tab activity. This holds for the automatic provider bootstrap and a custom `agent.command`.

## Evidence

- `defaults/zellij/config.kdl:26`: the managed popup has internal `pane_title "agent_popup"` and `preserve_terminal_title true`.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix-zellij-popup/src/main.rs:321`: preserving terminal titles currently renames the new pane to an empty string, allowing the command path to become the initial visible title.
- `runtime/yzx-agent.rs:31`: the automatic launcher execs the first available provider from the managed bootstrap.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator/src/ai_pane_activity_contract.rs:60`: spinner-shaped terminal titles are the activity signal.
- `README.md:122`: the published runtime contract says spinner titles drive compact tab activity without changing native tab names.
- Manual dogfooding on 2026-07-16 showed `/nix/store/...-yzx-agent/bin/yzx-agent` in the pane frame before a useful provider title appeared.

## Ownership

Yazelix owns the product label `agent` and the managed popup configuration. The popup child owns generic launch/title-preservation semantics if a true fallback primitive is required. The pane orchestrator remains the sole activity owner. Prefer an existing Zellij or popup capability; do not add a second activity signal or provider registry.

## Scope

In scope:
- Prove the title lifecycle from popup creation through launcher exec and provider OSC title updates.
- Introduce the smallest single-owner fallback that displays `agent` before or between meaningful provider titles.
- Preserve popup discovery, hide/reopen reuse, custom agent commands, and spinner-driven activity.
- Update the README LOC scorecard and CHANGELOG if project files or user-visible runtime behavior change.
- If the generic popup child must change, publish that owner change and update only the corresponding Yazelix pin.

Out of scope:
- Renaming the internal `agent_popup` identity unless the implementation proves it is user-visible and safe to separate.
- Provider-specific icons, colors, branding, title rewriting, settings, or a general pane-theme system.
- Changing tab names, activity markers, spinner recognition, popup lifecycle, or agent selection order.
- Modifying the Zellij fork when the existing popup/runtime boundary can express the contract.

## Implementation Notes

1. First test whether assigning the configured pane title during launch still permits later terminal OSC title updates.
2. If it does, use the existing popup title path and keep `preserve_terminal_title` behavior intact.
3. If it does not, add the smallest generic fallback-title semantic in the popup owner rather than inserting delays, polling, shell wrappers, or provider-specific title lists.
4. Keep the visible fallback `agent`; semantic provider titles may replace it naturally.
5. Add one focused lifecycle regression covering fallback, spinner replacement, and return to a non-busy title where the owning layer can test it deterministically.

## Verification

- Focused tests for the selected owner should exit 0 and prove fallback-title behavior without suppressing terminal-title updates.
- `cargo test --manifest-path /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix-zellij-popup/Cargo.toml --lib` should exit 0 if the popup child changes.
- `cargo test --manifest-path /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator/Cargo.toml --lib` should exit 0 if the activity boundary changes; avoid changing it unless required.
- `nix flake check` should exit 0.
- `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs` should exit 0.
- `nix profile add --refresh /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix --profile <tmp>` should install successfully.
- Manual dogfooding should show `agent` instead of the store path on initial open, preserve a provider spinner title while busy, clear the tab activity marker when idle, and reuse the hidden pane normally.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the proposed fallback prevents later provider OSC titles from appearing.
- Stop if activity would need polling, focus acknowledgement, timing delays, or a second owner.
- Stop before changing the Zellij fork or building a general title framework; record the missing primitive and request a narrower ownership decision.
- Stop if the fix breaks popup identity matching, hidden-pane reuse, custom commands, or native tab naming.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort: S if existing title semantics suffice; M if the popup child needs one generic fallback primitive. Risk: MED because terminal titles currently carry activity. Confidence: HIGH in the visual defect and user contract, MED in the exact implementation owner until the lifecycle experiment is run.

Rejected alternatives: displaying the provider executable path, permanently pinning `agent` and losing spinner titles, rewriting every provider title, sleeping before emitting OSC escapes, and adding a user-facing title setting for one fixed product role.
notes: Implemented in Yazelix main: yzx-agent emits one OSC 0 fallback title (agent) before exec. Custom agent.command and agent.args are positional launcher argv, so automatic and custom panes share the fallback and stable orchestrator marker. Provider OSC titles remain later in the byte stream and replace it naturally. Popup child and Zellij fork are unchanged; the obsolete custom marker rewrite was deleted. Fresh-eyes simplification removed the unexposed delimiter protocol, unreachable auto-provider argument forwarding, and duplicate custom/provider exec paths (21 Rust LOC). Focused contracts cover fallback -> spinner -> idle ordering, custom argv preservation, and every built-in provider argv. Automated flake/build/profile checks passed; manual initial-title, spinner/activity-clear, and hide/reopen dogfood remains.
close_reason: Completed; manual runtime dogfooding passed
