In scope:
- Sum a curated odd-numbered set of plane waves over aspect-correct normalized coordinates.
- Animate phase, radial scale, or a bounded orientation parameter while preserving coherent symmetry.
- Map amplitude to a truecolor palette with no frame-wide flashing or clipping.
- Add one `quasicrystal` CLI style.

Out of scope:
- No crystallography simulator, 3D diffraction model, arbitrary wave editor, FFT, or shader runtime.
- Do not accept visually redundant presets that differ only by hue.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and the appropriate random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, and resize handling. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Precompute direction vectors and coordinate factors that do not change each frame. Make terminal aspect correction explicit and keep wave count small enough for predictable CPU use.

## Verification

- Tests cover rotational symmetry within tolerance, finite amplitudes, deterministic phase stepping, resize behavior, and palette bounds.
- Visual fixtures show non-periodic structure and smooth motion at narrow, normal, and wide dimensions.
- Run the full child command floor.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if motion aliases into rapid flashing at normal frame cadence.
- Stop if the pattern becomes periodic stripes because too few or incorrectly oriented waves are used.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: blocked by the half-block field renderer. Standard-library trigonometry should be enough.
close_reason: Migrated without contract changes to child-owned epic yzs-mathematical-animation-collection-dou in yazelix-screen; the child repository is the sole active planning owner.

title: Add a Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion animation
description:
## Why

Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion produces moving spots, mitosis-like forms, waves, and coral textures. It adds a recognizable continuous cellular simulation whose behavior is distinct from the discrete Game of Life variants.

## Evidence

- Pearson maps Gray-Scott parameter regimes and patterns in https://arxiv.org/abs/patt-sol/9304003.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/game_of_life.rs` demonstrates grid lifecycle and resizing, while the new field renderer can display continuous concentrations.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement double-buffered A/B concentration fields, a documented Laplacian stencil, bounded timestep, and periodic boundaries.
- Seed deterministic perturbations and curate a small sequence of feed/kill parameter regimes with visibly different behavior.
- Color concentration and gradient without hiding the morphology.
- Add one `gray-scott` CLI style.

Out of scope:
- No PDE framework, GPU compute, arbitrary parameter UI, scientific-accuracy claims, or shared state with Game of Life.
- Do not collapse this into the Turing-pattern implementation.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and the appropriate random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, and resize handling. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Reuse buffers across frames and clamp or otherwise defend concentration bounds after each integration step. Document stencil, timestep, and boundary choices.

## Verification

- Tests cover deterministic seeds, finite bounded concentrations, mass/update invariants appropriate to the chosen discretization, periodic edges, and resize reset.
- Long-run tests catch numerical explosion; visual fixtures identify at least two parameter regimes.
- Run the full child command floor and manually inspect runtime cadence.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the selected timestep becomes unstable over an extended run.
- Stop if all curated regimes converge to blank or uniform fields within normal display duration.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: blocked by the half-block field renderer. Add no numerical crate unless benchmarks demonstrate a concrete need.
close_reason: Migrated without contract changes to child-owned epic yzs-mathematical-animation-collection-dou in yazelix-screen; the child repository is the sole active planning owner.

title: Add a native Matrix rain animation
description:
## Why

Matrix rain is immediately legible, visually strong in a terminal, and can be implemented natively without the external Perl/runtime boundary used by asciiquarium. It also gives `yzs` a typography-driven effect rather than another mathematical field.

## Evidence

- Rusty Rain is a Rust terminal implementation and visual reference at https://github.com/cowboy8625/rusty-rain.
- The `matrix-rain` crate documents a reusable implementation at https://docs.rs/matrix-rain/latest/matrix_rain/, but adopting it is not automatically preferable to a small native module.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/screen_runner.rs` distinguishes native animations from the bounded external asciiquarium process.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement bounded columns with randomized speed, head intensity, glyph mutation, and decaying trails.
- Use only one-column terminal-safe glyphs and deterministic local randomness.
- Clear correctly on resize and termination, and add one `matrix` CLI style.
- Compare local implementation with Rusty Rain and the `matrix-rain` crate for behavior, license, dependencies, and Nix impact before deciding whether to reuse code or a crate.

Out of scope:
- No external process, Perl dependency, font-specific wide glyphs, Katakana correctness claim, or full-screen TUI framework.
- Do not add configuration flags until one curated default proves useful.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and the appropriate random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, and resize handling. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Keep the column model native to the existing frame producer. A dependency is acceptable only if it materially reduces owned code and preserves the lifecycle contract; otherwise implement the small state machine locally.

## Verification

- Tests cover deterministic column evolution, trail decay, one-column glyph widths, resize shrink/grow, and bounded memory.
- Visual checks confirm bright heads, readable trails, varied speeds, and no stale columns after exit.
- Run the full child command floor and verify `yzs matrix` and integrated `yzx screen matrix`.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if an upstream choice introduces its own terminal ownership or event loop.
- Stop if selected glyphs have ambiguous or double width in supported terminals.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: independent of the half-block renderer. Keep this bead ready so it can land while field-renderer work proceeds.
close_reason: Migrated without contract changes to child-owned epic yzs-mathematical-animation-collection-dou in yazelix-screen; the child repository is the sole active planning owner.

title: Rename the Nova repository to luccahuguet/yazelix-nova after v1
description:
## Historical decision

The user once selected `luccahuguet/yazelix-nova` as the post-v1 repository name for Nova. The plan preserved the `yzx` command and Yazelix Nova product name.

## Current boundary

This closed bead records a superseded personal-account rename. It does not authorize a repository rename, replacement repository, remote update, public URL change, installer edit, or runtime change. The active organization migration belongs to `yazelix-5vl-move-nova-stack-to-yazelix-org-pqi`.

## Preserved rationale

An explicit Nova repository name keeps one product from appearing to own the Yazelix umbrella. The current organization plan retains that rationale and changes the target owner.

## GitHub constraints

GitHub documents rename behavior at https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/renaming-a-repository. GitHub redirects repository web and Git traffic, but it does not redirect hosted Actions references or project-site URLs. Reusing the old repository location breaks redirects. A future migration must verify Nix fetchers and flake behavior.

## Historical inventory

The plan required a tracked-file search across Nova, the Yazelix website, child repositories, flakes and locks, Home Manager examples, install commands, badges, workflows, release metadata, Cachix, source links, and local remotes. It kept closed Beads and historical release notes when their coordinates recorded real history.

## Historical execution outline

1. Confirm user approval and target availability.
2. Record repository identity, visibility, default branch, protections, releases, tags, issues, discussions, webhooks, secrets, environments, Pages, and Actions consumers.
3. Prepare owned reference updates without publishing them before the coordinate change.
4. Rename once through GitHub and leave the old location unused.
5. Update local remotes and publish coordinated reference changes.
6. Verify new URLs and old-name redirects across web, Git, Nix, installers, Home Manager, releases, and the website.
7. Record results and recovery conditions.

## Product scope

The historical plan changed repository identity. It excluded product integration, compatibility layers, command aliases, features, and runtime changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Nova v1 stabilization bead `yazelix-8u5-4-hnv` is closed and the user authorizes the rename.
- The target `luccahuguet/yazelix-nova` is available before execution.
- An inventory covers live owned URLs, Git remotes, Nix references and locks, Home Manager examples, installers, site links, workflows, hosted Actions consumers, badges, releases, Cachix, Pages, webhooks, secrets, and environments.
- GitHub renames the existing repository once and leaves `luccahuguet/yazelix` unused afterward.
- The repository preserves history, branches, tags, releases, issues, discussions, stars, visibility, protections, and required settings.
- Owned live references and local remotes use `luccahuguet/yazelix-nova` after the coordinated cutover.
- New-name clone, fetch, push, web, release, and workflow checks pass. Old-name web and Git redirects pass.
- Nix flake metadata, flake show, package build, temporary profile install, Home Manager evaluation, and the documented install path pass against the new name. Tests record old-name behavior instead of assuming it.
- Hosted GitHub Actions references receive updates before their next run.
- The `yzx` command, Nova product branding, runtime contracts, and repositories for other products remain unchanged.
- The bead records verification evidence, external references that owners must update, and recovery conditions.
notes:
Evidence recorded 2026-08-04:

- GitHub rename documentation confirms redirects for repository web information and Git clone, fetch, and push traffic. Project-site URLs are excluded.
- GitHub does not redirect calls to Actions hosted by a renamed repository and warns against reusing the old repository name.
- The Nova tree contained no `action.yml`, `action.yaml`, or `workflow_call` surface. Execution must repeat this audit and stop for a separate Actions migration if that changes.
- Repository and URL migration did not start.

Superseding decision, 2026-08-07:

- The intermediate organization target in the close reason is historical.
- The user selected `github.com/Yazelix/nova` as the canonical organization repository.
- Keep this bead closed. `yazelix-5vl-move-nova-stack-to-yazelix-org-pqi` owns migration scope, constraints, and evidence.
close_reason: Superseded by the maintainer-selected Yazelix organization migration in yazelix-5vl-move-nova-stack-to-yazelix-org-pqi. Keep the main repository named yazelix at github.com/yazelix/yazelix instead of renaming it to luccahuguet/yazelix-nova.

title: Make nova the canonical CLI in Nova v2
description:
## Product decision

Nova v2 will make `nova` the canonical public CLI, matching Eon's canonical `eon` CLI and aligning each sibling product's name with its front-door command.

## Release contract

- Nova v1 retains `yzx` as its canonical command.
- Edge may expose `nova` before v2 as a compatibility alias to dogfood packaging and detect command-name collisions.
- In v2, help, documentation, examples, onboarding, desktop launchers, and packaging use `nova` as the canonical command.
- `yzx` remains a silent compatibility alias throughout v2, with identical behavior and no warning noise. Its eventual removal is not decided here.
- One dispatcher owns behavior; the two executable names must not grow separate implementations.

## Scope boundary

This decision does not authorize a wholesale rename of internal `yzx-*` helpers, environment variables, configuration/state paths, or other implementation identifiers. Rename or alias a secondary public command only when a real user-facing coherence problem requires it. Eon is unaffected.

Before implementation, audit the `nova` executable namespace on supported Linux/macOS packaging surfaces. Record any collision that would make the public name impractical.

## Acceptance criteria

- An installed `nova` invokes the complete Nova CLI and all supported subcommands.
- V2 public surfaces consistently teach and invoke `nova`.
- Existing scripts using `yzx` continue to behave identically, including machine-readable output.
- Packaging and fresh-session checks exercise both names from the delivered artifact.
- Configuration, state, and environment contracts remain stable unless separately approved.
- CHANGELOG and v2 migration notes explain the canonical-name change and compatibility alias.
- Reconcile dependent planning that currently promises `yzx` as the final canonical command, including `yazelix-add-homebrew-tap-bottle-distribution-9c3-h7s`, before implementation.

## Out of scope

- Removing `yzx` in v2.
- Mass-renaming internals or user data paths.
- Changing Eon's CLI.
- Making this a breaking v1 change.

title: Add quota-only official limits to tokenusage
description:
## Why

Nova displays official Codex quota by default, but tokenusage 1.5.2 exposes official limits only through commands that still load all local usage history. On the investigated machine that means discovering a 4.9 GiB Codex session tree, reading a roughly 40 MiB parse cache, and potentially rewriting the full cache even when the caller needs only rate-limit percentages and reset times. Tokenusage already owns Codex OAuth refresh and app-server fallback, so the no-history capability belongs there rather than in Yazelix.

## Evidence

- `packaging/tokenusage.nix:4-13` pins the current crates.io release, tokenusage 1.5.2.
- tokenusage 1.5.2 `src/pipeline/live.rs:50-61` fetches official limits and then unconditionally calls `load_usage`.
- tokenusage 1.5.2 `src/pipeline/parsing.rs:297-341` discovers sources, loads the incremental cache, parses files, and rewrites the cache when dirty.
- tokenusage 1.5.2 `src/pipeline/parsing.rs:453-491` intentionally walks all Codex JSONL partitions because old sessions can receive new events.
- tokenusage 1.5.2 `src/pipeline/parsing.rs:1409-1415` serializes and writes the entire JSON cache.
- tokenusage 1.5.2 `src/pipeline/official.rs:180-220,2064-2113` already owns OAuth and Codex app-server fallback.
- The crates.io metadata names `https://github.com/hanbu97/tokenusage`, but that repository returned 404 during investigation. Contributor access and the actual upstream route must be verified before implementation.

## Contract

Tokenusage provides one documented machine-readable command for official Codex limits that completes without discovering local Claude/Codex history and without reading, pruning, or writing `parse-cache-v2.json`. Its JSON includes the same plan, primary/secondary used percentages, reset timestamps, and window durations already exposed as `official_codex`. Authentication refresh and app-server fallback remain tokenusage-owned. Missing authentication or unavailable limits fail predictably without falling back to local history parsing.

The exact CLI spelling may follow upstream conventions, for example `tu limits --provider codex --json` or `tu blocks --official-limits-only --json`, but Yazelix consumption must wait for a released, documented contract.

## Scope

In scope:
- Locate the active tokenusage upstream and confirm whether contributions/releases are possible.
- Add an official-limits-only command or flag that returns before `load_usage`.
- Reuse the existing `fetch_codex_official_limits` implementation and JSON types.
- Add focused tests proving no usage source or incremental cache is touched.
- Publish a tokenusage release with the new CLI contract and record its exact version and source revision.

Out of scope:
- Do not fork tokenusage, vendor its source, patch the crates.io tarball in Yazelix, or copy OAuth/app-server logic into the bar without a separate explicit user decision.
- Do not redesign token reports, caches, GUI/TUI surfaces, provider frameworks, or pricing.
- Do not add a daemon or live monitor.

## Implementation Notes

1. Verify the current upstream and contribution route before editing.
2. Reuse official-limit fetching directly; the new path must not construct usage sources or call `load_usage`.
3. Add no dependencies. The required HTTP, auth, app-server, serde, and Tokio code already exists.
4. Preserve the existing `official_codex` JSON field contract unless upstream chooses a smaller versioned equivalent.
5. Use a temporary XDG cache with a sentinel `parse-cache-v2.json` in tests and prove its bytes and timestamp remain unchanged.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` in the active tokenusage source should exit 0.
- `cargo test` in the active tokenusage source should exit 0.
- With valid Codex authentication and an empty temporary sessions root, the new command should return official limits successfully.
- With a sentinel tokenusage parse cache, running the new command should leave the file byte-for-byte unchanged.
- A Linux trace or equivalent focused test should show no open beneath Codex or Claude session roots.
- The published crate version should expose the documented command through `tu --help` and install through the existing Nix Rust package path.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the active upstream cannot be located or does not accept contributions/releases; record the evidence and ask the user to choose among waiting, an owned fork, or replacing tokenusage.
- Stop if quota-only behavior still calls `load_usage` or touches the incremental parse cache.
- Stop if implementation requires a new authentication owner or provider framework.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort S upstream once access exists, risk LOW/MED, confidence HIGH in the technical change and MED in upstream availability. This is not a Beta 4 blocker because the separate safety bead bounds current behavior. Rejected: empty `--codex-sessions-dir`, which tokenusage treats as a new source set and can use to prune the shared cache; direct OAuth duplication in Yazelix; a maintained Nix patch.
design:
Accepted architecture, 2026-08-12:
- Adopt FelixIsaac/tokenusage as the maintained collector upstream; do not continue the unavailable hanbu97 crates.io source line.
- tokenusage owns provider discovery, history parsing, and official-limit retrieval. Nova Bar owns normalized facts, cache/backoff, stale state, and rendering.
- This bead is the smallest vertical slice: add and release one Codex official-limits-only machine contract, then consume it through the existing Nova packaging path. Cursor and broader provider parity remain separate slices.
- A temporary GitHub contribution fork and PR are authorized for upstreaming. Do not create or retain a Yazelix-maintained tokenusage fork, vendor tree, or copied OAuth implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- The active tokenusage upstream and contribution or release route are identified before implementation; if no releasable upstream exists, the bead stops for an explicit user ownership decision.
- A documented machine-readable Codex official-limits command returns the existing plan, percentages, reset timestamps, and window durations without constructing usage sources or calling local-history loading.
- Success and authentication or error paths do not discover session files and do not read, prune, or write parse-cache-v2.json; unavailable limits never fall back to history parsing.
- One focused contract test makes any history-loader call fail, and one sentinel-cache integration check proves the cache bytes and timestamp remain unchanged.
- The upstream format and test suite passes, and a published version exposes the command in tu --help and installs through the existing Yazelix Nix packaging path.
notes:
Accepted upstream candidate, 2026-08-12:
- Maintained upstream is FelixIsaac/tokenusage, baseline main 51da743c4ab16c4c9495e7fb54f2e3ec4713ccc9 (1.11.2). Draft PR https://github.com/FelixIsaac/tokenusage/pull/2 is open and mergeable at head 35e4a0a5a53b91cadac00e3c6b12d603f3e439df. The luccahuguet fork is contribution transport only.
- Contract: `tu blocks --official-limits-only --json` returns the existing `official_codex` schema through tokenusage-owned OAuth and app-server retrieval before timezone parsing, source discovery, local-history loading, pricing, or parse-cache access. Authentication failure is non-zero with no history fallback. Config-driven `noCodex` is rejected. An explicit quota-only command ignores a valid `blocks.live` config default while preserving existing session-length and refresh-interval validation.
- Final patch: 8 files, 158 additions and 4 deletions, with no new dependency or provider abstraction. One Unix integration test covers help discovery, config-driven source-disable failure, authentication failure, a complete 300-minute primary and 10,080-minute weekly success schema from a local Codex endpoint, a missing pricing-file trap that makes any history-loader call fail, unchanged legacy-cache bytes and mtime, and absence of parse-cache-v3. A standard-library TCP listener remains the smallest success fixture.
- Exact-candidate checks at 35e4a0a on Linux passed: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features` (85 unit plus 1 integration); `cargo test` (same plus 12 doctests); `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features`; README and version sync scripts; `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts`; and `cargo build --release`.
- The contract test is enabled for Unix rather than Linux alone. Linux execution passed. An `aarch64-apple-darwin` cross-check from Linux stopped in ring because the host lacks an Apple C compiler (`cc` rejected `-arch` and the macOS deployment flag); this provides no native macOS runtime proof.
- Exact-head release measurements used valid Codex auth, empty config and HOME/XDG roots, an empty Codex sessions directory for the workaround, stdout discarded, and `/usr/bin/time`. Packaged 1.5.2 context remains 0.56s median and 15.93 MiB median peak RSS across five prior samples. Maintained 1.11.2 workaround at 35e4a0a: 0.55s and 17.87 MiB. Quota-only path: 0.45s and 15.03 MiB. Five network-dependent samples do not establish a stable latency improvement; the supported quantitative claim is 15.9% lower median peak RSS than the same-version workaround.
- Running the exact-head workaround populated a 390,318-byte OpenRouter pricing cache. A release-mode valid-auth `strace -f -e trace=openat` probe returned the complete plan/window schema, recorded zero session, parse-cache-v2/v3, or OpenRouter-pricing opens, and left the isolated cache empty.
- Nova consumption remains one narrow invocation replacement after release: replace the Nova Bar empty-source workaround with `tu blocks --official-limits-only --json`; retain Nova-owned normalization, one-minute freshness, two-minute failure backoff, stale state, and rendering. Nova will consume a tagged release, not the contribution fork or an unreleased patch.
- Rejected: a provider abstraction or test dependency; removing distinct help, authentication, or cache assertions; treating log-only `--only` selection as official-quota disablement; changing unrelated block validation; and a stable latency claim from network-dependent samples.
- No hosted checks, comments, or reviews are currently reported on the PR.
- Release gate: an upstream maintainer must merge and publish a release containing 35e4a0a or an equivalent accepted revision. Resume after release to record the exact tag and source revision and prove the released command through Nix packaging.

title: Upstream Nova Rio deltas and retire removable fork patches
description:
## Why

Nova now depends on a deliberately minimal Rio fork, but every surviving behavioral patch is generally useful or has a clear upstream decision path. Keeping accepted behavior only in Yazelix permanently creates rebase, release, and regression work. The goal is to offer each generic mechanism upstream independently, then remove only the fork patches that an exact upstream release replaces.

No pull request is authorized by this Bead. The maintainer explicitly said the project is not ready to open one yet.

## Contract

Consumer: upstream Rio users and Yazelix Nova users.

Trigger: one fork delta is reviewed against current upstream main, approved by the Yazelix maintainer for contribution, accepted upstream, and included in a pinned Rio release.

Observable result: upstream Rio owns the accepted behavior; Nova Rio removes the equivalent maintained patch; Nova pins and dogfoods the exact replacement without user-visible regression.

Important failure behavior: an already-upstream, rejected, stalled, or materially redesigned contribution leaves the current fork behavior and Nova pin intact. Do not silently remove behavior, bundle unrelated changes, force-push published history, or treat an open PR as an upstream replacement.

## Evidence

- `../nova-rio/README.md:3-22` records exact upstream baseline `b2e7c38bdc56bb86b346ca4f37b9aeaa5151d790` and four removal-gated deltas at fork revision `36f3e40b1a4c53929d646995b2cf28660b72af6e`.
- The reviewed local `upstream/main` reference is `701bf22f9d467d7c445ca047c427832cdc186f5c`, 51 commits beyond that baseline. None of the four fork commits is its ancestor, and their named mechanisms are absent there. Refresh upstream before implementation; this reference is evidence, not a future base.
- Kitty cleanup, commit `0f30576eaac5b7bb0bba90cc0acd456f4aa0bfd2`: `rio-vt/src/crosswords/mod.rs:4105-4115` clears obsolete direct placements only for alternate-screen full erase; `:6952-7015` proves main-screen scrollback and alternate-screen behavior.
- Balanced grid origin, commit `807a712000c3fa47ce5bca5c4b331e8403553723`: `frontends/rioterm/src/layout/mod.rs:88-95,165-181,1731-1735` owns one integer-pixel vertical origin; renderer, input, images, cursor trail, and IME consume it; `layout/compute_tests.rs:238-260` covers odd and even remainder behavior.
- Quit confirmation, commit `3974ce70e79878332e2d05ab0f7a97eef8ac5ba4`: `frontends/rioterm/src/renderer/confirm_quit.rs:40-90` measures the rendered text, balances padding, and draws the rounded border/background. Measurement and spacing are generic; Nova's orange treatment is product styling.
- Launch override, commit `c33387a91ef2b518b34e3523b01f1760c9f679c0`: `frontends/rioterm/src/cli.rs:24-38,66-68,102-114` defines and tests `--theme-mode dark|light`; `application.rs:34-55,73-80,568-576` keeps it authoritative across initial load and config reload.
- Closed Bead `yazelix-5vl-replace-mars-remove-cursors-j3ra` records full mechanical proof and accepted fresh-session dogfood for Nova `e1aee3cfadf5083a8af74e9aa07c2c9f7f6644c6` with Rio `36f3e40b1a4c53929d646995b2cf28660b72af6e`.

## Scope

In scope:

- Refresh and inspect current upstream Rio before shaping any contribution. Re-derive the minimum patch from current upstream code; do not mechanically replay the old commit.
- Treat the behaviors as separate review units and separate PRs: Kitty alternate-screen cleanup; launch-time theme override; shared balanced grid origin; quit-prompt measurement/spacing.
- Preserve the focused regression tests and add only the cheapest upstream-facing proof needed after drift.
- Present each proposed branch, diff, test evidence, and PR text to the Yazelix maintainer before any external write. Open a PR only after explicit approval for that specific contribution.
- Record upstream feedback and adapt only within the accepted behavior. A materially different API or product choice returns to the maintainer.
- After an accepted change ships in an exact upstream release, audit that release, remove the equivalent fork delta through safe additive history, update the fork boundary, pin the exact child in Nova, and run fresh delivery proof.

Out of scope:

- No PR, upstream issue, comment, branch push, or maintainer contact merely because this Bead exists.
- Do not send a four-feature mega-PR or include the fork README and expression-only cleanup commits.
- Do not upstream Mars behavior, Yazelix Cursors, Nova configuration, Nix packaging, branding, or unrelated Rio cleanup.
- Do not require Nova's orange quit border as upstream behavior. Offer generic measurement and balanced spacing first; contribute styling only if upstream explicitly wants it.
- Do not add a compatibility adapter, feature framework, dependency, watcher, or duplicate config owner.
- Do not rewrite or force-push published Nova Rio history, and do not change Nova main or stable without their normal promotion authority.

## Implementation Notes

1. Fetch current upstream only when implementation begins. Record exact base, release, relevant drift, and whether any behavior already exists equivalently.
2. Prepare Kitty cleanup first: it has the narrowest owner, direct protocol symptom, and strongest deterministic regression.
3. Prepare the generic launch override second. Keep the CLI finite to dark/light and prove it remains authoritative after reload.
4. Prepare the balanced grid-origin change third. Trace every paint/input/graphics/cursor/IME consumer again because this is the widest patch.
5. Split quit work into generic text measurement/balanced spacing and product color treatment. Retain the local color patch if upstream does not want that policy.
6. For each unit, create a clean contribution branch from the then-current upstream main and preserve authorship/provenance. Do not push or open a PR before explicit user approval.
7. An upstream merge is not a removal gate. Wait for an exact usable release, audit it, then update the fork and Nova through their normal checked delivery paths.
8. Close with one disposition per delta: already upstream, merged and released, retained after rejection, or intentionally deferred with the evidence that should reopen it.

## Verification

Before any approved PR:

- `git merge-base --is-ancestor <candidate-base> upstream/main` should exit 0 after refreshing the reference.
- `cargo fmt -- --check --color always` should exit 0.
- `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` should exit 0 or report only upstream-owned warnings explicitly accepted before contribution.
- `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test --features wgpu` should exit 0.
- `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test -p rio-vt kitty_placements_clear_only_on_alt_screen_full_erase --features graphics` should pass for the Kitty unit.
- `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test -p rioterm` should pass layout, CLI, application, and renderer tests.
- Each proposed PR diff should contain one behavior and its proof, with no Nova README or unrelated fork code.

Before removing an accepted fork delta:

- The exact upstream release source must contain the accepted mechanism and regression proof.
- `git diff <upstream-release>...<nova-rio-candidate>` must show that the retired behavior is no longer a maintained fork patch.
- Nova must pass `nix flake check`, `nix flake show --all-systems`, `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs`, and an isolated profile install.
- Fresh-session dogfood must cover the changed surface. Grid and quit work require visual resize/scale checks; Kitty requires Yazi image enter/close/erase behavior; theme mode requires dark/light launch and config reload.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if current upstream already provides equivalent behavior; prove equivalence and plan removal instead of submitting duplicate code.
- Stop if drift changes the owner or invalidates the existing regression.
- Stop before bundling multiple deltas to make a contribution appear larger or easier to land.
- Stop if upstream asks for a materially broader API, new dependency, or behavior Nova has not accepted.
- Stop before any external write without explicit maintainer approval for that exact PR.
- Stop before removing a local patch until an exact upstream release and fresh Nova dogfood replace it.
- Stop if preserving published fork history requires a force push or destructive rewrite; request a safe update decision.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort: L. Risk: MED. Confidence: HIGH for Kitty cleanup and launch override, MED for the cross-surface grid change, and MED/LOW for upstream acceptance of quit styling.

No new dependency is expected. Prefer upstream ownership and deletion from the fork over adapters.

Rejected alternatives: one mega-PR, mechanical cherry-picks onto current upstream, opening draft PRs before approval, deleting patches at merge time, requiring Nova branding upstream, and keeping equivalent patches after a released upstream replacement.
acceptance_criteria:
- Current upstream Rio is refreshed and audited at an exact revision before any contribution branch is prepared.
- Each of the four fork deltas receives an explicit independent disposition and never shares a PR with another delta.
- No upstream issue, comment, branch push, or PR is created without explicit maintainer authorization for that exact external write.
- Every proposed contribution is reduced to current-upstream code, carries focused proof, and passes upstream format, Clippy, and test gates appropriate to its surface.
- Generic quit measurement/spacing is separated from Nova's orange styling policy.
- A local patch is removed only after an exact upstream release contains equivalent behavior and Nova passes package, isolated-install, closure, and fresh-session dogfood checks.
- Nova Rio's README and maintained diff identify only the deltas that still remain after each accepted upstream release.
- Published fork history, Nova main, and Nova stable are not rewritten or advanced outside their existing authority.

title: Require verified linear channel promotions
description: Outcome: keep stable <= main <= edge on one linear history, with whole-revision fast-forward promotions only. Routine Stable promotions wait at least seven days; explicitly requested urgent fixes may move sooner without bypassing proof. Review the complete accumulated candidate diff, including intervening commits. Contract: Stable protection requires an unambiguous Version Gate aggregate that succeeds only when both native release jobs succeed, plus existing Linux and actual cache publication checks; missing Cachix credentials fail publishing. Enforce linear history and administrator checks on Main and Stable. Cadence, predecessor membership, whole-candidate acceptance and manual dogfood remain explicit maintainer policy; no automated publisher or new credentials. Scope: platform-neutral release policy and workflow outcome handling, plus explicitly Linux cache publication; leave native build arguments, timeouts, runtime, pins and Main/Stable refs unchanged. Verification: actionlint; execute gate and credential checks against success, failure, cancellation, skipping and missing-token cases; regenerate and verify AGENTS from the pinned Starcompass source; read back GitHub protections. Existing wn00 owns Darwin build staging; 71kp owns the later promotion and is governed by the weekly policy. No Stable promotion in this run.
notes:
## Accepted implementation

Published release safeguards on Edge at 7516678a8c6e344a1ae27d5fa56024ada42a1d93; corrected Linux publication is 13edc2480d58c84f51034dd7c561cf7472850921. Main and Stable enforce linear history and administrator checks, preserving no-force-push and no-deletion rules. Stable requires linux, publish_x86_64_linux, publish_aarch64_darwin and the unique release-gate from GitHub Actions (app 15368). The aggregate succeeds only when both native Version Gate jobs succeed. Predecessor membership, seven-day cadence, acceptance of the entire candidate and fresh-session dogfood remain explicit maintainer policy. No automated publisher, scheduler, service or secret was added.

Both cache jobs reject absent credentials and submit the requested output closures through synchronous cachix push. Linux passes Nix stdout to Cachix stdin with Bash pipefail: either build or upload failure rejects the required job. Both actions disable background publication. Darwin retains its existing nine-output guard and remote narinfo verification. This corrects failure behavior and removes the Linux daemon/socket/hook lifecycle; it is not described as an isomorphic refactor. The corrected executable surface is explicitly the Linux publishing job. Darwin implementation, native build arguments, outputs, Nix graph, runtime, permissions, job names, concurrency, timeouts and channel heads were not changed by the review.

## Source evidence and rejected mechanism

Cachix action v17 at 38b082610b782e7e93e209c35fd730d399dee866 defaults to daemon mode. Its generated post-build hook logs enqueue failures and returns success, and its README states substituted outputs do not trigger that hook. That mechanism cannot prove the required publication contract. Adopted the existing dependency's documented pipeline: https://docs.cachix.org/pushing/#pushing-runtime-closure. Exact upstream source is preserved in /tmp/nova-release-review-o90odtqr/cachix-action-main.ts.

## Verification

- Corrected exact-revision CI passed: https://github.com/Yazelix/nova/actions/runs/34246415687.
- Both actual cache jobs and every publishing step passed on 13edc248: https://github.com/Yazelix/nova/actions/runs/34246437891. Linux job 102129526299 executed the synchronous pipeline and reported that all requested store paths were already on Cachix; no new upload was needed. This proves the real idempotent publication path, not a newly transferred closure. Darwin job 102129526105 passed explicit publication and remote narinfo verification. Complete job/step metadata and Linux log are in /tmp/nova-release-review-o90odtqr.
- The reproducible regression probe /tmp/nova-release-review-o90odtqr/check-publish.py executes the real YAML step with Nix/Cachix stand-ins. The baseline failed because the step never invoked the publisher. The corrected step passes all four build/upload success-failure pairs, submits all 11 exact output lines and disables background publication. These probes cover errors without pretending to be real uploads.
- actionlint, git diff --check, all 25 release-result pairs and both credential guards passed. Only success+success admits the aggregate; absent/empty credentials reject both publishing jobs without exposing a token. Guard probe: /tmp/nova-promotion-policy-s1_boijg/check-guards.py. Both Python probes use locally installed PyYAML 6.0.1.
- AGENTS was rendered and source-checked against pinned Starcompass 95c29fa76a971726b65e1d1dc06c518d525c46a2 with the Yazelix source URL preserved. Before/request/after protection API evidence is in /tmp/nova-promotion-policy-s1_boijg; live protections were checked again during review. Original implementation CI: https://github.com/Yazelix/nova/actions/runs/34243314147.
- LOC is 28,926 (+60 for the full issue; +4 for the publication correction), with matching README and development scorecards. The extra lines replace the background publishing lifecycle with one native pipeline and document its contract.

## Boundaries and simplification decisions

Retained two explicit native-result checks, the unique aggregate, both credential guards and Darwin's output-count/narinfo checks. Removing them would weaken validation; a helper for two small guards would add a file and indirection. No further concrete defects or worthwhile simplifications were found in the reviewed changes.

The hosted cache runs use locked inputs. Full Version Gate was not rerun, so these results do not replace its native compatibility-build proof. wn00 still owns the known Darwin timeout; 71kp's eventual promotion waits for complete exact-revision release proof and the weekly policy. Main remains 352f1f77 and Stable e1610fb0. No Main or Stable promotion is part of this issue.
close_reason: Review fixed Linux publication; exact-revision CI, both cache jobs, guard checks and failure probes passed.

title: Verify Atuin in a fresh Nova session
description:
Goal

Determine whether user-installed Atuin works correctly in Yazelix Nova without adding Nova-owned integration unless a demonstrated gap requires it. Start with the default managed Nushell and its supported ~/.config/yazelix/nu/config.nu extension point.

Contract

A user who initializes Atuin from Nova’s supported Nushell hook can launch a fresh installed Nova session, record commands, search/select history through Atuin, and retain that history across a newly started session. Failure must be attributed to Nova, Atuin, or host configuration before choosing a fix.

Acceptance criteria

- Test an exact installed Nova revision from a newly started session, not the source checkout or an existing process.
- Configure user-installed Atuin only through ~/.config/yazelix/nu/config.nu; do not modify the packaged Nushell files.
- Verify initialization, command capture, interactive history search/selection, and persistence after closing and starting a fresh Nova session.
- Verify ordinary Nushell history and the Nova prompt/startup remain usable when Atuin is enabled.
- Record the Nova revision, Atuin version, platform, configuration snippet, observations, and any narrower unverified surfaces.
- If the existing hook works, close with evidence and add no runtime code. If it fails because of Nova, define the smallest Nova-owned contract and fix as follow-up implementation work; do not package or configure Atuin speculatively.

Scope boundary

This issue proves the default Nushell path only. Bash, Zsh, Fish, automatic Atuin installation, sync-account behavior, and Nova-owned Atuin configuration are outside scope unless separately chosen.
notes:
## Accepted state — 2026-08-09

User-installed Atuin works through Nova’s supported Nushell extension point with no Nova runtime change. The accepted test used installed Nova edge revision `57b0c8621894c59d058d7ba7d91464864b7c4917` (`Yazelix Nova 1.0.0`) on Linux x86_64, Atuin `18.16.1`, Nushell `0.113.1`, and Carapace `1.6.3`.

The user profile supplied Atuin. `~/.local/share/atuin/init.nu` was generated with `atuin init nu --disable-up-arrow`, and `~/.config/yazelix/nu/config.nu` sourced that static file. Packaged Nushell files remained unchanged. Sync, import, daemon, pty-proxy, and Nova-owned packaging/configuration were not enabled.

Mechanical checks proved a clean managed-shell startup, the normal Starship prompt, command capture with directory/exit/duration, one Atuin Ctrl-R binding, no Atuin Up-arrow binding, ordinary Nushell history availability, and a surviving Carapace external completer that returned `git checkout`. The maintainer then exercised the fresh-session interaction and reported that it works very well and feels like an upgrade to Nushell history. This satisfies the user-installed integration contract. No Nova defect or follow-up fix was found.
close_reason: Accepted after fresh-session user dogfood: Atuin works well through the existing Nushell hook with Carapace, prompt, and native Up-arrow history preserved; no Nova code required

title: Publish the Nova v1 article on X
description:
## Why

The Nova v1 article is published, but it has not yet been adapted into a focused X announcement. The release story is time-sensitive and the article already has a concise video asset suitable for discovery.

## Evidence

- `../nova-site/drafts/yazelix-nova-v1.md:2-12` marks the article published, names release `nova-v1.1.0`, and owns its title, description, source revision, and preview asset.
- `../nova-site/drafts/yazelix-nova-v1.md:15-55` contains the maintainer voice and the core story: daily utility, modal keyboard workflow, clearer component boundaries, and 75 percent less code than Classic.
- `../nova-site/public/blog/yazelix-nova-v1/media/nova-in-60-seconds.mp4` is the article-owned short demonstration; its poster is beside it.
- Canonical article URL: `https://nova.yazelix.com/blog/yazelix-nova-v1/`.

## User-visible contract

Consumer: people discovering Yazelix Nova through the Lucca or Yazelix X account.

Trigger: the maintainer approves the final copy and publishes it.

Observable result: one concise, platform-native X post introduces Nova v1 in Lucca voice, links the canonical article, and uses the article video or poster without overstating current release behavior.

Important failure behavior: do not publish from an account, upload media, create a thread, or make any other external write without explicit approval in the implementation run. Failed publication must leave the approved copy and media choice available for manual posting.

## Scope

In scope:
- Re-read the live article and verify the canonical URL immediately before drafting.
- Draft one X post around one strong hook, preferably the daily-workspace story, 63-second tour, or 75 percent code reduction.
- Keep the article URL in the post and verify current X length and media constraints at execution time.
- Prefer the article-owned MP4 when X accepts it; otherwise use the owned poster.
- Present exact final text and media to Lucca for approval before publishing.
- After approved publication, record the public post URL and publication time in this Bead.

Out of scope:
- No thread, scheduled campaign, paid promotion, article rewrite, release announcement rewrite, automated reposting, or reply campaign.
- Do not silently update claims from current Edge work or present the article source revision as the current Stable revision.

## Verification

- The canonical article and selected media URL or local asset are reachable before publication.
- The final text fits current X limits, contains the exact canonical article URL, and makes only claims supported by the article source record.
- Lucca approves the exact copy, account, and media before the external write.
- The published post is publicly reachable and its permalink is recorded in the Bead.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the live article, media, or social metadata is unavailable or materially different from the cited published source.
- Stop if account access, target account, or publication approval is missing.
- Stop before expanding one post into a thread or broader campaign.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort: S. Risk: LOW for drafting, MED for the irreversible external publication. No dependency or automation is needed.

title: Add host-Yazi package variants without bundled Yazi closure
description: Implement the accepted bounded host-Yazi slice from decision yazelix-maw-o4d and GitHub #672. Rename the Mars-free outputs to the uniform package family yazelix[-no-mars][-no-helix][-no-yazi] with no aliases. no-yazi packages must retain yzx-yazi, managed configuration, open/reveal/sidebar/editor/Zellij integration, but contain no runtime reference to pkgs.yazi. Resolve yazi and ya once from the effective runtime PATH for session-producing and Yazi-dependent commands. Missing binaries, failed version probes, and yazi/ya version mismatch are startup failures. A matching pair that differs from the Nova-tested version emits a warning and continues. Route yzx run yazi through the managed wrapper and yzx run ya through the resolved absolute ya. Host installations own optional preview dependencies. Keep the bundled default deterministic and unchanged apart from the package-family rename.
design: Nix remains the package-composition owner. Extend the internal mkYzx inputs with withManagedYazi and generate one source fact containing source, yazi command, ya command, and tested version for yzx. The bundled branch embeds pkgs.yazi paths; the host branch embeds command names only. Rust runtime resolution owns command lookup, executable checks, canonical paths, normalized version probes, pair validation, and warnings. Runtime apply exports YZX_YAZI_BIN and YZX_YA so yzx-yazi and all yzx-open helpers consume the same pair without re-resolving. The private yzx-yazi launcher must require YZX_YAZI_BIN instead of embedding pkgs.yazi. Home Manager keeps only programs.yazelix.package. Do not add a generic registry, builder, source option, shell sourcing, explicit host path option, or compatibility alias.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Eight explicit package outputs exist under yazelix[-no-mars][-no-helix][-no-yazi], and runtime/runtime-no-helix aliases do not exist. 2. Existing bundled outputs still launch locked Yazi and pass existing contracts. 3. Every no-yazi output has no reference path to the locked pkgs.yazi output. 4. A valid host yazi/ya pair is canonicalized once and used by layouts, popups, opener follow, reveal, sidebar refresh, yzx run yazi, and yzx run ya. 5. Missing, non-executable, unprobeable, or pair-mismatched binaries fail actionably. 6. A matching pair different from the tested version warns and continues. 7. Doctor reports selected source, lookup PATH, resolved paths, pair version, and tested version. 8. Unrelated yzx run commands and recovery commands do not require Yazi preflight. 9. Home Manager documentation demonstrates package selection plus user-owned pkgs.yazi. 10. README LOC scorecard and CHANGELOG reflect the package/runtime contract. 11. Focused Rust checks, nix flake check, flake show, package builds, closure/reference checks, and temporary profile installation pass for the changed surface.
notes: Implemented the accepted eight-output package matrix with no runtime aliases. Host-Yazi variants retain Nova integration while resolving canonical yazi/ya paths, rejecting missing/unprobeable/mismatched pairs, warning for matching untested versions, pinning a complete inherited pair across session children, and ignoring a partial legacy private pair in favor of fresh PATH resolution. Home Manager continues to use programs.yazelix.package plus user-owned pkgs.yazi. Final x86_64-linux measurements: yazelix 2,447,857,424 bytes / 619 paths; yazelix-no-yazi 2,044,345,752 / 500; yazelix-no-mars 1,475,471,032 / 591; yazelix-no-mars-no-yazi 1,049,301,704 / 460; minimal 754,017,176 / 162. Managed-Yazi removal saves 403,511,672 bytes (384.8 MiB) with Mars and 426,169,328 bytes (406.4 MiB) without Mars. Verification passed: six Rust launcher tests, focused host-Yazi/no-Mars/no-Helix/bundled contracts, all 34 compatible local flake checks, Home Manager, real locked yazi/ya smoke, all-system flake evaluation, all eight package realizations, default build, YAML parse, diff/LOC/stale-name guards, and default plus minimal temporary profile installs.
close_reason: Implemented and verified the explicit package matrix and bounded host-Yazi runtime contract.

title: Dogfood Nova on exact EonTerm
description:
## Decision and scope

Dogfood Nova on the exact EonTerm product selected by the user through one fixed x86_64-linux opt-in output. This is the final integration and comparison run before default cutover: current `yzx launch` remains Mars-backed, and this issue cannot remove Mars, change defaults, add a generic provider, or broaden platform claims.

## Prerequisites and ownership

- Eon `eon-4is.5` has accepted EonTerm through the temporary Eonova bridge at exact Eon and Nova revisions.
- Venus `ven-native-clipboard-paste-uas` proves native clipboard paste and `ven-lq4` proves safe hyperlink interaction at exact accepted revisions.
- Eon `eon-eonterm-presentation-e4f`, `eon-consume-venus-background-blur-k8o`, and `eon-eonterm-application-identity-xwi` are accepted. Nova `yazelix-5vl-map-eonterm-presentation-0kd6` and `yazelix-5vl-eonterm-nova-identity-e8ra` consume opacity and identity; Nova uses the approved EON-C14 blur-on default without adding another override or policy owner.
- `yazelix-5vl-eonterm-kitty-graphics-decision-totz` is closed with an explicit outcome. If parity is required, its exact Orbit/Venus/Eon graphics proofs are accepted before this run; if a bounded regression is accepted, this run proves truthful capability reporting and the documented loss.
- Closed `yazelix-5vl-eonova-shifted-punctuation-9g3h` remains discovery evidence only; this run rechecks the exact final path.
- Exact final EonTerm candidate reproduces or disposes `ven-render-braille-progress-wcf` and `ven-stable-cursor-blink-v4o`. A confirmed owner defect is fixed separately before a promote recommendation; Nova adds no compensation.

EonTerm owns native lifecycle, component identity, Orbit Session hosting, and Venus presentation. Nova owns its wrapper, branding, runtime preparation, exact pin, managed tools, Zellij configuration, workspace, and keys. Zellij remains the workspace/session owner inside the hosted command. This issue consumes exact EON-C1 through EON-C4, EON-C11 through EON-C15, ORB-C1 through ORB-C10, and the accepted Venus contracts named by the prerequisites; it changes no child contract.

## Observable contract

A user explicitly selects one Nova EonTerm dogfood package or app. Nova prepares its existing environment and asks exact `eonterm` to host exact `yzx enter`. The managed workspace opens with Nova identity and accepted presentation settings in one native surface, preserves the live Session across client loss, and reports unsupported or failed behavior explicitly. There is no Mars, Rio, Eonova runtime dependency, hidden fallback, copied protocol, or default change.

## References before code

Required: current Nova instructions, `yzx launch` and `yzx enter`, package constructor/capability variants, desktop identity, root appearance and configuration, Zellij config, runtime preparation, Linux checks, exact Eonova/EonTerm proofs, every prerequisite above, current pinned Mars behavior and performance tools, Orbit `orb-bi4.5.4` accepted workload envelope, and the measurement design in `orb-1sd`.

Conditional: exact Orbit, Venus, Nova Zellij, Mars, compositor, or benchmark source only after a captured boundary or measurement question. Product instrumentation, public traces, adapters, and new benchmark dependencies require separate approval.

Rejected: generic surface interface, permanent multi-terminal support, Mars fallback, Eonova dependency, duplicated compatibility graph, input workaround, platform expansion, default-package changes, incomparable benchmark conditions, or subjective timing as promotion evidence.

## Acceptance

1. One explicit x86_64-linux output builds, installs, and opens exact EonTerm hosting exact `yzx enter`; normal Nova packages and `yzx launch` remain unchanged.
2. Its closure contains no Mars or Rio. Diagnostics report exact Nova, EonTerm, Eon, Orbit, and Venus lineage without replacing Nova product identity. Private exact inputs are acceptable for this private dogfood; no public-distribution claim is made.
3. Fresh installed dogfood records tabs, panes, popups, editor, file manager, Git flow, long-running work, `?`, a shifted-punctuation corpus, ordinary keys, managed bindings, mouse, focus, native `Ctrl+Shift+V`, multiline/bracketed paste, resize, Unicode, selection/copy, clickable hyperlinks, alternate screen, scrollback, opacity, default blur, native identity, detach/reconnect, failure, and cleanup. It records the selected Kitty/Yazi graphics outcome and exact Braille/cursor-blink disposition.
4. Before the first accepted performance run, record exact candidates, machine/display/GPU, window/grid/font, workload commands, repetitions, observation methods, and numeric pass/fail ceilings. Run the same exact Nova workload through current pinned Mars and EonTerm under those fixed conditions.
5. Compare cold launch to first coherent frame, idle CPU/RSS, sustained fullscreen-output CPU/RSS and final convergence, representative Neovim and large Yazi/TUI work, resize convergence, Venus loss, and reattachment. Record p50/p95 or an explicit bound where meaningful. Measure keypress-to-visible-pixel latency with Typometer only when the real platform path is observable; otherwise declare it unavailable before the run and use no internal or title proxy.
6. Record exact closure sizes and store-path counts separately from performance. Size neutrality cannot substitute for behavior or latency.
7. EonTerm must pass the predeclared envelope and show no unexplained material regression against Mars on the selected workloads. A failed metric names the likely owner and blocks promotion; this issue does not repair it.
8. Exact revisions, artifacts, raw-result locations, platform, checks, gaps, and one promote/defer/reject recommendation are recorded. Promote requires no open P0/P1 integration defect in the exact component set and no unresolved confirmed rendering defect from the named dogfood reports.
9. Required Nova checks, temporary-profile install, fresh-session proof, docs/LOC updates for the opt-in surface, and `git diff --check` pass.

Stop and route a missing contract to its owner. Do not compensate in Nova, broaden into a provider abstraction, weaken a failed threshold after measurement, or change the default in this issue.
notes: Planning reconciliation — 2026-08-14 America/Sao_Paulo: the former presentation chain was split with user approval. `ven-terminal-presentation-settings-5y7`, `eon-eonterm-presentation-e4f`, and `yazelix-5vl-map-eonterm-presentation-0kd6` now mean background opacity only. Configured family/fallbacks/size/line-height/geometry in this dogfood issue require `ven-terminal-typography-geometry-settings-ojv`, `eon-terminal-typography-geometry-config-b63`, and local blocker `yazelix-5vl-map-eonterm-typography-geometry-ppf4`. This note changes no product contract or implementation and preserves the existing dogfood acceptance scope.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Planning reconciliation — 2026-08-14: final EonTerm dogfood now consumes EON-C13 opacity, proved EON-C14 default blur, and deferred EON-C15 application identity. Nova accepts the Eon blur-on default and adds no second blur setting or policy owner.

title: Evaluate workspace-root pane creation and Alt m policy
description:
## Question

Should plain `Alt m` continue using native Zellij `NewPane`, which inherits the current pane cwd, or should Yazelix offer a workspace-root pane action?

The current behavior is acceptable and familiar, but the focused pane can be Yazi in a deeply nested directory, a shell after `cd`, or a locally drifted editor. The pane orchestrator already exposes `open_workspace_terminal`, so a workspace-centric action may be useful without changing how all panes behave.

## Evaluate

- Keep current `Alt m -> NewPane` unchanged.
- Replace `Alt m` with an orchestrator-owned workspace-root terminal.
- Preserve `Alt m` and add a separate command/key/menu action.
- Add a setting only if dogfooding demonstrates durable demand for both defaults.
- Behavior before an explicit workspace exists, after a retarget, with Yazi focused below the root, and with shell/Helix pane-local drift.
- Whether the workspace action should open the configured shell and how it should interact with layouts, floating panes, and pane focus.
- Relationship to packaged `:yzx-new-shell`, which intentionally opens at the current file directory when a file exists; do not erase that distinct file-local workflow without evidence.

## Guardrails

- This is a decision bead, not authorization to change `Alt m` or add a setting.
- Reuse the orchestrator workspace root and existing terminal-opening action.
- Do not force existing panes to change cwd or make focused-pane cwd canonical.
- Do not add multiple near-duplicate bindings without a clear discoverability story.
- Current native behavior remains the baseline if no option is clearly better.

## Outcome

Record the preferred policy, key/command surface if any, bootstrap behavior, and rejected alternatives. Create an implementation bead only after the maintainer chooses a direction.
acceptance_criteria: The bead closes with a documented choice among keeping native Alt-m, replacing it with workspace-root pane creation, or adding a separate surface. The decision is dogfooded from nested Yazi, drifted shell/editor, bootstrap, and explicit-retarget states; it identifies the orchestrator action to reuse and does not add a setting or keybinding by itself.

title: Add sponsorship to Nova release notes
description:
## Delivered contract

Readers of all 13 reviewed GitHub releases receive one short footer linking to the canonical https://github.com/sponsors/luccahuguet destination. Each original body remains byte-for-byte intact as the prefix of the edited body. Release IDs, tag refs, titles, draft/prerelease flags, publication timestamps, assets and Latest selection remain unchanged.

Lucca authorized these published body edits on 2026-09-07 after reviewing the scope. The pre-edit inventory exactly matched nova-v1.1.0, nova-v1.0.0, nova-v1.0.0-beta.1 through beta.5, v17, v16, v14, v13, v12 and v11; all 13 reported immutable=false.

## Footer and ownership

If Yazelix saves you time, you can support continued development on [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/luccahuguet).

GitHub release bodies own the published copy. docs/development.md contains the same copyable footer and requires it once in future release notes. README and development LOC scorecards count 28,739 tracked lines; the 11 added lines document this manual release step. No automation is needed unless the documented step repeatedly fails.

## Scope and proof

Platform-neutral documentation and release-copy work. No release creation, tag/asset mutation, runtime change, package change or channel promotion. Original API snapshots, exact before/candidate bodies and verified after responses are preserved in /tmp/nova-ya2z-iyk5ihp6.

Serial gh release edit --notes-file writes passed per-release API checks, including preservation of legacy CRLF line endings. A final complete inventory read and git ls-remote comparison confirmed all 13 exact bodies, release metadata, tag refs and Latest selection. Canonical-footer and tracked-text scorecard checks plus git diff --check passed. No Nix or Darwin build is required for this documentation-only surface.

notes: Completed 2026-09-07. Proof: /tmp/nova-ya2z-iyk5ihp6/verification.txt, releases-before.json, releases-after.json, tags-before.txt and the per-release snapshots. All 13 published bodies match their prepared append-only candidates; documentation checks pass.
