title: Confirm canonical Nova Home Manager and Mars on macOS
description:
## Why

The pre-cutover macOS gate can prove Nova's published staging package, Home Manager module, Mars, and managed workflow on real Darwin hardware. It cannot prove the atomically renamed canonical `yzx` package and `github:luccahuguet/yazelix` install path before those surfaces exist. Stable Nova v1 still needs that final canonical confirmation, and GitHub issue 577 must remain open until it happens.

## User outcome

During the Nova beta, a real macOS Home Manager or nix-darwin user installs canonical Yazelix, activates the canonical module, runs the `yzx` command floor, launches Mars, and uses managed Zellij, Yazi, and Helix without Linux-only helpers or desktop entries.

## Scope

- Start only after the canonical cutover publishes a Nova beta from `luccahuguet/yazelix`.
- Reuse the smallest test plan and environment evidence from the staging macOS validation bead.
- Test a published canonical input without local overrides.
- Verify `yzx help`, `yzx status --json`, `yzx doctor`, `yzx enter`, and `yzx launch` from Terminal.
- Verify Home Manager-owned canonical config is declarative/read-only and not mutated.
- Verify Mars keyboard input plus managed Zellij, Yazi, Helix, and Yazi-to-editor open.
- Confirm Darwin receives no Linux desktop entry or Linux-only runtime dependency.
- Record exact version, architecture, install shape, commands, and results in GitHub issue 577 through the canonical main issue-mapping bead.
- Close GitHub issue 577 only after the macOS user confirms the canonical beta.

## Out of scope

- Do not block the beta source swap on a public surface that does not exist until that swap.
- Do not add compatibility for the former development command or repository paths.
- Do not broaden macOS or terminal support beyond the tested contract.
- Do not close from cross-evaluation alone.

## Verification

- Canonical Darwin package and Home Manager boundaries evaluate/build without overrides.
- A real macOS activation exposes only the canonical `yzx`.
- The command floor and Mars-managed workflow pass on real hardware.
- Config ownership remains declarative and Linux-only surfaces are absent.
- GitHub issue 577 contains the evidence and is closed.
- Any failure has an owner-correct P0/P1 beta follow-up.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the canonical beta is unpublished or the test uses a local override.
- Stop if a non-macOS agent attempts to substitute evaluation for manual runtime evidence.
- Stop stable Nova v1 while this canonical confirmation or any resulting P0/P1 fix remains incomplete.

## Maintenance Notes

This is an internal post-cutover release gate. The main repository's `yazelix-8u5-5-fl0` bead remains the sole owner of GitHub issue 577 and its `external_ref`; do not duplicate that mapping here.
notes: Decision accepted 2026-07-25: sustained active Yazelix use on macOS by Tyce, with no reported macOS regression during the Nova beta, is accepted as real-world observational evidence for the declared macOS floor. The exact current candidate also passed its aarch64-darwin build/cache job. This evidence means “no known macOS regression,” not that every command in the earlier one-time checklist was individually witnessed. A point-in-time manual confirmation is no longer a stable-v1 blocker; any concrete macOS failure reported later receives an owner-correct P0/P1 follow-up. GitHub issue 577 is no longer a release gate and was not externally changed by this Beads decision.
close_reason: Accepted sustained active macOS use without reported regression, together with green aarch64-darwin build/cache evidence, as the Nova v1 macOS floor; a separate scripted confirmation no longer blocks release.

title: Launch Yazelix Nova v1
description: Yazelix Nova 1.0 is the canonical public product at `Yazelix/nova`, installed as `yzx` with config root `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/yazelix` and state root `$XDG_DATA_HOME/yazelix`. One linear `edge -> main -> stable` history owns all release channels. Classic remains preserved through frozen archival refs and immutable tags. The former development repository is private. The first-party ecosystem lives in the `Yazelix` organization. The stable release identity is `nova-v1.0.0`.
acceptance_criteria: Complete when the accepted release revision belongs to `edge`, while `main`, `stable`, and annotated tag `nova-v1.0.0` identify that exact verified revision; the public GitHub Release and install command use current `Yazelix` organization paths; Linux CI, Linux cache publication, Darwin cache publication, local flake checks, package build, and an isolated public-tag install pass; the installed product reports Yazelix Nova 1.0.0; and Classic archival refs remain preserved.
notes: Accepted 2026-08-09 at exact revision a5cd038a4acf11d24bca0b328043c61fa1712182. Edge CI 31324770021, Main CI 31325115228, Linux and aarch64-darwin cache publication 31325115209, and Stable CI 31325573340 passed. Local all-system evaluation, all Linux flake checks, package build, isolated checkout install, and isolated public-tag install passed. `github:Yazelix/nova/nova-v1.0.0` resolves exactly to the accepted revision and reports Yazelix Nova 1.0.0. The user explicitly authorized deleting the earlier public release and tag at 55a82ed93090c8d2294bf887ddbc68b678ea9398 and recreating the same v1 identity to eliminate stale repository names and links; any preexisting lock to the earlier revision remains historical.
close_reason: Published the clean canonical Nova 1.0.0 release at a5cd038a with current Yazelix organization identities, exact channel and tag alignment, green Linux and Darwin delivery gates, and successful public-tag installation proof.

title: Stop orphaned asciiquarium after terminal teardown
description:
## Why

Stable could leave asciiquarium-rs orphaned after the Alt Shift S screen popup or its terminal was torn down. The observed process was reparented to PID 1, held deleted PTY descriptors, survived for more than three hours, and consumed 99-101% of one logical CPU. The packaged fork revision c78b76e8 predates upstream beef5b7d, which fixes this exact EOF-terminal signal-loop failure.

## Ownership decision

- cablehead/asciiquarium-rs owns bounded runs and clean exit when its controlling terminal disappears.
- Yazelix Screen owns consuming an exact upstream revision and launching it with the existing duration/any-key contract.
- Main Yazelix owns the exact Screen pin, package integration, installed-runtime verification, and release severity.
- The luccahuguet fork was a temporary contribution path for bounded-run support. Upstream ccdb19a contains that work and beef5b7d adds the lifecycle fix, so Yazelix no longer consumes the fork.
- Do not add a second process supervisor, PTY implementation, Python check, or terminal lifecycle owner to Screen or Main.

## Scope

Pin upstream beef5b7d directly in Yazelix Screen, publish Screen, update Main to that exact revision, and verify ordinary any-key exit, timed welcome exit, focused popup/PTY teardown, whole-window teardown, and repeated open/close behavior. Use a focused disposable teardown probe as release evidence without retaining a duplicate upstream lifecycle test in Yazelix.

## Out of scope

No generic process manager, daemon, Screen redesign, aquarium removal, local mirror of upstream signal handling, or unrelated animation work. A permanent upstream regression test is a separate contribution only if explicitly chosen.
acceptance_criteria:
- A disposable PTY teardown probe reproduces the old pinned orphan/busy-loop failure and passes with upstream beef5b7d.
- Closing the screen popup or its terminal leaves no asciiquarium-rs or yzs descendant after a bounded grace period.
- The three-second welcome exits normally, ordinary any-key exit remains correct, and terminal state is restored.
- Yazelix Screen consumes exact upstream beef5b7d directly; no runtime dependency on the luccahuguet fork or local lifecycle wrapper remains.
- Screen and Main pin exact published revisions; focused child checks, Nix builds, Main flake checks, a temporary profile, installed-runtime refresh, and fresh-session popup dogfood pass.
- No Python/PTTY framework, process wrapper, or duplicate terminal-lifecycle owner is added to Yazelix repositories.
notes:
Implementation evidence 2026-08-03: revalidated orphan PID 234390 as PPID 1 running the old Nix-store asciiquarium with --exit-on-any-key. SIGTERM reproduced the broken handler behavior; SIGKILL removed the orphan. Compared pinned c78b76e8 with upstream beef5b7d: upstream contains the bounded-run contribution at ccdb19a plus setup cleanup, and differs only by the terminal-death fix. The same disposable PTY/process-group probe failed against c78b76e8 and passed against the upstream-backed Screen build. A proposed Screen-side Python regression check was removed after ownership review. Yazelix Screen deb5c8babf295caaaaccaba2e6b5d75c1a9c1f49 pins cablehead/asciiquarium-rs beef5b7dae179937c67f9e1557e02d64be55fa71 directly.

Fresh-session runtime evidence 2026-08-03: fast-forwarded Edge to Main 164acebc77033cdbaea3453405446e5943bcf826 and launched independent session nova-aquarium-teardown-164acebc through the installed Edge package. The real yzpp screen_popup selected asciiquarium-rs. Toggling the popup closed removed both yzs and asciiquarium at the first 50 ms check. Reopening the aquarium and killing the whole Zellij session also removed both at the first 50 ms check. Direct one-second duration and any-key exit passed, terminal state restored, and pgrep found no remaining yzs or asciiquarium process. Main flake check (92 checks), all-system show, package build, temporary-profile install/status, installed Main/Edge refresh, CI run 30829705232, and Linux/Darwin cache run 30829703437 all passed.
close_reason: Completed: Main and Edge consume fixed upstream asciiquarium directly; exact teardown probes, real fresh-session popup and whole-session teardown, local release checks, CI, and Linux/Darwin cache publication passed with no remaining processes.

title: Audit Nova v1 forks and exact pins
description:
## Why

Nova v1 now uses the rebuilt Steel-enabled Helix fork already pinned and dogfooded on edge. Before the final release, inspect every shipped fork and exact child pin, with Helix revision `7e6cd307d00783c16ad4cff99ed71936d34f6572` as an explicit v1 release input. Keep the audit bounded to shipped components and confirmed release defects.

## User-visible contract

The v1 release resolves from published exact child revisions with reviewed retained diffs, no known upstream P0 or P1 fix left behind, and no dependency on dirty, local, floating, private, or experimental state. Yazi file and directory actions reach the current managed Helix instance through the exact rebuilt-fork contract without moving Nova v2 navigation or composition into v1.

## Scope

- Inventory the shipped `yzx -> Mars -> Yazelix Zellij fork` chain and every Yazelix-owned child in the v1 package closure.
- Audit exact Helix runtime revision `7e6cd307d00783c16ad4cff99ed71936d34f6572`, including its reviewed upstream base, retained Rust and Steel delta, license, public availability, package identity, and Main-owned adapter boundary.
- Confirm later child revisions do not need to replace the exact runtime pin merely because the child repository default branch advanced for documentation or CI.
- Review the Zellij, pane-orchestrator, popup, bar, cursor, Mars, and other release-relevant exact pins.
- Record each current pin, reviewed target, upstream relationship, retained fork diff, license, publication state, and verification.
- Move a child only for a confirmed v1 contract, upstream P0 or P1 fix, or release blocker.
- Prefer upstream when no Yazelix-specific contract remains.
- Publish child fixes before updating Main locks.
- Preserve the accepted asciiquarium teardown fix and its exact child pins.
- Carry the rebuilt Helix through installed Linux proof and either fresh macOS bridge proof or an explicitly narrowed macOS interaction claim before v1.

## Boundary

Forest, notify, glyph, zj-radar, tiled-Yazi deletion, attention-owner replacement, and broader Nova v2 composition stay outside this audit. The rebuilt Helix fork is in scope only as the mechanism for the existing v1 Yazi-to-editor contract. Do not run an update-everything sweep, adopt a dependency major, redesign a fork, delete a fork without an ownership decision, or implement session and v2 navigation work here.
acceptance_criteria:
- The asciiquarium terminal-teardown regression and exact child pins remain fixed and verified.
- A v1 inventory names each shipped release-relevant child, current and target revisions, reason, retained delta, upstream status, license, publication state, and proof.
- Main locks the published Helix runtime revision `7e6cd307d00783c16ad4cff99ed71936d34f6572`; the package closure and installed editor identify that revision.
- The audit reviews the rebuilt Helix upstream base, retained Rust/Steel boundary, deleted old-fork machinery, public availability, license, focused child checks, and Main adapter contract.
- Later child documentation or CI commits do not silently replace the exact runtime pin without a release-relevant reason and renewed proof.
- Only children required by current v1 behavior or a confirmed release defect move.
- Each moved child is clean, published, and passes its format, tests, build, license, and repository checks.
- Forest, notify, glyph, zj-radar, tiled-Yazi deletion, attention-owner replacement, and broader v2 composition remain outside the v1 package graph.
- Flake check and all-system show, package build, temporary-profile install, installed-runtime refresh, and focused fresh-session dogfood pass with the accepted exact pins.
- The rebuilt Helix bridge has fresh macOS interaction evidence before v1, or the release explicitly narrows the macOS interaction claim to the evidence actually available.
- Deferred children remain unchanged and the audit records why.
notes:
## Accepted audit state

Audit date: 2026-08-06. Main revision reviewed: 30963c89b444e693fb96b7a59e5ab9327c01dd93 on edge. Pin policy: retain an exact published revision unless current v1 behavior, a confirmed P0 or P1, or a release blocker requires a move. The audit mapped every direct flake input to a real package, source, plugin, schema, or check consumer; no unused direct input was found. Every exact GitHub revision is publicly reachable and every repository is public and unarchived. No pin moves are accepted by this audit.

## Exact closure inventory

- Helix: current and target 7e6cd307d00783c16ad4cff99ed71936d34f6572; public MPL-2.0. The reviewed base is mattwparas/helix steel-event-system at 8d189f46. Five Yazelix commits retain the config-directory seam, package alias, 15-line Steel action module, Steel composition module, and native authenticated transport. The child scorecard measures 711 additions and 4 removals outside documentation, including 19 configuration Rust lines, 54 Steel lines, 384 native transport lines, and focused tests. Old fork machinery is absent. The child default branch is three documentation and CI commits ahead, so the runtime target remains 7e6cd307. Main owns only package composition and the narrow Yazi adapter.
- Mars: current and target 129981b3a5b9f0a9ef1fa60d2742845cb1722db3; public MIT. It is based on Rio v0.4.10 and carries the terminal-owned Nova product delta, measured at 74 files and 8778 additions versus 918 removals from the reviewed Rio base. The child default branch is three documentation, Beads, and test-simplification commits ahead with no shipped runtime reason to move. Rio v0.5.14 is a major renderer and terminal rebase, not a bounded v1 pin update; reassess it after v1 in the Mars owner.
- Zellij: current and target c9e4c246ea47ad06e79f87aca7073fafe89ba8f1 on yazelix_kgp_preview; public MIT. The configured branch head equals the pin. Against the reviewed custom base, the retained fork delta is 24 files, 1584 additions, and 451 removals for Kitty graphics passthrough and cursor placement, Yazelix titles and status hints, permission prompt state, and theme-mode replay. Official v0.44.3 remains the release base. Unreleased upstream work includes native Kitty graphics and may later delete part of the fork, but it is not a released v1 replacement and no current P0 or P1 was found.
- Zellij bar: current and target c4df0d0228a4ed7c9aaa13f985378fc1d78516f6; public Apache-2.0. It is a standalone child that packages the exact zjstatus overlay and the Nova bar templates. Default branch equals the pin.
- Zellij pane orchestrator: current and target for this audit 128b70bb5f1b00755453a8521228ac89626caa86; public, standalone, and behaviorally current. The source has no LICENSE or COPYING file, Cargo.toml has no license field, and GitHub reports NOASSERTION even though the child Nix metadata claims Apache-2.0. This is the sole confirmed release defect and is owned by P1 blocker yazelix-8u5-4-hnv.4. Publish the source license first, then repin only this child.
- Zellij popup: current and target f4c7c875be7a426a8756f5885b032d64326d34cd; public Apache-2.0, standalone, default branch equals the pin.
- Zellij screen: current and target deb5c8babf295caaaaccaba2e6b5d75c1a9c1f49; public Apache-2.0, standalone, default branch equals the pin. The accepted exact revision contains the asciiquarium terminal-teardown repair, whose child and Main proofs are already closed.
- Yazelix cursors: current and target d2d20a2e739f7db76af50ceb9fc279cba9baad7e; public Apache-2.0, standalone, default branch equals the pin.
- Yazi Bistro: current and target 2e4e199c359a1bc753741d7cc492464f0ff6bede; public Apache-2.0 at the repository root with per-flavor source and syntax licenses. It is a standalone catalog owner and default branch equals the pin.
- zjstatus: current and target a9859a94aaa745339a3e7933d97bd9d2777855d4 on the configured Yazelix branch; public MIT. The branch head equals the pin. The retained overlay is 7 files, 388 additions, and 71 removals for the activity pipe, simplification, and host theme. Upstream changes after the fork point are dependency-only, so no v1 move is justified.
- auto-layout.yazi: current and target e24bee9f6dd15ff80eae1b3dc1a6b06ee7e66121; public MIT. The retained fork is three commits and the functional diff is main.lua plus documentation, with 160 additions and 49 removals in main.lua for current Yazi compatibility. The exact fork head is current.
- starship.yazi: current and target 159eaba5b5052bf78ff6cfbfe4e527b946818c82; external, public MIT, exact default head.
- Yazi schemas: current and target c24ee499e7ba84b89fcc7357f6c40aeadc5000a5; external, public MIT. The only later default-branch change is GitHub Actions dependency maintenance.
- Nixpkgs and Home Manager: exact infrastructure revisions 567a49d1913ce81ac6e9582e3553dd90a955875f and f469c79b955609d6a8fdd9e689be76a93b1621d7, both public MIT. Broad channel refresh is excluded because the current closure is green and no v1 defect requires it.

## Proof and publication

- Hosted CI run 31067783488 passed at exact revision 30963c89, covering flake shape, Helix-free evaluation, and focused Linux checks.
- nix flake show --all-systems passed at 30963c89 and exposed the supported Linux and Darwin packages, apps, and checks. This is evaluation evidence, not Darwin runtime proof.
- nix flake check --print-build-logs passed all 13 x86_64-linux checks, including Helix bridge contracts, Zellij sidecar and theme parity, Home Manager, host Yazi, and no-Helix and no-Mars contracts.
- nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs produced /nix/store/shnqd9rjkp71n2x88119iia3fmczl7m6-yazelix.
- An isolated nix profile install resolved exactly edge revision 30963c89, reported Yazelix Nova 1.0.0-beta.4, and yzx status --json succeeded. The installed closure editor reported helix 25.07.1 at 7e6cd307.
- Existing fresh-session maintainer dogfood covers this exact runtime code: Nova edge opened normally, reveal worked, and file and directory opens from both sidebar and popup reached the existing Helix instance. Commits after the dogfooded runtime revision contain planning state only.
- Mars exact-revision Actions prove Linux and macOS child paths; the Windows-native child job failed, but native Windows is not a declared v1 platform. Other children rely on their focused local checks plus the exact Main closure proof where no exact-revision hosted run exists.

## Bounded claims and deferrals

The rebuilt Helix bridge is manually proved on Linux. Darwin flake evaluation, cache evidence, and sustained Nova use support the already declared macOS floor, but there is no fresh manual macOS interaction proof for the rebuilt Helix bridge. Therefore v1 currently makes no claim that Yazi-to-existing-Helix interaction was manually verified on macOS; release may replace this narrow claim only with fresh macOS evidence.

Mars on Rio v0.5, Zellij unreleased upstream Kitty graphics, and broad Nixpkgs or Home Manager refreshes remain unchanged. They are larger child-owner work with no confirmed current v1 P0 or P1. Forest, notify, glyph, zj-radar, tiled-Yazi deletion, attention-owner replacement, and broader Nova v2 composition remain outside the package graph and this audit.
close_reason: Completed the exact v1 closure audit at 30963c89. All shipped inputs are exact, public, reachable, mapped to consumers, and retained unless a release-relevant reason exists. No pin moves are accepted. Linux closure and installed Helix 7e6cd307 are verified; the macOS Helix interaction claim is explicitly narrow. P1 source-license blocker yazelix-8u5-4-hnv.4 owns the sole confirmed release defect and blocks the v1 release task.

title: Wrap the portable Linux Nova archive as an optional AppImage
description:
## Outcome

Offer an optional `x86_64-linux` AppImage by wrapping the already proven portable Nova release tree in a standard AppDir. AppImage owns single-file Linux launch and desktop metadata; it does not own Nova composition.

Impact: LOW to MEDIUM after the direct archive/installer exists. Effort: M. Risk: MEDIUM because FUSE, desktop integration, and CLI ergonomics vary across distributions. Confidence: MEDIUM; user demand should justify it.

## Evidence

- AppImage requires a correct AppDir with an `AppRun` entrypoint and relocatable internal paths: https://docs.appimage.org/packaging-guide/index.html and https://docs.appimage.org/reference/appdir.html
- Nova needs host filesystem, shell, terminal, editor, and agent integration, which makes Flatpak/Snap sandboxing a poor first boundary.
- The portable Linux archive and immutable release assets already provide the only runtime payload this package may consume.

## Scope

- Begin only after the direct `x86_64-linux` archive and shell installer are accepted and AppImage has a distinct user benefit.
- Map the exact portable release root into an AppDir; add only `AppRun`, desktop metadata, and icon/CLI passthrough needed by AppImage.
- Default to the no-Rio `nova enter` contract or a clearly documented CLI passthrough. Do not imply GUI launch until a separate portable Rio artifact exists.
- Test direct and extracted execution because FUSE availability differs across Linux systems.
- Keep desktop integration optional and honest; no updater daemon in the first slice.

## Verification

- Build one AppImage without changing the Nova runtime tree.
- On clean Linux without Nix, run help/status/doctor and a fresh `nova enter` through both direct and extracted execution.
- Verify no runtime path requires `/nix/store`, the AppDir, or the build path after extraction.
- Record FUSE requirements/fallback, artifact identity/hash/size, and tested distributions.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if AppImage needs a second dependency graph, runtime layout, or child-package patch set.
- Stop if the direct archive/installer already satisfies the same users and no concrete single-file/desktop value remains.
- Stop before adding Rio, Flatpak, Snap, auto-update, or broad architecture support.

## Dependency Decision

Use AppImage tooling only after the shared portable archive exists. Keep this P3 and optional; the v2 Nix-free baseline does not depend on it.

title: Install Nova with Homebrew from the portable release archive
description:
## Outcome

Install Nova with `brew install yazelix/tap/nova` by placing the already proven portable release archive under the Homebrew prefix and exposing `nova` plus the `yzx` compatibility alias.

Homebrew owns package-manager metadata, download, activation, upgrade, and uninstall. The Nova release archive owns every runtime binary, plugin, config, asset, notice, and compatibility claim.

Impact: MEDIUM after direct archive installation works. Effort: M. Risk: MEDIUM. Confidence: HIGH in the ownership split and MEDIUM that Homebrew is worth maintaining before user demand is measured.

## Evidence

- Homebrew formulae install into versioned Cellar prefixes, support `libexec`, and can expose wrapper commands: https://docs.brew.sh/Formula-Cookbook
- Bottles generally assume Homebrew default prefixes (`/opt/homebrew`, `/usr/local`, `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew`), so Nova itself must remain prefix-independent: https://docs.brew.sh/FAQ
- The portable archive and release-manifest beads provide the payload and integrity contract; the formula must not recreate `flake.nix` composition.

## Scope

- Start with Apple Silicon macOS only after the public `aarch64-darwin` archive passes relocation, Gatekeeper/signing, and fresh-session proof.
- Use an external Yazelix tap; do not target Homebrew/core initially.
- Keep the formula small: target URL/hash/version, install the archive into `libexec` or the formula prefix, expose `nova` and `yzx`, and run non-GUI tests.
- Use normal `brew upgrade` and `brew uninstall`; preserve Nova user configuration.
- Add Linuxbrew only after the same formula consumes the Linux archive without platform-specific package composition.
- Decide whether upstream archives are installed directly or Homebrew bottles merely mirror the exact same payload. Do not make bottle production a requirement without a measured benefit.

## Verification

- On a clean Apple Silicon Homebrew environment without Nix, install from the local tap and run version/help/status/doctor plus a fresh no-Rio `nova enter` session.
- Verify formula paths can move across Homebrew Cellar versions without embedded prefix or `/nix/store` dependencies.
- `brew audit`, `brew test`, upgrade, and uninstall pass; uninstall removes package-owned files and links but preserves user config.
- The installed artifact identifies the exact Nova release revision and hash.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the formula starts naming individual Nova dependencies or rebuilding the runtime tree.
- Stop if the Darwin release archive is unsigned/unnotarized where required, non-relocatable, or lacks clean-machine proof.
- Stop if publishing a tap requires a new repository or external mutation without explicit user authority.

## Dependency Decision

Use Homebrew only as a frontend over the released archive. Do not make Homebrew a second build source of truth, add a Ruby packaging layer beyond one formula, or require bottles before the direct formula is useful.

title: Evaluate asciiaquarium as a Yazelix screen style
description: Evaluate asciiaquarium as an optional terminal-safe style owned by yazelix-screen rather than copied into Nova runtime code. Check packaging, license, terminal behavior, resize/input/exit semantics, and whether the experience is worth its closure cost.
design: Accepted. yazelix-screen owns the style and launches asciiquarium-rs as a separately packaged GPL-2.0-or-later process; no GPL code is copied or linked into Apache-2.0 yzs. The contribution fork adds generic --duration-seconds and --exit-on-any-key options, preserving upstream defaults. Yazelix consumes exact published child and fork revisions. Rejected: reimplementing the aquarium, linking it as a library, an unbounded timeout wrapper, and a permanent divergent fork.
acceptance_criteria: Record upstream identity, license, package closure, rendering/input/resize behavior, and whether yazelix-screen can own it without copied main code. End with accept/reject. If accepted, create child-owned implementation and Nova consumption beads with a published-child release gate.
notes: Upstream cablehead/asciiquarium-rs v0.1.0 was tested in a PTY: SIGTERM cleanup worked, q/p/r worked, and Space did not exit. Contribution fork c78b76e84cd2c8b0e2f3b4e817e9cb90aee768a2 adds bounded duration and any-key exit while preserving defaults, and ensures its cleanup guard exists before alternate-screen setup so setup errors also restore raw mode. It passed format, Clippy, 14 tests, one-second duration, and key exit checks. Draft upstream PR: https://github.com/cablehead/asciiquarium-rs/pull/1. Incremental cost in the Yazelix Nix package set was measured at about 1.17 MiB because runtime libraries are shared. Resize remains owned by crossterm/upstream. Accept: the experience is distinct, bounded, skippable, and cheap enough.

title: Add truthful agent activity decorations to Nova tabs
description:
## Why

Nova does not currently display agent activity decorations, so the carried-over title and P1 bug framing are stale. The useful feature is to show a compact, truthful busy marker on the tab whose managed agent is working while keeping native Zellij tab names entirely user-owned. Classic already fixed its rename conflict by moving presentation out of native tab names; Nova should reuse that architectural result without assuming its current popup produces the same signal.

## Evidence

- `packaging/bar-render-request.nix:10-23` asks the bar child to package and render its own `zjstatus.wasm`.
- `flake.lock` currently resolves the bar child `zjstatus` input to upstream `dj95/zjstatus@17609e4`; that upstream source has no `tab_activity_pipe_name` or `pipe_tab_activity` implementation.
- The generated Nova layout nevertheless contains `tab_activity_pipe_name`, busy marker `·`, and alert marker `✓` from `yazelix-zellij-bar/presets/yazelix_runtime_bar.template.kdl:19-22`. Those keys are inert with the packaged upstream wasm.
- `../yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator/src/status_bar_cache.rs:34-55,108-135` already produces the all-tab activity snapshot and pushes it to every known zjstatus instance without renaming tabs.
- `../yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator/src/ai_pane_activity_contract.rs:60-77` recognizes spinner-prefixed terminal titles as activity, and `src/ai_pane_activity.rs:61-125` also accepts explicit `register_ai_pane_activity` facts.
- Nova has no `register_ai_pane_activity` producer. Live `zellij action list-panes --json` inspection showed a running `codex resume` popup exposed as the fixed title `agent_popup`.
- `../yazelix-zellij-popup/src/main.rs:298-325` opens a command pane and then calls `rename_pane_with_id` with the configured popup title.
- `../yazelix-zellij/zellij-server/src/panes/terminal_pane.rs:1007-1023` returns a non-empty custom `pane_name` instead of the terminal application title, explaining why Nova masks the spinner title used by the existing detector.
- Classic published the durable presentation pieces in pane-orchestrator `8cea8ec`, bar `7ceee67`, zjstatus fork `524a6bf`, and main integration `75029436`. The fork branch `luccahuguet/zjstatus@yazelix-tab-activity-pipe` still exists.

## User-visible contract

When the managed Nova agent exposes a trustworthy working signal, its tab shows one compact busy decoration. When no trustworthy signal is available, Nova shows no activity decoration rather than equating process lifetime, popup visibility, or focus with model work. The decoration is presentation-only: explicit tab names survive activity updates and remain raw/editable in Zellij rename mode. Existing tab focus, click, create/delete, truncation, fullscreen/sync/floating indicators, and terminal-bell styling remain native zjstatus behavior.

## Scope

In scope:
- Restore or rebase the smallest activity-capable zjstatus tabs-widget extension and make the Yazelix bar package/runtime select a compatible wasm instead of emitting unsupported KDL.
- Keep the pane orchestrator as the sole tab-local activity fact owner and `pipe_tab_activity` producer.
- Establish one truthful activity input for the Nova managed agent popup. Prefer reusing the existing spinner-title contract if popup identity can remain reliable; otherwise prove the smallest explicit signal or Zellij title-seam change.
- Evaluate three bounded signal paths from source and live evidence: preserve terminal-title visibility without losing popup identity; expose the raw terminal application title separately from the custom pane name in the Yazelix Zellij fork; or consume a stable provider event through `register_ai_pane_activity`.
- Scope the first supported signal honestly. Codex spinner-title behavior is sufficient for the first slice; other configured providers get markers only when they expose the same proven contract.
- Correct stale child documentation that still describes native tab-name mutation or claims the upstream-packaged wasm supports activity keys.
- Add a packaged compatibility check so the selected `zjstatus.wasm` and generated activity KDL cannot silently drift apart again.
- Update README LOC scorecard and CHANGELOG when project/runtime files change.

Out of scope:
- Inferring activity from the long-lived agent process, popup visibility, pane focus, or the presence of a Codex subprocess.
- Reintroducing `rename_tab_with_id`, tab-name suffix persistence, a command-widget replacement tab strip, broad pane polling, or a new status-bar implementation.
- Provider-specific compatibility claims without a real working/idle signal.
- The hidden or unfocused-tab clearing regression; that is a separate dependent bead.
- Agent command-center, notifications, popup redesign, or general terminal-title API expansion beyond the smallest demonstrated signal gap.

## Implementation Notes

1. First make a controlled Nova popup produce the same working/idle signal used in Classic and inspect the pane manifest, activity snapshot, and pipe payload.
2. Rebase or validate zjstatus fork `524a6bf` against the currently selected upstream before pinning it. Preserve live `TabInfo.name`, raw rename-mode labels, tab-id keyed activity, JSON containing `::`, click behavior, and truncation.
3. Choose the smallest signal seam that preserves popup identity. If removing the custom rename is considered, prove all popup toggle, displacement, cwd-restart, sidebar interaction, and hidden keep-alive paths still identify the pane.
4. If a Zellij API field is needed, expose the raw terminal title separately; do not overload the user/custom pane name.
5. Keep marker glyph/style configuration in `yazelix-zellij-bar`; keep activity facts and reduction in the pane orchestrator.
6. Add no new production or development crate.

## Verification

- Focused pane-orchestrator tests prove facts are keyed by stable tab id and pipe snapshots never mutate native names.
- Focused zjstatus-fork tests prove busy/idle/alert parsing, live-name precedence over stale payload names, rename-mode raw names, JSON containing `::`, tab movement, truncation, and existing bell behavior.
- Focused popup or Zellij tests prove the selected activity signal remains visible without losing packaged popup identity.
- A package-level check proves the rendered activity keys are paired with an activity-capable `zjstatus.wasm`.
- Relevant child formatting, tests, WASI builds, and Nix builds pass before child publication.
- `nix flake check`, `nix flake show --all-systems`, `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs`, and a temporary-profile install pass.
- After `nix profile upgrade --refresh yazelix`, a fresh multi-tab dogfood pass shows the marker only on the working agent tab and confirms tab rename during activity.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the proposed source cannot distinguish working from an idle interactive agent process.
- Stop if exposing terminal-title activity breaks popup identity, hide/reopen state, cwd retarget restart, or unrelated floating-pane behavior.
- Stop if the renderer path writes activity into `TabInfo.name` or replaces native tab semantics with polling.
- Stop if the old zjstatus fork cannot be rebased narrowly; review the minimal extension against current upstream instead of pinning stale code blindly.
- Stop before claiming support for providers that do not expose a tested activity signal.

## Maintenance Notes

This issue is deliberately reclassified from a P1 bug to a P2 feature. Classic is a reference implementation, not a port target. The durable ownership rule survives: native tab names are user data; activity is a fact; the bar renders the fact.

Effort: M across integration seams. Risk: MEDIUM, concentrated in obtaining a truthful popup signal. Confidence: HIGH about the missing renderer pin and masked-title cause; MEDIUM on the cheapest signal seam until live instrumentation chooses it.

Rejected alternatives: process-lifetime markers, focus-driven markers, tab renaming, broad `list-panes` polling, and a second tab strip.
acceptance_criteria:
- A managed agent with a proven working signal decorates only its own tab with the configured busy marker; idle or unknown agents do not show a false marker.
- Explicit native tab names remain unchanged in Zellij state while activity starts, updates, and ends, and rename mode displays and edits the raw live tab name.
- The packaged bar uses a zjstatus implementation that consumes `pipe_tab_activity`; generated activity KDL is not paired with an upstream wasm that ignores it.
- The selected Nova popup activity source is documented and tested, preserves popup identity/lifecycle, and does not infer work from process lifetime, visibility, or focus.
- Live tab identity, focus, click switching, creation/deletion, movement, truncation, fullscreen/sync/floating indicators, and bell styling remain intact.
- Focused tests cover tab-id keyed snapshots, stale payload names versus live names, JSON protocol framing, rename mode, and the chosen signal seam.
- Child changes are published before lock updates, exact child and main checks pass, the installed runtime is refreshed, and a fresh multi-tab dogfood pass confirms working decoration plus rename-during-activity.
notes: Implemented the activity slice without native tab-name mutation or a Zellij fork. Published popup a13ef50 and 72b898a (preserve and reveal terminal application titles), pane orchestrator 5cd75d4 and 8d4712a (managed-command scoping plus reliable all-plugin activity broadcast), bar facd2e4 (accurate consumer contract), and reused the focused zjstatus extension 524a6bf. Main pins those children, wires the managed agent command marker, preserves the agent terminal title, and checks the packaged wasm for activity support. Focused child tests passed (popup 32, orchestrator 79, zjstatus activity/name/protocol tests), along with child WASI and Nix builds. Main nix flake check, nix flake show --all-systems, nix build .#yazelix, temporary-profile install, and installed-profile refresh passed. Fresh installed two-tab dogfood showed only the working agent tab decorated, preserved dogfood-renamed in native state when renamed during activity, cleared the marker on idle while unfocused, and preserved popup pane identity through hide/reopen. No process-lifetime, focus, visibility, or tab-renaming inference was added.

title: Add semantic config for managed shell integrations
description:
## Why

Yazelix Nova currently initializes Carapace, Zoxide, and Starship inside the managed Nushell runtime by default. That is the right default, but users may eventually need a small supported way to disable or inspect those managed shell integrations without replacing the whole Nushell config or editing packaged files.

## Current Contract

Inside `yzx`-managed Nushell:

- Carapace completions are generated and sourced by default.
- Zoxide init is generated and sourced by default.
- Starship owns the left and right prompt by default.
- Optional user files under `~/.config/yazelix/nu/env.nu` and `config.nu` are layered after packaged config.
- Normal user Nushell config is not loaded by default.

## User-Visible Behavior

A user can use the Yazelix semantic config surface, and later Ratconfig, to inspect and optionally toggle managed shell integrations such as Carapace, Zoxide, and Starship. Defaults preserve the current curated shell behavior.

Possible first settings:

```toml
[shell]
carapace = true
zoxide = true
starship = true
```

Names are illustrative; choose final names only when implementing the contract.

## Scope

In scope:
- Add the smallest semantic config surface for managed Nushell integrations if/when a real need appears.
- Keep defaults equal to current behavior: Carapace, Zoxide, and Starship enabled.
- Route all validation through the shared Yazelix config core.
- Make `runtime/yzx-nu.rs` or its owner consume the settings without loading ambient user shell config.
- Surface the settings in Ratconfig only if the config core owns them.
- Add focused checks for defaults, toggling each integration, and generated Nushell config contents.
- Update README, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG, and LOC scorecard if implemented.

Out of scope:
- Do not add Bash, Zsh, Fish, or arbitrary managed-shell selection in this bead.
- Do not import the user's normal Nushell config.
- Do not build a generic shell plugin manager.
- Do not translate native shell config through Ratconfig.
- Do not add this setting before someone actually needs to disable or inspect an integration.
- Do not weaken the current managed shell reproducibility contract.

## Implementation Notes

1. Prefer booleans over a generic plugin list.
2. Keep generated Nushell config deterministic and easy to test.
3. Preserve `PATH` setup so enabled tools remain available inside managed Nushell.
4. If disabling Starship, define the resulting prompt behavior explicitly before coding.
5. Carapace support remains a curated managed-shell default, not a promise to support every external shell.

## Verification

- Config contract check proves missing settings default to current enabled behavior.
- Check proves disabling Carapace removes the generated Carapace source line and leaves Nushell launch working.
- Check proves disabling Zoxide removes the generated Zoxide source line and leaves Nushell launch working.
- Check proves disabling Starship has a clearly defined prompt result.
- Existing `yzx-nu` checks still prove enabled tools work when defaults are used.
- `nix flake check` if runtime generation changes.
- `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs` if packaged runtime changes.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if this turns into generic shell support.
- Stop if toggles require importing ambient user shell config.
- Stop if the first requested setting is only theoretical and adds config surface without a current user workflow.
notes: Prime-beads review 2026-06-27: defer until there is a concrete user need to disable or inspect managed shell integrations. The bead remains the prerequisite for managed multi-shell selection, but should not appear as ready feature work while the toggle need is theoretical.

title: Add an Alt Shift S manual screen popup
description:
## Why

A single deliberate action should open the existing Yazelix random visual as a transient full-size workspace cover without creating another renderer, idle watcher, or retained process. Because config, agent, Git, menu, and sidebar actions already use one managed-key pipeline, the screen action should join that same remappable surface rather than becoming a fixed exception.

## User-visible contract

From an ordinary pane, the configured keybindings.screen chord opens one transient 100%-width/100%-height managed popup running the packaged Yazelix screen random selector. The packaged default is Alt Shift S. Every new invocation starts a new random selection. Ordinary screen input exits, removes the popup, and restores the prior focus and workspace state. This is a visual cover, not a session lock or privacy boundary.

Users can remap keybindings.screen for newly launched sessions. The setting uses the same key syntax, case-insensitive collision validation, status/doctor reporting, Ratconfig editing, Home Manager serialization, and generated Zellij replacement path as other managed actions. General support for leaving actions unmapped is separate bead yazelix-5vl-lvj.

## Ownership

- yazelix-screen remains the sole renderer, style inventory, random selector, input/exit owner, and package owner.
- Yazelix owns the built-in popup, managed key setting/default, validation, generated binding, key reference, documentation, and runtime integration.
- The generic popup child remains unchanged and owns generic geometry, transient lifecycle, and focus restoration.

## Scope

In scope: one built-in transient screen popup, keybindings.screen with Alt Shift S default, managed-key collision validation and runtime replacement, key reference/config UI/Home Manager/status integration, generated-package contracts, documentation, changelog, and LOC scorecards.

Out of scope: idle activation, authentication or security claims, retained hidden state, new styles or renderers, configurable random pools, keyless managed actions, changing Alt Shift F or direct yzx screen behavior, and child-repository changes.

## Implementation decision

The popup invokes the pinned yzs random binary directly. config.kdl is an input to the yzx package, so invoking packaged yzx from that config would create a flake construction cycle. yzx screen delegates to this exact renderer, so direct store-backed argv preserves the existing behavior without a wrapper or ambient PATH lookup.
acceptance_criteria:
- keybindings.screen is a documented managed key setting with packaged default Alt Shift S and next-launch application.
- A custom valid chord replaces the generated screen popup binding and the default binding is absent.
- The setting participates in canonical syntax and collision validation against managed, custom-popup, and fixed packaged chords.
- The action opens exactly one transient 100%x100% popup running pinned yzs random argv; ordinary input exits and restores prior workspace focus/state.
- Status, doctor, Ratconfig, Home Manager, key-reference parity, packaged defaults, and generated contracts include the setting.
- Direct yzx screen, menu access, existing popup keys, and Alt Shift F remain unchanged.
- No unmapping syntax, idle automation, keep-alive state, new renderer, new setting beyond keybindings.screen, or security claim is added.
notes: Implemented the screen popup and remappable key through the existing canonical managed-key pipeline. Verification passed: pinned yzx-config tests, runtime/generated contracts including a custom Ctrl Shift S binding with no retained Alt Shift S bind, key-reference parity, Home Manager, nix flake check, nix flake show --all-systems, nix build .#yazelix, temporary-profile install, and installed-profile upgrade/inspection. Direct path-based cargo test remains unsuitable while the neighboring Ratconfig worktree is on its unfinished v6 API; the pinned Nix yzx check ran all 48 yzx-config tests successfully. GUI dogfood was not launched because repository instructions require an explicit user request.
close_reason: Implemented and verified the transient random screen popup with remappable keybindings.screen defaulting to Alt Shift S.

title: Decide whether global Alt z earns its orchestration cost
description:
## Decision

Decide whether one global `Alt z` accelerator is worth the orchestration needed to summon the persistent Yazi popup and start its existing zoxide workspace picker from any focus state.

## User value

The current reliable path is `Alt Shift Y`, then Yazi-owned `Alt z`. A global `Alt z` would compress that frequent action to one chord. Keeping the explicit two-step path as the underlying composition is acceptable; duplicate entry paths are not themselves a defect.

## Evidence and constraint

The v1 prototype required cross-process receiver identity, startup registration, queueing, and popup replacement recovery. Dogfood exposed dead queues and startup churn. It was rejected for v1 because the implementation was brittle, not because the interaction was bad.

## Decision boundary

Accept implementation only if one boring mechanism can reuse the existing Yazi-owned action without terminal key synthesis, a second workspace/root owner, stale receiver queues, or popup replacement churn. Otherwise retain the explicit two-step path and close this decision. A separate chord is allowed for comparison but should not be added merely to avoid solving interception semantics.

## Scope

This issue owns product and mechanism evaluation only. Recheck current Zellij, yzpp, pane-orchestrator, and Yazi capabilities; preserve the previous negative runtime evidence; compare the one-chord benefit against the remaining state and recovery cost. Any accepted implementation receives a separate bounded issue.

## Verification

A positive decision must name the sole action owner and prove the proposed mechanism from editor, shell, tiled Yazi, visible popup, hidden popup, and sidebar-hidden states, including cancel, startup, and process-replacement failures. A negative decision records what evidence would make the idea worth revisiting.
acceptance_criteria:
- The decision compares global `Alt z` with the current `Alt Shift Y` then `Alt z` path using current source and runtime evidence.
- The prior queueing, registration, identity, and popup-churn failures remain explicit constraints.
- A positive result has one Yazi-owned action path and no key synthesis, duplicate workspace owner, or brittle receiver queue.
- The maintainer explicitly accepts or rejects the complexity tradeoff before implementation planning.
- No runtime, keymap, popup, or package change is made in this decision issue.
notes: Deferred after v1 dogfood, not permanently rejected. The maintainer considers the interaction valuable but is unsure whether one fewer chord justifies the cross-process complexity. Revisit only against current native/plugin capabilities.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Reopened: The maintainer clarified that global Alt z remains a valuable idea deferred after difficult v1 prototypes, not a permanently rejected feature.

title: Implement and dogfood the minimum v1 session contract
description:
## Accepted implementation

Nova v1 delegates session lifecycle to packaged Zellij and keeps one session owner. Plain `yzx enter` / `yzx launch` create fresh sessions; `--session NAME` creates a fresh named session; `attach NAME` attaches a live full-name target without reapplying the managed layout. The native `Ctrl-Alt-o`, then `w`, manager switches live sessions and type-to-create starts a new session with the Yazelix layout.

The generated config selects `default_layout "layout"` and the packaged layout directory. Runtime projection rewrites both the active layout file and its directory when appearance, shell, or widgets materialize a state-owned layout. `layout_dir` is integration-owned and rejected from the user Zellij sidecar.

Session names are immutable in the supported contract. Mars owns terminal-window creation, Zellij owns session mechanics and PTYs, yzx owns public composition and generated layout defaults, the orchestrator owns canonical workspace state, and the existing bridge owns Yazi-to-Helix routing.
design: Use native Zellij arguments and configuration only. Do not add a registry, custom picker, daemon, PTY owner, rename layer, restore layer, or session framework. Full names are the supported attach surface; unique-prefix matching and structural resurrection remain upstream Zellij behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Plain and named creation, full-name live attach, native switching, and native type-to-create follow the approved contract.
- The Yazelix layout is selected for creation and is not reapplied during attach or switching.
- Detach/reattach and switching preserve tabs, panes, processes, working directories, and Yazi-to-existing-Helix routing.
- Generated-config checks cover the default layout, packaged and materialized layout directories, command help, and sidecar ownership. Manual isolated-runtime checks cover missing attach and live-name collision; ambiguous prefixes, stale metadata, and already-attached policy remain Zellij-owned behavior outside the Yazelix test contract.
- Fresh isolated-session dogfood covers plain and named creation, live attach, native type-to-create, switching, detach/reattach, Yazi-to-Helix open, and clean teardown.
- Flake check/show/build and exact-candidate temporary-profile installation pass. The user profile can consume this working-tree candidate after it is committed and published on Edge.
- No fresh alias, registry, custom picker, daemon, session framework, rename support, or sharing/resurrection scope is introduced.
notes:
Candidate: edge HEAD e37444869c3c5654ebd8675f244bbe04b06e11d5 plus this issue's uncommitted working-tree diff; exact package /nix/store/vjdp30iwjhqzzb1hwknxjbksc6wlxiwi-yazelix.

Mechanical proof on x86_64-linux: `nix flake check --print-build-logs` (122 checks), `nix flake show --all-systems`, `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs --print-out-paths`, focused contracts build, `git diff --check`, Rust formatting checks, and LOC scorecard (27,046) pass.

Delivery proof: the exact candidate installed to an isolated Nix profile and identified `Yazelix Nova (1.0.0-beta.4)`. Fresh isolated sessions accepted plain and named creation, live attach, native manager switch and type-to-create, detach/reattach, Yazi `README.md` open into the existing Helix pane, missing attach failure, live-name collision failure, and explicit teardown. Test directories were moved to trash.

`nix profile upgrade --refresh yazelix` returned success but matched no profile entry because the installed entries are named `yazelix-edge` and `yazelix-main`; neither can contain this uncommitted candidate. The isolated exact-candidate install is the delivery proof for this revision. Refresh the user Edge entry after commit/push.

Accepted P3 limitation inherited from the decision: plugin-bound agent toggle and `Alt h` / `Alt l` can briefly stall after switching into a session with no connected client; native `Alt 1-9` remains responsive and recovers the bindings.

title: Reassess Yazi materializer extraction with a second consumer
description:
## Why

The bounded Yazi materializer may eventually serve main Yazelix or another runtime, but extracting it before a second consumer would add release, pinning, API, and coordination overhead without deleting any real owner. Reassess only after the local crate's contract is stable and another consumer is ready to adopt it.

## Evidence

- `ARCHITECTURE.md:123-142`: separate repositories require independent users, release cadence, a stable artifact/API, low product coupling, and deletion of a real local owner.
- The local materializer implementation bead establishes a product-coupled config-home contract first.
- Main Yazelix currently owns a broader independent Yazi materialization surface; theoretical reuse is not adoption.

## Decision Criteria

Extract only if all are true:

- A concrete second consumer will call the same input/output contract.
- The second consumer deletes or relinquishes its existing materialization owner.
- The CLI/library contract is stable enough to version independently.
- Runtime-specific paths and policy can be provided without compatibility adapters or duplicate owners.
- Cross-repo release/pin updates are cheaper than atomic local changes.

Keep local if any are true:

- Yazelix Nova remains the only caller.
- Main Yazelix still requires broader import/migration behavior.
- Extraction needs Nova-specific path shims.
- Changes still need to land atomically with `yzx-yazi`.

## Scope

In scope when reactivated:
- Inspect all current callers and the local crate API/CLI.
- Identify the concrete second consumer and the owner it will delete.
- Compare local-crate versus shared-repo release costs.
- Decide keep local or extract.
- If extracting, create implementation beads with exact repository, artifact, API, and migration boundaries.
- Update ARCHITECTURE with the decision.

Out of scope:
- Do not extract code during this decision bead.
- Do not create a generic Yazi configuration framework.
- Do not add compatibility adapters for hypothetical consumers.
- Do not make extraction block power-user functionality.

## Verification

- `rg -n "yzx-yazi-config|yzx-yazi" .` and equivalent searches in the proposed consumer should identify every real caller.
- If no second consumer exists, close with a keep-local decision and no code changes.
- If extraction is selected, the follow-up plan must name the deleted owner and independent verification commands.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop immediately if no concrete second consumer exists.
- Stop if the proposed consumer cannot delete its current owner.
- Stop if the API remains coupled to Yazelix Nova paths or atomic runtime changes.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort: S decision. Risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH.

Current recommendation: keep the crate local. Rejected: extraction based only on possible future reuse.
notes: The bounded power-user Yazi outcome is complete. This remains deferred as an independent architecture decision and should reactivate only when a concrete second consumer can delete an existing owner.

title: Decide which Nova settings may apply live
description:
## Decision

Determine which current Nova settings, if any, should apply to an already-running session. This bead chooses the contract only; it does not authorize a broad live-apply implementation.

## Scope

- Inventory candidate settings already present in the canonical config model.
- Classify each candidate as safely live, next-session, package-time, or rejected.
- Name the native owner, trigger, observable result, failure behavior, and current/next-session consistency rule for every accepted candidate.
- Prefer existing owner-native reload or command surfaces. Reject polling, file watchers, duplicate Ratconfig state, and cross-owner reconstruction.
- Rank only high-value candidates whose live behavior is materially better than the current next-session contract.
- Obtain maintainer approval for one bounded first implementation slice, then create or update a separate implementation bead.

## Boundaries

Do not implement settings in this decision bead, promise universal live reload, add a general watcher or daemon, duplicate configuration representation, or make package/session-scoped values appear live.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every reviewed candidate is classified as safely live, next-session, package-time, or rejected with its single owner and reason.
- Each accepted live candidate has an explicit trigger, observable result, failure behavior, and rule for agreement with the next session.
- The decision identifies the smallest high-value first slice and records meaningful rejections.
- The maintainer explicitly accepts or rejects that first slice before implementation planning.
- No runtime, config, watcher, daemon, polling loop, or duplicate Ratconfig state is added by this decision bead.
- Any accepted implementation is owned by a separate bounded bead and uses existing native owner surfaces.
notes:
Accepted planning direction, 2026-08-23:

- Keep this as a bounded decision, not a promise of universal live reload.
- Existing useful lifetimes already fit their owners: appearance and selected Zellij fields apply live; shell and Atuin apply to new panes or shells; editor and open logging apply to new opens; Starship applies to new prompts; Yazi and Helix apply to their next managed process.
- The strongest remaining candidate is popup geometry/configuration because the pinned yzpp already consumes Zellij's native PluginConfigurationChanged event. Evaluate projection into the active runtime config before proposing any new watcher.
- Managed keybindings and bar widgets remain secondary candidates and require owner-native reload proof.
- Welcome settings, mutation of an already-running agent process, polling, a daemon, and a general Nova watcher are rejected.
- Any accepted slice receives a separate implementation Bead.

title: Evaluate bounded host-tool sourcing after the Nova beta
description:
## Why

GitHub issue #584 was a concrete user request to omit selected bundled leaf tools, use host-managed versions, reduce duplicate Nix closure size, and avoid Yazelix shadowing the user’s preferred toolchain. Classic implemented that request through #585 with `runtime_tool_sources`, `lib.mkYazelix`, a package builder, runtime-tool registry/manifest, and doctor policy. Nova intentionally does not carry that architecture, but the underlying user problem deserves a fresh evaluation after the canonical beta rather than being forgotten.

This is a Nova-native product decision. It does not promise to restore the Classic API or implementation.

## Irreducible User Outcomes

Evaluate these separately:

1. **Command preference:** selected integrations invoke the host-managed command instead of Nova’s packaged binary.
2. **Closure reduction:** the selected package and its unique dependencies are absent from the realized Nova closure.
3. **Failure clarity:** missing or incompatible host tools fail visibly and actionably.
4. **Reproducibility:** the default package remains complete and deterministic; opting out is explicit.

A solution that only changes PATH precedence does not satisfy closure reduction. A solution that only omits packages without defining command/failure behavior does not satisfy host-tool sourcing.

## Evidence

- https://github.com/luccahuguet/yazelix/issues/584 records the user request and a brittle placeholder-package workaround.
- https://github.com/luccahuguet/yazelix/issues/585 records the broader Classic implementation.
- The requester explicitly valued the shipped result and intended to try it.
- Main decision `yazelix-slim-runtime-boundaries-7ej8l.5.3` removes the Classic builder/registry surface from Nova v1 and requires this loss to be explicit.
- `the completed staging work` freezes the slim v1 Nix/Home Manager API and must not absorb this evaluation before beta.
- Current Nova packaging embeds direct store paths and one complete runtime package, so Classic host-source modes cannot be copied mechanically.

## Timing

Run after `yazelix-8u5-3-j8h` publishes the canonical Nova beta. Use actual beta closure measurements, package references, user feedback, and the final `yzx run`/doctor/environment behavior. This bead does not block beta or stable v1 by default. If the evaluation discovers a P0/P1 adoption blocker, explicitly revise the stabilization graph rather than silently expanding this bead.

## Options To Compare

- Keep the fixed complete package and whole-package Home Manager override only.
- Prefer host commands for a very small allowlist while accepting no closure savings.
- Add bounded build-time omission for a very small allowlist of leaf tools, with one Nix owner and one generated runtime fact source.
- Split genuinely optional integrations into independently installed packages without a general tool registry.
- Publish a documented custom-package recipe outside the supported module/API.
- Reintroduce a generalized Classic-style builder/registry. Treat this as the high-cost baseline to beat, not the default.

Candidate tools must be leaf integrations, not bootstrap/runtime owners. Mars, Zellij, Nushell, graphics wrappers, core utilities, and package-owned helpers are excluded unless a separate architecture decision proves otherwise.

## Questions

- Which tools dominate unique Nova closure size after shared dependencies are accounted for?
- Which packaged tools currently shadow real user-managed commands?
- Can one small allowlist solve the demonstrated use cases without a generic registry?
- Can doctor/runtime consume one generated fact source without duplicating Nix policy in Rust?
- Does Home Manager need a first-class option, or is a whole-package/custom-package path sufficient?
- How does the design behave on Darwin as well as Linux?
- How many beta users actually request this after seeing Nova’s package size and behavior?

## Acceptance Criteria

- Measure the complete Nova package closure and unique marginal closure for plausible leaf candidates on at least the primary Linux system; evaluate Darwin constraints even if exact closure measurement is unavailable.
- Re-read #584/#585 and collect any Nova beta feedback rather than treating Classic architecture as the requirement.
- Compare the options above against LOC/ownership, Nix evaluation cost, closure savings, command precedence, doctor behavior, platform support, and failure modes.
- Record one decision: keep fixed package, document a custom-package escape hatch, accept one bounded host-source slice, or defer with a concrete evidence threshold.
- If accepted, define an exact tool allowlist, one source of truth, Home Manager/flake shape, diagnostics, package impact, focused verification, and create a separate implementation bead.
- If rejected, explain the user-facing alternative honestly and state what future evidence would reopen the decision.
- Do not change source, public API, or stable-release dependencies in this decision bead.

## Dependency Decision

No crates or package changes belong in this evaluation. A future implementation must record production/dev crates, in-house logic, and packaging impact separately. Default bias: Nix/std and one generated fact source; reject frameworks and duplicate registries.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the work starts copying Classic `runtime_tool_sources`, `mkYazelix`, manifests, or validators before proving they are necessary.
- Stop if a proposal claims closure savings without measuring unique retained references.
- Stop if host preference can silently select an incompatible tool.
- Stop if beta/stable scope expands without explicit maintainer approval.

Effort: M decision. Risk: MED/HIGH because package composition and PATH semantics affect reliability. Confidence: HIGH that evaluation is warranted; intentionally undecided on implementation.
notes: Decision accepted 2026-07-21 from GitHub #672 and maintainer review. Accept one bounded host-Yazi slice only. Publish the complete package family yazelix[-no-mars][-no-helix][-no-yazi], with no runtime compatibility aliases. Home Manager continues selecting programs.yazelix.package; host tools remain user-owned. no-yazi removes the pkgs.yazi store reference, resolves one yazi/ya pair from the effective runtime PATH, rejects a missing or mismatched pair, warns but continues when the matching pair differs from the Nova-tested version, routes managed Yazi launches through yzx-yazi, and leaves optional preview dependencies to the host installation. Current runtime-no-helix measurement: 1,180,113,400-byte closure; Yazi has 426,169,208 unique NAR bytes across 131 paths. Classic registry/builder and generic host-tool options remain rejected.
close_reason: Accepted a bounded Nova-native host-Yazi package slice with explicit package outputs, measured closure savings, one runtime resolution owner, and no Classic registry or builder.

title: Validate Android access to existing Codex sessions
description:
## Contract — MOBILE-CODEX-OBSERVATION-001

Consumer: the user's Android phone checking existing Codex sessions on the Linux development host. Opening a session must show current host conversation state; reopening after phone sleep or network reconnection must catch up without a duplicate conversation or stale snapshot. Reading a session must not interrupt or fork desktop work. No Nova mobile app, package, or parallel session-state owner is introduced.

The user selected a polished phone experience and authorized retrying Kittylitter if current evidence supports it. This expands the previous SSH-only validation into validating an existing native client for Codex observation. Nova's headless yzx enter/Zellij attach remains the existing terminal fallback; its broader mobile terminal validation is not claimed by a Codex-only proof.

## Bounded scope

Inspect current upstream and installed versions, repair the existing Kittylitter host setup when necessary, and verify host session reads and reconnection against the actual running Codex environment before user Android dogfood. Prefer a maintained released client and its native connection path. Preserve existing pairing/configuration and desktop sessions. Record any inability to follow live desktop sessions honestly instead of inventing a sync service or silently switching session ownership.

## Acceptance

The user can check an existing Codex conversation from Android, see a later desktop update in that same conversation, and recover current state after background/foreground and reconnection. Record exact host/client versions and distinguish scripted host proof from phone proof. If the chosen client cannot meet this contract, report the limiting mechanism and the smallest supported alternative.
acceptance_criteria: Existing Codex conversation is current on Android, follows a desktop update without a fork, and catches up after phone sleep and reconnection. Host build, connection identity, installed versions, and manual phone evidence are recorded. No change to Nova runtime packaging or desktop session ownership is implied.
notes:
State: existing Kittylitter host installation repaired; Android acceptance remains pending. This is a Linux host setup change outside Nova packaging; no Nova runtime code or dependency changed.

User direction: Android; previous Kittylitter sessions appeared stale; wants a great solution and authorized another Kittylitter trial. The current scope is checking existing Codex conversations, with freshness after reconnect and no fork/interruption of desktop work. Ordinary Nova/Zellij mobile SSH validation remains a separate unproved surface within the original broader mobile direction.

Concrete local defect: kittylitter.service pointed to a removed binary under the temporary npm _npx cache and was repeatedly failing with systemd 203/EXEC (9,695 restarts first observed; 9,712 when stopped). Stopped the failed service, verified the official 0.3.6 Linux release checksum (095bded5c62495873b7b930f54d7e37bd36e387188d8f10cd26664ce0a70eafd), installed it at ~/.local/share/kittylitter/releases/0.3.6, linked ~/.local/bin/kittylitter, and used the native install command to point the existing enabled user service at that permanent path. Service is active/running and the restart counter stayed at 9,712 during checks. ~/.config/kittylitter/host.toml, including the existing pairing token, is byte-identical to the pre-repair backup. Backups are private under ~/.local/state/kittylitter/setup-backups/20260905.

Versions and ownership: released Kittylitter 0.3.6 pins Alleycat 417f2a9fe38cbed63754f0af7df61f32ec3034e6. Native Codex CLI and managed app-server both report 0.153.2. The bridge uses Codex's native managed app-server/proxy; the first probe starts that backend on demand. No custom transcript watcher, sync service, alternate Codex binary, or mobile app was built. The npm latest tag is still 0.3.4, so an unqualified npm update would not install the verified GitHub release.

Host proof: kittylitter probe through the same Iroh/WebSocket path used by a paired phone successfully lists existing sessions and reads the current Nova thread with includeTurns=true. Its output includes the user's current Kittylitter request and assistant updates made after repair. A second connection using the same private client identity reads the later phone-test request, proving fresh persisted conversation reads across reconnect. Raw logs are private under /tmp/nova-mobile-kittylitter; source excerpts and checksum artifacts are there too.

Proof limit: thread/read from the separate managed backend labels the running CLI conversation notLoaded and its unfinished persisted turn interrupted. This proves transcript freshness, not a live event subscription or accurate running status for an independently owned CLI session. Current mobile source uses thread/resume to attach a listener and resubscribes on reconnect; Android open-session updates, sleep/wake, and same-thread desktop continuation still need actual phone proof. Do not claim those pass from the host read probe.

Phone handoff requested: update/open Android KittyLitter, reuse the existing paired computer entry, open the Nova conversation, confirm that the service-repair message is visible, and report the app version. Then check a later desktop update and background/foreground or network reconnection. Existing LAN and Tailscale duplicates should not be used simultaneously: upstream #66 still reports split thread identity for that setup.

References: https://github.com/0xSero/litter/releases/tag/v0.3.6 ; https://github.com/0xSero/litter/issues/127 (old websocket mismatch closed after expanded conformance proof); https://github.com/0xSero/litter/issues/175 (hydration/reconnect changed in 1.6.0); https://github.com/0xSero/litter/issues/66 (duplicate server identities remains open). Official ChatGPT Remote currently documents Mac/Windows desktop hosts and does not provide a direct Linux CLI mobile setup; Happy requires its wrapper to launch/own Codex sessions and has not been accepted as an existing-desktop-session viewer.

title: Evaluate Yazi themes and flavors in Nova
description: Determine whether Nova's managed native Yazi files already provide a clear theme and flavor workflow and identify the smallest remaining user-visible gap. Preserve native Yazi ownership through theme.toml, package.toml, Ratconfig file actions, and Home Manager text/source passthroughs. Do not add a second theme registry or broad materializer.
acceptance_criteria: Test installation and activation of a representative Yazi flavor with writable and Home Manager-owned Nova config. Document the exact workflow and ownership boundary. Close as already supported if current surfaces are sufficient; otherwise create one focused implementation bead for the demonstrated gap.
notes: Validated 2026-07-14. Writable flow: installed yazi-rs/flavors:catppuccin-mocha with packaged Ya 26.5.6 into ~/.config/yazelix/yazi; package.toml locked rev 4770a34, Nova materialized the flavor/theme/package files, and Yazi debug reported catppuccin-mocha for dark and light. Home Manager flow: the flake check links a store-backed example.yazi through generic xdg.configFile, materializes it with the existing yzx-yazi-config owner, and Yazi accepts the selected flavor. Demonstrated gap: packaged ya was not resolvable through yzx run. Fixed by mapping literal ya to the existing version-matched YZX_YA path; no theme registry, catalog, importer, or materializer abstraction was added. Documented writable and Home Manager ownership. Checks passed: cargo test for yzx-yazi-config, home_manager, nix flake show --all-systems, nix build .#yazelix, temporary profile install, live package listing, and nix flake check. Classic asset bundle, random selectors, semantic theme setting, importer, and asset renderer remain rejected for Nova.
close_reason: Native Yazi flavors are supported in writable and Home Manager-owned Nova config; the packaged ya workflow is exposed and documented.

title: Ship one Nix-free installation path for Nova v2
description:
## Outcome

Nova v2 offers one supported installation path that does not require Nix on the user machine, while Nix remains the deterministic build and composition owner.

The selected first vertical slice is one managed Helix/Yazi, no-Rio `x86_64-linux` portable archive, immutable release assets, and a versioned POSIX shell installer. It proves `nova enter` in the user's current terminal. The `yzx` command remains a compatibility alias. Darwin, Homebrew, AppImage, and full Rio distribution evolve from the same artifact contract after this slice rather than becoming simultaneous v2 blockers.

- Consumer: a user who wants Nova without adopting Nix.
- Trigger: install a published Nova version through the selected Nix-free frontend.
- Observable result: the installed runtime uses its packaged binaries, plugins, configuration, and assets without a target-side Nix installation or live `/nix/store`.
- Failure behavior: integrity, compatibility, installation, and startup failures are explicit and leave the previous installed version and user state usable.
design:
One owner and one frontier:

1. Define the portable runtime-root and artifact manifest contract.
2. Prove one `x86_64-linux` no-Rio archive on clean Nix-free systems.
3. Publish immutable archives, checksums, notices, manifest, and provenance.
4. Install that artifact with a small POSIX shell frontend.
5. Extend the same contract to `aarch64-darwin`, then let optional Homebrew/AppImage frontends wrap it.

Nix remains the release factory. Frontends place/select artifacts and never reproduce package composition. `nix bundle`, `nix-portable`, and `nix-community/nix-bundle` are rejected as the final contract because they are Linux-only and preserve Nix/store virtualization. cargo-dist is a design reference, not a dependency, until it demonstrably removes more lifecycle code than it adds.
acceptance_criteria:
- One portable runtime-root contract owns binaries, libraries, plugins, configuration, assets, notices, path resolution, and artifact metadata.
- A clean supported `x86_64-linux` machine with no Nix installation and no `/nix/store` mount can install an immutable no-Rio release and run `nova --version`, help, status/doctor, and a fresh `nova enter`; `yzx` behaves as the compatibility alias.
- The no-Rio `nova launch` surface gives its existing clear unavailable diagnostic; GUI launch is not falsely required from a terminal-free payload.
- No executable, interpreter, loader entry, symlink, plugin/config path, or invoked runtime path requires a live `/nix/store`.
- The published artifact has an exact version/revision, checksum, machine-readable target manifest, redistribution notices, and verifiable build provenance.
- Installation is user-owned, atomic, versioned, supports an exact-version rollback path and clean uninstall, and preserves user configuration and the prior version on failure.
- Installation frontends consume the one release artifact contract and contain no Nova package-composition policy.
- Nix packages and existing Linux/Darwin gates remain green as the reference build path.
- Every claimed platform has installed-artifact and fresh-session evidence from the exact released archive; compilation and cross-evaluation alone are not support proof.
notes: Research decision recorded 2026-08-28. The v2 baseline is the Linux no-Rio archive plus POSIX installer, not every packaging format. Darwin is the next platform extension because Nova already builds there and Homebrew depends on it. Homebrew and AppImage remain optional wrappers; Omarchy remains a downstream compatibility proof. Full Rio archive distribution is deferred until the terminal runtime spine is proven because graphics dependencies, desktop integration, and Apple app signing/notarization add a separate boundary.

title: Define the relocatable Nova runtime contract
description:
## Outcome

Define one portable runtime-root contract that Nix can assemble and every Nix-free frontend can consume without reconstructing Nova.

- Consumer: the Nova launcher, release workflow, shell installer, and later Homebrew/AppImage wrappers.
