- Trigger: packaging the managed no-Rio Nova variant for use outside the Nix store.
- Observable result: one versioned directory tree owns executable discovery, plugins, configuration, assets, dynamic libraries, notices, and artifact metadata through paths relative to the runtime root.
- Failure behavior: packaging fails when an executable path, symlink, loader path, plugin URL, or required asset escapes the root or requires a live /nix/store.
- Surviving owner: flake packaging remains the composition owner; installers only place and select an already composed artifact.

Impact: HIGH. Effort: M. Risk: HIGH because the current closure is large and path substitution is pervasive. Confidence: HIGH that this contract is the prerequisite; MEDIUM on the final relocation mechanism until the inventory is complete.

## Evidence

- `README.md:65-67` says Nova currently requires Nix; no-Rio already defines the terminal-free `enter` surface.
- `flake.nix:682-839` injects absolute package paths into wrappers, Zellij config, and the Rust launcher.
- `flake.nix:862-885` assembles the top-level package with symlinks into separate store outputs rather than one relocatable root.
- The current `yazelix-no-rio` package measures about 1.5 GiB across 633 closure paths, has 22 direct references, and contains 46 `/nix/store` matches in installed command/config/layout/libexec surfaces. The minimal no-Rio/no-Helix/no-Yazi closure is still about 857 MiB across 199 paths. These measurements make this a relocation and composition problem, not an installer-script problem.
- Official Homebrew formula guidance installs payloads below a versioned prefix and supports `libexec`, but does not relocate arbitrary Nix closures: https://docs.brew.sh/Formula-Cookbook
- Official AppImage guidance starts from a correct AppDir and warns against hard-coded paths: https://docs.appimage.org/reference/appdir.html
- Official `nix bundle` can run outside the store, but its documented bundler is Linux-only: https://nix.dev/manual/nix/2.24/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-bundle
- `nix-portable` and `nix-community/nix-bundle` virtualize `/nix/store` with Linux namespaces, bubblewrap, or proot instead of removing the runtime dependency: https://github.com/DavHau/nix-portable and https://github.com/nix-community/nix-bundle

## Scope

In scope:

- Start with exactly one payload: managed Helix + managed Yazi + no Rio. Do not reproduce the full Nix variant matrix in release archives.
- Inventory every executable, interpreter, dynamic library, plugin/WASM, config template, runtime asset, font requirement, host command, license, and generated absolute path needed by `nova help`, diagnostics, and `nova enter`.
- Define a stable runtime-root layout with `bin`, `libexec`, `lib`, `share`, and metadata only where each directory has a current consumer.
- Define how the launcher discovers its root from its own executable path and how child commands receive that root. Runtime configuration must not infer package paths independently.
- Define which tools are bundled and which are explicit host prerequisites. Missing host capabilities must produce owned diagnostics.
- Define a small artifact manifest containing schema version, Nova version/channel/revision, target triple, payload variant, entrypoints, compatibility floor, and file/checksum identity needed by release/install consumers.
- Choose the relocation mechanism per platform seam: relative executable/root paths in Nova-owned code; patched ELF interpreter/RPATH only where needed on Linux; `@loader_path`/`@rpath` install names where needed on Darwin.
- Add the cheapest build-time inventory check capable of rejecting escaping symlinks, executable configuration references, and dynamic loader dependencies.
- Record redistribution and notice inputs for the complete selected closure so release packaging has one source of truth.

Out of scope:

- No shell installer, Homebrew formula, AppImage, GUI/Rio bundle, auto-updater, target matrix, or new package manager in this decision.
- No requirement that the portable artifact be built without Nix.
- No general-purpose Nix closure relocator and no copying of Nix package composition into scripts.

## Verification

- Produce a checked-in contract or executable package check that names the runtime root owner, layout, manifest fields, host prerequisites, and target-specific seams.
- Generate an inventory for the exact no-Rio candidate and account for every runtime-loaded path and direct store reference.
- Demonstrate on a fixture that moving the root does not change path resolution and that an escaping symlink or `/nix/store` runtime path fails the check.
- `nix flake check` and both Linux and Darwin package evaluation remain green when the shared packaging contract changes.
- `git diff --check` passes.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the proposal requires a second package-composition owner outside the flake.
- Stop if a supposedly portable design still depends on mounting or emulating `/nix/store`.
- Stop before adding a dependency unless it owns relocation across both required platform seams and removes more lifecycle code than it adds.
- Stop if the full closure inventory exposes a redistribution conflict; record the exact component/license and resolve it before an archive is published.

## Dependency Decision

Reject `nix bundle`, `nix-portable`, and `nix-community/nix-bundle` as the final product contract because they are Linux-only and preserve Nix/store virtualization. Do not adopt cargo-dist yet: its manifests and installer UX are useful references, but Nova is a multi-project Nix assembly and the existing release workflow can own one archive contract with less new machinery. Reconsider cargo-dist only if its generic-build support demonstrably deletes the local release and installer logic.

title: Build the x86_64-linux no-Rio portable Nova archive
description:
## Outcome

Build the first real Nix-free Nova payload: one relocatable `x86_64-linux` archive with managed Helix and Yazi and without Rio.

- Consumer: a Linux user or installer on a machine with no Nix installation.
- Trigger: extract the archive into any user-owned absolute path and invoke `nova` or its `yzx` compatibility alias.
- Observable result: help, identity, diagnostics, and a fresh `enter` session use the packaged tools, plugins, configuration, and assets without a mounted Nix store.
- Failure behavior: an unsupported kernel/libc/terminal or missing host prerequisite produces a clear diagnostic before partial session startup; a failed extraction never mutates an existing installation.

Impact: HIGH. Effort: L. Risk: HIGH because the measured no-Rio closure is about 1.5 GiB and currently relies on hundreds of store paths. Confidence: HIGH in the target and no-Rio boundary; MEDIUM in the final ELF/libc compatibility floor until exercised on clean distributions.

## Evidence

- `README.md:296-300` already defines no-Rio as the terminal-free package where `enter` works and `launch` explains that Rio is unavailable.
- `flake.nix:923-927` exposes the exact managed Helix/Yazi no-Rio composition to reuse.
- The current no-Rio closure is about 1.5 GiB across 633 paths, with large Python, Nushell, Git, Helix, Yazi, Zellij, FFmpeg, font, and libc inputs. Archive size and compatibility must be measured, not guessed.
- Helix release history has treated old-glibc compatibility as a release concern, supporting an explicit Linux compatibility floor rather than an implicit build-runner floor: https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/releases
- Zellij publishes target-specific archives, including Linux musl artifacts, as a useful compatibility reference: https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij/releases

## Scope

In scope:

- Consume the accepted portable-runtime contract and the existing `yazelix-no-rio` composition; do not define a second file layout.
- Produce one reproducible compressed archive for `x86_64-linux`, initially `tar.gz` unless measured size makes another universally installable format clearly better.
- Rewrite Nova-owned absolute paths to the runtime root and relocate packaged ELF interpreters, RPATHs, shared libraries, scripts, WASMs, configuration, and assets as required.
- Keep host integrations explicit. Nova may invoke user shells, clipboard tools, agents, and configured editors from the host only where the current contract already permits them.
- Choose and record the oldest supported glibc/kernel floor from actual clean-system tests. Prefer the existing dependency graph over introducing a second musl build universe unless glibc testing proves it necessary.
- Record compressed size, extracted size, file count, startup time, and the largest contributors. Reduce obviously unused closure content only when the inventory proves it is not loaded.
- Preserve `nova` as the canonical command and `yzx` as the v2 compatibility alias.

Out of scope:

- No Rio, desktop entry, AppImage, Homebrew, Linux aarch64, Darwin, Flatpak, Snap, auto-updater, or distro package repository.
- No promise that every Linux distribution is supported.
- No package slimming by removing managed Helix or Yazi from this first complete payload.

## Verification

- Build from one exact revision through Nix, extract under at least two unrelated paths, and verify identical behavior.
- In a clean `x86_64-linux` environment with no `nix` executable and no `/nix/store` mount, run `nova --version`, `nova help`, `nova status --json`, `nova doctor`, the corresponding `yzx` alias checks, and a fresh PTY-backed `nova enter` smoke.
- Exercise at least one oldest-supported glibc image and one second mainstream distribution family; keep this to the smallest pair that can falsify the compatibility claim.
- Verify no symlink escapes the extracted root and no executable, interpreter, dynamic loader entry, plugin/config path, or invoked runtime path requires `/nix/store`. Document harmless build/debug strings if zero textual matches is not feasible.
- Prove the included Zellij plugins load, managed Helix starts, managed Yazi starts, and cancellation/exit returns the terminal cleanly.
- `nova launch` fails with the existing clear no-Rio diagnostic rather than attempting GUI startup.
- Record the archive hash, sizes, exact source revision, test images, and manual fresh-session result.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if success depends on mounting `/nix/store`, proot, bubblewrap, user namespaces, setuid helpers, or a target-side Nix installation.
- Stop if a runtime path is fixed by copying package composition into a frontend instead of correcting the portable-root owner.
- Stop and split a specific upstream/fork defect only when one child binary itself cannot be redistributed or relocated without an independently maintainable change.
- Stop before claiming broad Linux support from one container image or compilation alone.

## Dependency Decision

Use Nix as the release factory and native ELF relocation tools already available in nixpkgs. Do not add `nix-portable`, `nix-bundle`, AppImage tooling, or cargo-dist to this slice. Consider a musl child build only after the glibc floor fails the chosen compatibility contract.

title: Build and prove the aarch64-darwin no-Rio portable Nova archive
description:
## Outcome

Extend the accepted portable-runtime contract to one real macOS target: an `aarch64-darwin` no-Rio Nova archive that runs after extraction on a Mac without Nix.

- Consumer: an Apple Silicon macOS user who supplies a capable host terminal.
- Trigger: extract the archive at an arbitrary user path and run `nova enter`.
- Observable result: Nova resolves its packaged tools, dylibs, plugins, configuration, and assets relative to its runtime root and starts a fresh managed session.
- Failure behavior: incompatible macOS versions, quarantine/signature failures, or missing host capabilities produce actionable diagnostics without weakening Gatekeeper globally.

Impact: HIGH for cross-platform distribution. Effort: L. Risk: HIGH because Darwin relocation and direct-download trust behavior differ materially from Linux. Confidence: HIGH that the no-Rio boundary is correct; MEDIUM on signing/notarization details until tested from an actual downloaded artifact.

## Evidence

- `README.md:81-84` records real `aarch64-darwin` package builds but says the earlier interactive checklist and Rio GUI remain unverified.
- `.github/workflows/publish_nix_cache.yml:134-148` already builds every Darwin package variant on `macos-15`, including no-Rio, providing a real platform build owner to extend.
- Apple documents `@rpath` and loader-relative dependent libraries as the native mechanism for relocatable directory layouts: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/DeveloperTools/Conceptual/DynamicLibraries/100-Articles/RunpathDependentLibraries.html
- Apple documents Developer ID signing, hardened runtime, timestamps, and notarization for software distributed outside the App Store: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution
- Homebrew uses the default Apple Silicon prefix `/opt/homebrew`; a future formula should install this same portable payload rather than assume that prefix inside Nova: https://docs.brew.sh/FAQ

## Scope

In scope:

- Reuse the same runtime-root layout, manifest schema, command names, and no-Rio managed Helix/Yazi composition proven on Linux.
- Build on a real Apple Silicon runner and relocate Mach-O install names and load commands with `@loader_path`/`@rpath` where required.
- Select and record a minimum supported macOS version from the packaged binaries and actual execution evidence.
- Decide and implement the minimum public-distribution signing/notarization path required for a directly downloaded CLI archive. Keep secrets only in the release workflow and make unsigned local builds clearly non-release artifacts.
- Prove behavior after downloading or transferring the archive so quarantine/Gatekeeper behavior is represented, not only a local Nix-store extraction.
- Run the no-Rio command and fresh-session surface in a capable host terminal.

Out of scope:

- No Rio `.app`, GUI launch, Intel macOS, universal binary, DMG/PKG, Homebrew formula, auto-update service, Keychain integration, or macOS-specific configuration fork.
- No weakening Gatekeeper, instructing users to disable security globally, or relying on a Nix-installed shell environment.

## Verification

- On an `aarch64-darwin` machine with no target-side Nix dependency, extract under at least two unrelated paths and run `nova --version`, `nova help`, `nova status --json`, `nova doctor`, alias checks, and a fresh `nova enter` session.
- `otool -L` and recursive load-command inspection show that packaged dylibs resolve inside the runtime root or to documented system frameworks; no live `/nix/store` path is required.
- `codesign --verify --deep --strict` succeeds for the public candidate. Exercise `spctl`/Gatekeeper from a downloaded or quarantined archive and record the result; require notarization before public release when that test or Apple policy requires it.
- Included Zellij plugins, managed Helix, and managed Yazi start and exit cleanly in the tested terminal.
- Record exact macOS version, hardware architecture, archive identity/hash, signing identity class, notarization result, and fresh-session observation.
- Keep Linux and Darwin flake/package gates green at the exact shared-contract revision.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the Darwin implementation introduces a second runtime layout or package-composition owner.
- Stop if success requires Nix paths, shell initialization from a Nix profile, disabling Gatekeeper, or undocumented unsigned-binary exceptions.
- Stop before expanding to Rio or Intel macOS; those are separate product choices with different proof and signing cost.
- Stop if the Linux contract must materially change; update and re-prove the shared contract first.

## Dependency Decision

Use native Mach-O run paths and Apple code-signing/notarization tools. Do not add a cross-platform bundling framework solely for Darwin. Sequence this after the Linux archive so only one relocation frontier is under architectural change at a time.

title: Publish immutable Nix-free Nova release assets
description:
## Outcome

Publish each proven portable Nova archive as an immutable, inspectable release asset with one metadata and integrity contract for installers and package-manager wrappers.

- Consumer: users, the shell installer, Homebrew/AppImage packaging, and downstream verification automation.
- Trigger: an authorized immutable Nova version tag points at an exact accepted revision and a target archive has passed installed-artifact proof.
- Observable result: the release contains predictably named archives, checksums, a machine-readable manifest, redistribution notices, and verifiable build provenance tied to that tag and revision.
- Failure behavior: any build, inventory, checksum, notice, attestation, or installed-artifact check failure prevents publication; reruns cannot silently replace a released asset.

Impact: HIGH. Effort: M. Risk: MEDIUM because release permissions and artifact immutability are security boundaries. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- The current workflows publish Nix closures to Cachix but do not publish standalone runtime archives (`.github/workflows/publish_nix_cache.yml`).
- GitHub documents artifact attestations for binary provenance and supports verification with `gh attestation verify`: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/use-artifact-attestations/use-artifact-attestations
- GitHub recommends immutable releases and provenance as software-supply-chain controls: https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/tutorials/implement-supply-chain-best-practices/securing-builds
- cargo-dist demonstrates useful release conventions—target archives, checksums, a machine-readable manifest, aliases, and installer consumers—but adopting the framework is not required to use those conventions: https://github.com/axodotdev/cargo-dist
- The selected Nova payload contains hundreds of dependency paths, so redistribution notices must be generated from the exact closure rather than maintained as a handwritten short list.

## Scope

In scope:

- Add one bounded tag-triggered release job after the existing version and platform gates for the exact revision. Bound permissions, concurrency, timeouts, retention, and secret use.
- Publish one `tar.gz` (or the format accepted by the archive bead) per proven target with stable names containing Nova version, target triple, and no-Rio payload identity.
- Publish `SHA256SUMS` and a small versioned JSON manifest mapping supported target triples to artifact URL/name, size, hash, payload variant, minimum OS/libc contract, source revision, and entrypoints.
- Generate license and notice material from the exact selected closure and include it in each archive or as a clearly associated release asset.
- Generate an SBOM using an already available Nix/GitHub capability when practical; do not add a large framework only to produce one format.
- Use GitHub artifact attestations for build provenance, with least-privilege `id-token`/`attestations` permissions isolated to the release job. Checksums remain the installer-facing corruption/integrity contract when the user does not have `gh`.
- Publish Linux as soon as its archive is proven. Add Darwin to the same manifest schema only after the Darwin bead passes; do not redesign the release contract.
- Record exact artifact sizes and set a review threshold for unexpected growth rather than hiding it behind release automation.

Out of scope:

- No mutable `latest` asset replacement, nightly channel, delta updater, CDN, package registry, Homebrew tap, AppImage, signing service beyond the chosen platform/provenance needs, or publication of unproved targets.
- No release job that recomposes Nova independently of the flake artifact owner.

## Verification

- A release dry run from an immutable candidate creates the exact archive, manifest, checksum, notices, and provenance files without publishing.
- After authorized test publication, download assets through their public URLs into a clean environment, verify the exact checksum, verify GitHub provenance with `gh attestation verify`, extract, and run the target archive installed-artifact checks.
- Manifest version/target selection rejects unsupported targets and does not require a shell installer to parse arbitrary release-page HTML.
- A repeated run against an existing immutable version refuses to overwrite assets.
- Workflow permissions are `contents: read` by default and elevated only for the publication/attestation steps; concurrency prevents duplicate publication.
- Record workflow URL, revision/tag, artifact hashes, target results, and any unverified platform explicitly.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the archive has not passed its clean-machine, no-Nix proof.
- Stop if any selected component lacks known redistribution terms or required notices.
- Stop if release automation rebuilds a different payload from the one that passed the platform gate.
- Stop before publishing a real user release without explicit release/promotion authority.
- Stop if provenance requires broad repository permissions or long-lived signing secrets that cannot be isolated.

## Dependency Decision

Extend the existing GitHub Actions release surface and use GitHub-native attestations. Do not add cargo-dist in the first slice: borrow its artifact/manifest conventions, then reconsider only if its generic-build mode deletes more workflow and installer code than it introduces. Use standard archive and SHA-256 tools already present on the runners.

title: Install Nova from its release archive with a POSIX shell installer
description:
## Outcome

Ship the first supported Nix-free installation frontend as a small POSIX shell installer over the immutable portable archive contract.

- Consumer: a user on a supported target who wants Nova without installing Nix or Homebrew.
- Trigger: download or pipe the versioned installer, optionally selecting an exact Nova version and install root.
- Observable result: the installer selects the matching published archive, verifies it before extraction, installs it into a versioned user-owned directory, and exposes `nova` plus the `yzx` v2 compatibility alias.
- Failure behavior: unsupported targets, missing tools, network errors, checksum failures, extraction failures, and smoke-test failures leave the previously selected installation and user configuration untouched.

Impact: HIGH. Effort: M. Risk: MEDIUM because installers cross a remote-code trust boundary and mutate PATH-visible state. Confidence: HIGH that this is the smallest complete first frontend.

## Evidence

- The umbrella requirement is optional Nix-free installation; Homebrew and AppImage are useful later but each adds a packaging ecosystem before the common archive has user evidence.
- uv provides a strong reference UX: standalone versioned shell installers, GitHub release downloads, custom install directories, and a no-PATH-mutation mode: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/ and https://docs.astral.sh/uv/configuration/installer/
- Homebrew formulae can later install the same archive under a prefix; choosing shell first avoids encoding Nova composition in Ruby: https://docs.brew.sh/Formula-Cookbook
- The release manifest and checksum sidecar remove any need to scrape GitHub HTML or parse full JSON with a new dependency.

## Scope

In scope:

- Default to a user install under the XDG data directory on Linux and the corresponding documented user-owned location on macOS; permit one explicit install-root override. Do not require `sudo`.
- Store payloads in versioned directories and update one atomic `current` selector only after checksum, extraction, and smoke checks pass.
- Expose `nova` and `yzx` through a user-selected bin directory, defaulting to `~/.local/bin` where appropriate. Offer `--no-modify-path`; never silently edit multiple shell startup files.
- Support stable/latest only through release metadata plus an exact `--version` option. Re-running the installer performs upgrade; installing a prior exact version provides rollback without a separate updater daemon.
- Detect `uname` OS/architecture and map only to targets present in the release manifest. Begin with `x86_64-linux`; enable `aarch64-darwin` without installer redesign after its archive is proven and published.
- Require only ordinary platform tools such as `/bin/sh`, `curl`, `tar`, and an available SHA-256 command. Use a predictable artifact name plus `SHA256SUMS` so the installer does not need `jq`.
- Download into a newly created temporary directory, verify the exact filename/hash before extraction, validate the archive root, and atomically activate it.
- Provide an uninstall command or installer mode that removes only installer-owned versions and links when those links still point into the owned root. Preserve all Nova user configuration, sessions, and unrelated files.
- Print post-install PATH guidance and provenance-verification guidance. A piped command is documented as a convenience; a downloadable inspect-then-run path is equally prominent.

Out of scope:

- No package composition, Nix evaluation, target-side Nix, Homebrew, AppImage, GUI installer, root/system-wide default, shell framework, updater daemon, telemetry, automatic deletion of older versions, or source build.
- No claim for targets absent from the release manifest. No `nova launch` success requirement for the no-Rio payload; it must retain the clear unavailable diagnostic.

## Verification

- Run a syntax/lint check appropriate for POSIX shell and one deterministic fixture test against a local fake manifest/archive for target mapping, checksum rejection, failed extraction, activation, upgrade, rollback, and uninstall ownership.
- In a clean supported machine/container with no `nix` executable and no `/nix/store` mount, install from the published assets and verify `nova --version`, `nova help`, `nova status --json`, `nova doctor`, `yzx --version`, and a fresh PTY-backed `nova enter` session.
- Corrupt the archive and prove the installer rejects it while the previous `current` version still runs.
- Install to a path containing spaces and to a non-default root; verify relative runtime discovery still works.
- Verify `--no-modify-path` changes no shell configuration. Verify uninstall leaves user configuration and unrelated bin links untouched.
- On each newly enabled platform, run the installed-artifact and fresh-session checks on that real platform before documenting support.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the installer needs to know individual Nova child packages or recreate the archive tree.
- Stop if safe installation requires a new runtime dependency or privileged system mutation.
- Stop if checksum/provenance data cannot be tied to the exact immutable release asset.
- Stop before enabling a target whose archive lacks clean-machine proof.
- Stop if update/uninstall cannot distinguish installer-owned paths from user-owned state.

## Dependency Decision

Use POSIX shell and native download/archive/hash tools. Do not add an installer framework, JSON parser, updater daemon, or cargo-dist initially. The stable artifact naming and checksum sidecar are sufficient; reconsider a framework only after a second frontend proves duplicated lifecycle logic.

title: Build a Nova-native agent command center
description: Give Yazelix a local-first mission-control surface for starting, observing, focusing, reviewing, validating, and archiving multiple agent task lanes. Reuse Nova Zellij sessions, worktrees, Beads, and existing popups. Begin passive-first; do not add a Yazelix daemon, arbitrary send-input fleet control, or provider-framework sprawl.
acceptance_criteria: A written first-slice contract defines task-lane identity, durable state, session/worktree ownership, and passive status derivation. It explicitly evaluates a versioned machine-readable initial snapshot plus a bounded additive activity stream against existing Zellij/plugin, Beads, worktree, and yzx status owners. If that interface is accepted, stable lane/session identities, typed result/error semantics, stale or dropped-event recovery, and initial-snapshot-then-follow behavior are part of the contract. One small vertical slice can start or register a lane, list it, and focus or inspect its work without disturbing unrelated sessions. Validation covers stale-lane handling and worktree/session safety. Transcript capture, completion inference from quiet terminal output, arbitrary send-input fleet control, a Yazelix daemon, and broader automation remain explicitly deferred.
notes: External design reference at TUIOS revision 4cc64e58daee7faa872790d185e29d108e7dd461: JSON verb protocol https://github.com/Gaurav-Gosain/tuios/blob/4cc64e58daee7faa872790d185e29d108e7dd461/docs/protocol.md and aggregate view https://github.com/Gaurav-Gosain/tuios/blob/4cc64e58daee7faa872790d185e29d108e7dd461/README.md#discovery--navigation. The genuinely useful patterns are self-description through list-verbs, stable result discriminators and error codes with actionable hints, a complete initial snapshot followed by additive events, bounded subscriber queues with explicit gap markers, and wait-for replacing blind polling. For Nova, borrow the contract shape only: prefer read-mostly lane/session state, activity, focus, and inspection derived from current owners. Do not add a TUIOS dependency, generic terminal control plane, PTY owner, raw send-text, capture-pane transcript surveillance, or output-regex claims that an agent completed. Reuse native Zellij/plugin events and yzx status --json; require a new child contract only if the accepted first slice proves those owners lack a necessary capability.

title: Compare terminal agent-management tools for Nova
description:
## Why

A Zellij community discussion identifies five actively developed approaches to terminal-native coding-agent management: Herdr, zj-radar, zj-agents, captain-miao, and zellaude. Nova already has a managed agent popup, tab-activity owner, a proved zj-radar candidate, a planned v2 navigation rail, and a broader command-center goal. Choosing another tool by feature list alone could duplicate status, session, notification, terminal, or attention ownership.

## Evidence

- Source discussion: https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij/discussions/5391#discussioncomment-17908201.
- Herdr: https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr — terminal runtime with persistent sessions and agent awareness; Apache-2.0 at initial recon.
- zj-radar: https://github.com/marktoda/zj-radar — Zellij agent-status sidebar; MIT at initial recon.
- zj-agents: https://github.com/kaankoken/zj-agents — Zellij-oriented agent classification and notification system; Apache-2.0 at initial recon.
- captain-miao: https://github.com/hyperlogue/captain-miao — multiplexer-independent agent-session dashboard; MIT at initial recon.
- zellaude: https://github.com/ishefi/zellaude — Claude-aware Zellij status-bar plugin; MIT at initial recon.
- `README.md:260,268` records the current orchestrator and activity-aware status-bar owners.
- `runtime/yzx-agent.rs:29-77` owns the current managed agent-popup provider selection and failure behavior.
- `defaults/zellij/config.kdl:28-30,130-133` owns the packaged agent popup and key.
- Bead `yazelix-5vl-radar-first-sidebar-xj0.1` already proves zj-radar v0.2.2 at `b73e3ce31ee49b62eff50287c50b11fae416d767`; do not repeat that spike.
- Epic `yazelix-nova-agent-command-center-srmq-2hd` owns the future Nova-native command-center outcome. Epic `yazelix-5vl-radar-first-sidebar-xj0` owns the accepted v2 Forest/radar navigation direction and single attention owner.

## Decision Contract

Compare exact reviewed revisions of all five tools against Nova rather than ranking generic feature lists. The result must recommend one of: consume an upstream tool, reuse a narrow contract or interaction pattern without a dependency, retain the current zj-radar and Nova direction, or adopt none. Name the surviving owner for sessions, terminal processes, agent status, attention navigation, notifications, worktree identity, and durable task state.

## Scope

In scope:
- Record exact revision, license, release/package model, maintenance activity, supported agents, status derivation, API or pipe contracts, Zellij/version requirements, Linux/macOS implications, and Nix fit for each tool.
- Compare product layer: full terminal/session runtime, Zellij plugin, status-bar replacement, or external dashboard.
- Compare state fidelity and failure behavior for working, blocked, done, idle, stale, and unknown states.
- Compare focus/navigation, click behavior, notifications, permission requirements, bounded backpressure, viewport/output capture, privacy, and security boundaries.
- Measure owner, dependency, process, configuration, and approximate LOC impact on Nova. Credit code or ownership deleted, not feature count alone.
- Reuse the completed zj-radar proof and current Herdr/session evidence. Run at most one isolated disposable spike if source review cannot resolve the leading candidate.

Out of scope:
- Do not change Nova source, package pins, layouts, default keys, agent configuration, or user files during the investigation.
- Do not replace Zellij, Herdr, the v1 session contract, the v2 navigation decision, or the current tab-activity owner without a separately approved product decision.
- Do not install all candidates, create forks, copy source, enable desktop notifications, or run setup commands against ambient configuration.
- Do not infer agent completion solely from quiet terminal output without documenting false-positive and stale-state behavior.

## Investigation Notes

1. Pin every reviewed source to a commit and read its README, architecture, protocol, packaging, permission, license, and release surfaces directly.
2. Build one evidence matrix using the same ownership and failure criteria for every candidate.
3. Treat existing zj-radar dogfood as direct evidence and test only materially changed revisions or unresolved contracts.
4. If a runnable comparison is necessary, isolate config, permissions, sessions, state, and package destination; prefer upstream artifacts and documented commands.
5. Record the decision and meaningful rejections in this Bead, then update the parent command-center contract. Create implementation work only for a user-accepted outcome.

## Verification

- `br show yazelix-5vl-radar-first-sidebar-xj0.1 --json` must be cited for existing radar evidence.
- `rg -n "agent|activity|zjstatus" README.md runtime defaults crates flake.nix` must identify the current Nova owners before recommending changes.
- Every matrix entry must link an exact commit and primary-source documentation for the claimed mechanism.
- Any disposable spike must record exact package identity, isolated paths, commands, results, teardown, and whether Linux/macOS behavior was actually exercised.
- The final Bead state must contain one recommendation, rejected alternatives, ownership map, dependency impact, residual risk, and the evidence that would reverse the decision.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before changing runtime or package state; implementation requires a separately accepted Bead.
- Stop and request a product-scope decision if the leading option replaces the terminal, multiplexer, or session owner rather than composing with Nova.
- Stop a candidate evaluation if its license, source, protocol, or required data capture cannot be verified.
- Stop a runnable spike if it requires ambient setup mutation, unbounded pane scraping, or undocumented permissions.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort M, implementation risk LOW because this Bead is read-only, decision risk MED, confidence HIGH that comparison is valuable. Prefer one owner and the smallest consumed contract. Rejected upfront: adopting every tool, comparing screenshots only, or reopening the completed zj-radar proof without evidence of material upstream change.
acceptance_criteria:
The investigation is accepted when:

- Exact revisions, licenses, maintenance state, packages, supported agents, state mechanisms, APIs, permissions, platform implications, and Nova ownership impact are recorded for Herdr, zj-radar, zj-agents, captain-miao, and zellaude.
- The comparison distinguishes full runtime replacement from composable plugin, status-bar, and dashboard roles.
- Existing zj-radar and Herdr/session evidence is reused; any new dogfood is limited to one isolated leading-candidate spike justified by an unresolved decision.
- One recommendation names the surviving owner for sessions, terminals, agent status, attention, notifications, worktrees, and durable task state, with meaningful alternatives rejected explicitly.
- No source, package pin, runtime configuration, layout, key, ambient tool configuration, or user session changes during investigation.
- An implementation Bead is created only after the user accepts a concrete outcome; choosing no dependency is a valid result.
notes:
## Current recommendation

Keep stock zj-radar as Nova's single live agent-status and attention rail. Replace mandatory Codex hook onboarding with a basic, event-driven fallback inside zj-radar, then leave provider integrations as optional enrichment.

The basic Codex contract should use events Radar already receives:

- `CommandChanged` identifies a Codex pane and retains that identity until the pane returns to its shell or exits.
- `PaneUpdate.title` maps Codex's braille activity title to `running` and either `Action Required` title to `pending`.
- A known Codex pane with no activity title is `idle`.
- A real `zj_radar.status.v1` producer event always overrides inferred state.
- If a `running -> idle` transition while unfocused is rendered as `done`, it must be named an observation-relative heuristic and clear on focus.
- If the user disables title activity or animations, the fallback degrades to presence/idle instead of inventing precise state.
- No pane-content reads, process-table scans, per-pane timers, new permissions, ambient configuration writes, or Nova-owned agent parser.

This is the smallest architecture because Zellij already supplies command and title changes, Codex already publishes useful status in its terminal title, and Radar already owns the rail and pane lifecycle. A proof belongs upstream in zj-radar first. Nova should consume an upstream release; create a fork only if a small general-purpose upstream change is rejected after the behavior is proven.

## Exact reviewed sources

Core candidates from the Zellij discussion:

- Herdr `94f6d9c0d9bb9cf9ffae99d8bbfb09e9bf2fc9e0`: Apache-2.0 terminal runtime and session owner. Strong reference, wrong dependency layer for Nova.
- zj-radar `0b1672606ca118f6241df687889142c8b52d03fe` (`v0.6.0`): MIT Zellij rail, push protocol, Claude/Codex/OpenCode producers, existing Nova owner. Best fit.
- zj-agents `39795f26960505e378c619ffaf0963efd712bfeb`: MIT OR Apache-2.0, hookless Zellij detector. It polls visible pane text and running commands roughly once per second and asks for more permissions. Useful fallback evidence, not the preferred owner.
- captain-miao `07e4a47886f5861294511ae28553201a16276f1f`: MIT multiplexer-independent session dashboard. Its managed Codex profile can preseed trust hashes, but that reserves configuration ownership and couples to Codex internals. Reject for Nova.
- Zellaude `1d1d56c6d29155d59ed9bd1386f970168f781bb8`: MIT Claude-only Zellij tab-bar replacement with auto-installed hooks. It duplicates Nova/Radar presentation and does not solve Codex.

Additional mechanism references:

- Fleet `30450f0970bbc1e45ed2ff8488fe00908644cfe0`: MIT tmux dashboard. Its hybrid discovery explicitly lets hook state override process/title inference; title outranks stale scraped output. This validates basic-plus-enhanced semantics, but its process scans and pane scraping are unnecessary under Zellij events.
- RimZ `cb8c0dce559177305e53a2f061a85bd449d922ce`: MIT Zellij/tmux control room. Strong source for provider adapters and ownership, but it owns durable state, hooks, workspaces, commands, and sidebar behavior that Nova already owns or deliberately defers.
- Agent View `5e9d735bef0b5678c43580747e96590c3598d002`, ai-agent-manager `dd2d72d6c75cc3b8b80392058a84891917e85b86`, tmux-scout `25cc2a038d10a726b9d28f2a908c4602e11366b8`, and pane-patrol `1eb2182810856c7d3771733c93a7574b52239100`: useful hybrid/parser precedents, all tmux-oriented and dependent on hooks, pane scraping, process scans, or both.
- AgentHUD `262d1c540e416b3c8aafa9e61fdec3d6232cd579`: cross-provider history/report reference based on private session stores. It lacks a natural Zellij-pane identity contract and is not a live rail owner.
- Falcode `972df9c2b7c3741c9cea88dbae50b4547b344ca2`: Zellij popup with hook/extension reporters and filesystem polling. It does not support Codex and does not simplify Nova.
- Rook `7cb77a38dc7e180305fbee43cec9ca65fb50383c`: MIT macOS terminal/session replacement. It cleanly separates automatic foreground-process identity from optional reported turn state and recognizes agent progress markers in terminal titles. That ownership split supports Nova's proposed basic/enhanced model, while the product itself is outside Nova's cross-platform Zellij boundary.
- gentle-agent-state `963e85379ebf66f5304797b015327e133e6f4b6a`: MIT small cross-agent adapter for tmux, Zellij, and Ghostty. It proves that OpenCode and Pi user-level plugins can be low-friction and that pane titles are a useful transport, but its Claude/Codex paths still require installed hooks and it would duplicate Radar's state owner.

Provider-native evidence:

- OpenAI Codex `5adb68a49933ae446bf11935662c83dba55a0804` (`rust-v0.152.1`) exposes activity and action-required state in its terminal title. Its `/hooks` browser toggles one trusted hook at a time; startup offers bulk trust only for hooks that still need review. No official bulk-enable operation was found.
- Codex legacy `notify` is a single config slot and reports only turn completion. Radar supports it behind `setup codex --legacy-notify`; reject it as Nova's default because it displaces another notifier and still lacks running/pending state.
- OpenCode has an auto-loaded plugin API with typed permission, question, session-status, idle, and error events. Radar v0.6.0 already consumes this route.
- Pi `4e69b0c28060f0f02fbe38bfa7c21a2e2eb25057` auto-discovers user-level extensions and exposes `agent_start`, `agent_settled`, turn, tool, and shutdown events. This is a clean future producer route without a project-level trust prompt.
- Claude Code plugins can package hooks, so Radar's Claude plugin avoids manual settings edits. Grok Build exposes hooks but retains a trust boundary.

## Rejected defaults

- `yzx seed-zjradar-hooks`, copied trust hashes, or `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`: Nova must not impersonate the user's trust decision or couple to Codex hash internals.
- Mandatory seven-hook Codex setup: it is the exact onboarding failure under investigation.
- A new Nova tracker, daemon, transcript reader, process scanner, or pane parser: duplicates Radar and expands permissions/privacy/maintenance.
- zj-agents as the default: more polling, permissions, UI parsing, and state ambiguity than the title-event seam.
- Herdr, RimZ, Captain Miao, or another session manager as a dependency: each would reopen Nova's runtime/session ownership.

## Reversal conditions

Choose a different path only if an isolated latest-Radar proof shows that Zellij does not deliver Codex command/title changes reliably, Codex removes the title state without a replacement contract, or passive state cannot coexist with authoritative producer events. In that case, dogfood stock zj-agents in isolation before considering a fork or Nova-owned implementation.

title: Document Nova agent-status references
description:
## Context

The agent-status investigation now spans Zellij plugins, tmux dashboards, full terminal runtimes, provider-native extension APIs, and OpenAI Codex source behavior. The evidence lives in Beads and temporary research checkouts, so later work cannot review or challenge the decision from one canonical repository document.

## Goal

Create and commit `docs/agent-status-references.md` as Nova's durable, citation-first living reference ledger. It should distinguish the implemented explicit-provider model from the blocked passive/basic proposal, and record exact reviewed revisions, mechanism categories, ownership tradeoffs, decisions, rejected alternatives, and reversal evidence.

## Non-goals

- Do not change runtime behavior, package pins, layouts, keys, permissions, provider configuration, or user files.
- Do not copy candidate source or turn the document into a feature checklist.
- Do not claim a passive Radar adapter is implemented before its proof issue completes.

## Approach

- Start from decision bead `yazelix-nova-agent-command-center-srmq-2hd.1` and verify every exact revision and primary link again.
- Group references by product layer: runtime/session replacement, dashboard/orchestrator, multiplexer-native rail, passive detector, provider-native event API, and transcript/history reader.
- Use one compact matrix for ownership, status source, onboarding, permissions/data access, Linux/macOS fit, dependency/fork cost, and Nova disposition.
- State current delivery plainly: the narrow Yazelix Radar fork owns the rail and exact provider events; optional one-time Codex setup belongs to child xj0.16. The proposed zero-config command/title fallback is blocked by xj0.14 because normal Nova topology loses title edges. Provider precedence remains a requirement if that proposal resumes, not a delivered feature. Distinguish stock upstream reference revisions from the installed fork pin.
- Mark proposed, source-proven, mechanically proven, and dogfooded claims separately.
- Name this file as the repository owner for agent-status reference and decision evidence. Future changes to Radar/provider selection, status derivation, or a reviewed exact revision must update it in the same change rather than creating another research note.
- Link the document from the README documentation area and update the README tracked-text LOC scorecard for the exact resulting tree. No changelog entry is needed unless user-visible runtime behavior also changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- The document cites exact commits for the five discussion candidates and the strongest additional references, plus exact provider-native sources.
- It records the current Nova owners and does not imply that a reviewed project is adopted.
- It explains why unconsented hook seeding, trust bypass, transcript scraping, process polling, and full runtime replacement are rejected defaults, while explicit user-approved child setup remains supported.
- It records the failed title-signal proof, the resulting blocked passive adapter, and the conditional zj-agents evaluation. The failure does not authorize polling or adoption; a different product boundary requires an explicit decision.
- It contains a short maintenance rule stating which changes require refreshing the ledger and how stale exact-revision evidence is labeled rather than silently deleted.
- README links the document and its LOC scorecard matches the exact tree.
- `git diff --check` passes and all links are syntactically valid; a link checker is used if the repository already has one.

## Risks and rollback

The main risk is documentation claiming more proof than exists. Use explicit evidence-state labels. Rollback is deletion of the document and README link; no runtime state is involved.
notes:
Accepted state — 2026-09-07: docs/agent-status-references.md is the canonical reference ledger. It records the retained Radar ownership, implemented xj0.19 setup flow, blocked xj0.14 title signal, conditional zj-agents evaluation, provider trust boundary, rejected defaults and reversal/maintenance conditions. The five discussion candidates and five strongest additional references have exact verified source revisions; Codex/Pi native revisions were rechecked and dated OpenCode/Grok primary-source references supplement them. Claude is labeled mutable official documentation evidence, not a closed-client source audit. Fleet is nicknisi/fleet at the recorded 30450f09 revision. Historical xj0.1 attention-next failure and xj0.16/xj0.19 proof limits remain explicit. Producer-over-inference precedence is proposed, not delivered.

Verification: git diff --check passed. A temporary standard-library check verified 49 Markdown links, all 42 reference definitions, relative file/heading targets and exact Git source paths/line ranges; no existing repository link checker was found. The README link and both scorecards match 28,568 tracked-text LOC (+244; Markdown 4,402), counting the new reference ledger and excluding Beads/lockfiles/assets. This is platform-neutral documentation, so no runtime build, installation, provider configuration, permissions, package pin, GUI or channel promotion changed. Historical runtime evidence remains attached to its original exact revisions. Link-check results: /tmp/nova-2hd2-link-check.json. Unrelated existing Beads edits are preserved.
close_reason: Documented the accepted Radar model and exact references; preserved blocked/historical proof boundaries; links, diff and LOC checks passed.

title: Propose bulk hook enable and disable in Codex
description:
## Context

OpenAI Codex `rust-v0.152.1` commit `5adb68a49933ae446bf11935662c83dba55a0804` can bulk-trust hooks that still need review during startup, but its `/hooks` browser enables or disables only the selected trusted hook. A source that installs several hooks therefore makes users toggle them one at a time, while trusted-but-disabled hooks no longer qualify for startup review.

This is an upstream Codex UX gap. Nova must not work around it by writing trust state, copying internal hashes, or bypassing hook trust.

## Goal

Propose an upstream Codex bulk action that enables or disables all visible hooks, preferably with an optional source/config grouping, while preserving trust review and explicit user control.

## Scope

- Reconfirm current behavior in official Codex docs or source at execution time.
- Open a concise upstream issue describing the installed-many-hooks case, the trusted-but-disabled trap, expected bulk interaction, and security boundary.
- If maintainers accept the direction, implement only the smallest TUI action and tests in a separate authorized contribution run.
- Keep Nova's passive Radar path independent; this issue improves optional enriched integrations rather than blocking them.

## Non-goals

- No automatic enabling, trust bypass, Nova configuration mutation, private hash reproduction, or provider-specific special case in Codex.
- No upstream issue or PR without explicit external-write approval in that run.

## Acceptance criteria

- The upstream report links the exact hook-browser and startup-review source behavior and gives a reproducible multi-hook case.
- The proposal distinguishes trust from enablement and does not reduce the confirmation required for untrusted definitions.
- Any accepted implementation has focused tests for bulk enable, bulk disable, mixed trust state, and no-op behavior.
- Nova has no dependency on upstream acceptance.

## Risks and rollback

Bulk actions can make a security-sensitive screen too easy to misuse. Preserve explicit selection/confirmation and keep the action reversible. If maintainers reject it, close with the reason; do not add a Nova trust workaround.

title: Reassess yzx-open extraction only with a second consumer
description:
## Why

`crates/yzx-open` is the only local helper that might eventually deserve extraction, because it implements a concrete editor-open/Helix-bridge protocol. Today it is still tightly coupled to Yazelix Nova state, Zellij pane behavior, and the managed Helix wrapper, so extracting it now would add release/API overhead without a second consumer. The decision should be revisited only when main Yazelix, another Yazelix runtime, or a non-Yazelix tool wants to consume the same open protocol.

## Evidence

- `crates/yzx-open/src/main.rs:17`: `Config` is built from Yazelix-specific environment such as editor, Zellij binary, state dir, session id, Zellij session name, and log level.
- `crates/yzx-open/src/main.rs:99`: `Config::from_env` reads `YAZELIX_STATE_DIR`, `YAZELIX_HELIX_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID`, `YZX_EDITOR`, `YZX_ZELLIJ`, and Zellij session state.
- `crates/yzx-open/src/main.rs:119`: bridge discovery assumes the Yazelix Helix bridge directory under `state_dir/helix_bridge/<session_id>`.
- `crates/yzx-open/src/main.rs:255`: bridge requests use a protocol that is currently owned by Yazelix Helix integration.
- `crates/yzx-open/src/main.rs:299`: request payloads are Helix-specific actions: `helix.open_directory` and `helix.open_files`.
- `crates/yzx-open/src/main.rs:321`: fallback behavior shells out to Zellij to open a managed editor pane.
- `flake.nix:229`: the helper is packaged directly from `./crates/yzx-open` into the Yazelix Nova runtime.
- `flake.nix:258`: the Yazi wrapper injects `YZX_OPEN`, `YZX_ZELLIJ`, and managed editor variables for this helper.

## Decision To Revisit

Reassess whether `yzx-open` should become a separate repo, shared crate, or remain local only when at least one concrete second consumer exists.

Criteria that would justify extraction:
- Another repo needs to call the same bridge/open protocol.
- The bridge protocol has stable versioning and compatibility expectations.
- The helper can expose a small documented API/CLI without depending on Yazelix Nova packaging internals.
- Release cadence can be independent without making Yazelix Nova harder to change.

Criteria that keep it local:
- The only caller is Yazelix Nova's packaged Yazi/sidebar flow.
- The fallback behavior remains Zellij-pane-specific.
- Protocol changes need to land atomically with Yazelix Helix and the `yzx` runtime.
- Extraction would require compatibility shims or broad environment adapters.

## Scope

In scope when this decision is revisited:
- Compare current `crates/yzx-open` callers in this repo and main Yazelix.
- Identify whether a stable bridge/open API exists or whether this is still product glue.
- Decide between local crate, shared crate within this repo, separate repo, or no extraction.
- Record the decision in ARCHITECTURE and close this bead with the chosen path.

Out of scope:
- Do not extract `yzx-open` now.
- Do not create a compatibility layer for hypothetical callers.
- Do not rename the CLI or change bridge semantics as part of this decision.
- Do not make this a blocker for the canonical swap unless another bead explicitly elevates it.

## Verification

- If the decision is to keep local, `br close` this bead with notes naming the checked callers and why extraction is still not justified.
- If the decision is to extract, create implementation beads with exact repo/crate/API scope before moving code.
- `cargo test --manifest-path crates/yzx-open/Cargo.toml` should exit 0 for any local refactor done during investigation.
- `nix flake check` should exit 0 if package wiring is touched during investigation.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if no second consumer exists; keep this deferred.
- Stop if extraction would require support for non-Zellij fallback behavior without an explicit user-chosen product requirement.
- Stop if protocol ownership between Yazelix Nova and Yazelix Helix is unclear; resolve that decision before moving code.

## Maintenance Notes

Current recommendation: keep `yzx-open` local. Separate repo extraction requires independent users, independent release cadence, and a stable API, not just a file that could be reused someday.

title: Decide whether Nova should hide the native bottom status bar
description:
## Decision

Decide whether Nova should let users reclaim the native one-row Zellij hint/status surface while preserving discoverable mode and key help through the smallest existing-owner path.

Evaluate the current layouts and native Zellij capabilities first. Compare keeping the row, omitting it at session creation, a native toggle if one exists, and one on-demand help surface already owned by Zellij or Nova. The useful outcome from GitHub issue #621 belongs here.

## Boundaries

Do not implement the choice in this decision bead, port Classic bar materialization, create a second permanent status system, add a prefix mode solely for discovery, intercept ordinary direct chords, or duplicate the packaged key owner. If no option genuinely reclaims the row without harming modes, layouts, popups, narrow widths, or discoverability, reject the feature.
acceptance_criteria:
- The decision records whether the native row can be omitted or toggled without breaking Zellij modes, layouts, popups, narrow widths, or help discoverability.
- Keeping the row, omitting it, native toggling, and the smallest on-demand discovery paths are compared against current Nova behavior.
- One accepted option names its owner, invocation, persistence, failure behavior, and exact proof; rejection records the blocking Zellij limitation.
- The maintainer accepts or rejects the outcome before implementation.
- No code, second permanent bar, new prefix mode, key interception, or duplicate key-help owner is added by this decision bead.
notes: External UX reference at TUIOS revision 4cc64e58daee7faa872790d185e29d108e7dd461: which-key waits 500 ms after a prefix chord, then shows only the bindings available in that chord and disappears on the next key; see https://github.com/Gaurav-Gosain/tuios/blob/4cc64e58daee7faa872790d185e29d108e7dd461/docs/CONFIGURATION.md#whichkey_enabled. The useful principle is expert-invisible, on-demand discovery. Nova uses direct chords rather than a leader hierarchy, so do not add a prefix mode merely to copy it. Evaluate the smallest existing-owner path among searchable command-menu actions with keys, the Ratconfig Keys inventory, native mode help, or one explicit transient help overlay. Reject any option that replaces one reclaimed row with a second permanent bar, intercepts ordinary direct chords, or duplicates the packaged key owner.

title: Make Nova bar widgets degrade progressively under tab pressure
description: When long or numerous tabs consume width, hide lower-priority right-side widgets progressively instead of dropping the complete right area. The bar child owns rendering and Nova owns the published child revision plus integration smoke. Use Nova’s fixed widget order; do not port Classic widget-tray configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce whole-right-side loss on published Nova. Define widget priority from the fixed Nova render request, implement the smallest child-owned progressive degradation supported by zjstatus, preserve native tab behavior, publish the child, update the Nova lock, and manually verify long-name/many-tab layouts. Stop and record the smallest alternative if zjstatus cannot express it cleanly.

title: Ship restrained notifications in Nova v2
description: Nova v2 includes a restrained notification system. Define and ship the smallest useful event and delivery policy for action-required, failure, and long-running completion signals without creating a noisy status system. Prefer existing terminal/Zellij surfaces; any desktop delivery must be explicitly platform-gated and optional. Integrate agent-lane events with the command-center owner rather than duplicating agent state.
acceptance_criteria: Define the first event set, urgency, suppression/deduplication, delivery owner, platform behavior, and user control before implementation. The policy explicitly evaluates severity-specific duration floors, sticky action-required failures, universal dismissal, and whether dismissal can preserve the keypress intended for the underlying pane without mode or input corruption. One accepted vertical slice demonstrates a valuable notification without noise and has focused routing, suppression, expiry, dismissal, narrow-terminal, and conflicting-input tests. Desktop helpers are gated; agent state remains owned by the command center.
notes: External UX reference at TUIOS revision 4cc64e58daee7faa872790d185e29d108e7dd461: https://github.com/Gaurav-Gosain/tuios/blob/4cc64e58daee7faa872790d185e29d108e7dd461/docs/CONFIGURATION.md#notification-settings uses separate severity durations, sticky errors, and dismissal that still forwards Esc to the underlying surface. Borrow the questions, not the literal key behavior: Nova must prove any pass-through is safe across Zellij modes, shells, Helix, Yazi, popups, and copy/search states. Prefer existing Zellij or top-bar delivery and command-center-owned events. This reference does not authorize a desktop notifier, daemon, notification history service, or duplicate agent-state owner.

title: Evaluate shared build ownership for first-party Zellij WASI plugins
description: After Nova v1, compare the two child-owned WASI build recipes with a neutral published shared builder. Extract only if total owner count, LOC, inputs, release steps, and failure boundaries shrink and both child recipes are deleted. Nova remains a package consumer and contract validator.
acceptance_criteria: Record current and proposed LOC, owners, inputs, releases, platform gates, and failure boundaries. Extraction wins only if both plugin children consume one published neutral builder and delete their duplicate generic recipes while Linux and Darwin package contracts pass. Otherwise close with accepted-duplication evidence. Nova gains no build implementation.

title: Add columns mode if the Yazi sidebar survives v1
description:
## Why

With a single managed Yazi sidebar, Yazelix Nova can bring back a useful vertical split shape without reintroducing main Yazelix's broader layout system. The intended model is not multiple real startup layouts; it is one startup layout plus sidebar-aware swap variants for the main content area.

## Evidence

- `layout.kdl:13`: the real startup layout has one vertical split containing the managed `sidebar` pane.
- `layout.swap.kdl:1`: the current open variant puts all non-sidebar panes in one stacked content area.
- `layout.swap.kdl:13`: the current closed variant only collapses the sidebar; there is no alternate content arrangement.
- `config.kdl:120`: sidebar toggle currently uses raw `NextSwapLayout`, which must be fixed before adding more variants.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator/src/layout_state_contract.rs:20`: the shared pane orchestrator currently models only one layout family, `Single`.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator/src/layout_state_contract.rs:44`: the orchestrator's swap order only knows `single_*` and agent variants, so it cannot preserve sidebar state across a new columns mode yet.

## User-Visible Behavior

A user can switch the main work area between the current stacked mode and a columns mode while keeping exactly one managed Yazi sidebar. Toggling the sidebar preserves the selected content mode: stacked-open -> stacked-closed, columns-open -> columns-closed, and back. The startup session remains the current open stacked/sidebar shape.

## Scope

In scope:
- Add a sidebar-aware columns content mode to Yazelix Nova's swap layout contract.
- Keep one real `layout.kdl`; do not add alternate startup layout files.
- Add open/closed swap variants for the columns mode in `layout.swap.kdl`.
- Preserve the current stacked behavior as the default startup mode.
- Update layout checks to prove every variant contains exactly one managed `sidebar` pane and that open/closed widths are coherent.
- Update the pane-orchestrator child package only as much as needed to understand content mode plus sidebar state.
- Update the Nova flake lock/input after the child package change, if the child package is touched.
- Add a semantic command/key path for cycling content mode only if the product key is chosen in the implementation slice; do not overload `Alt Shift h`.
- Update README, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG, and LOC scorecard for user-visible layout/key behavior.

Out of scope:
- Do not port main Yazelix layout families wholesale.
- Do not add a bottom-terminal layout in this bead.
- Do not add right-sidebar/agent layout variants as part of this columns slice.
- Do not make raw Zellij swap cycling the user-facing layout control.
- Do not make layout KDL user-configurable.
- Do not add a general layout DSL or separate layout crate.

## Implementation Notes

1. Complete the radar surface contract first and use its semantic `toggle_sidebar` action; do not add columns while `Alt Shift h` still invokes raw swap cycling.
2. Prefer low-churn naming if the shared orchestrator contract makes renaming expensive: keep `single_open`/`single_closed` as the current stacked pair and add a clearly named columns pair, or explicitly migrate to `stacked_*` only if the child/main compatibility cost is understood.
3. In the child orchestrator, model content arrangement as a separate axis from sidebar visibility. Do not make `toggle_sidebar` mean "next swap layout".
4. The columns variant should split only the non-sidebar content area. The managed `sidebar` pane identity and command stay unchanged.
5. If the shared child plugin cannot safely grow this contract without risking main Yazelix's current `yzx_side.swap.kdl`, stop and record the smaller child-plugin contract needed for runtime-specific layout sets.
6. Treat the content-layout key as a separate design choice. A future command/menu item is better than binding `Alt Shift h` to layout cycling.

## Verification

- `cargo test --manifest-path /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator/Cargo.toml --lib` should exit 0 if child orchestrator logic changes.
- `nix build /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator#yazelix_zellij_pane_orchestrator --no-link` should exit 0 if the child package changes.
- `nix flake check` should exit 0 and prove the packaged Nova layout/check contract.
- `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs` should exit 0 after Nova layout or lock changes.
- `nix profile add --refresh /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix --profile <tmp>` should install the package if runtime files change.
- `nix profile upgrade --refresh yazelix` after runtime package changes.
- Manual dogfooding before claiming UX: toggle sidebar in both stacked and columns modes and confirm the Yazi sidebar remains the same managed pane.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if `Alt Shift h` is still raw `NextSwapLayout`.
- Stop if adding columns requires broad layout-family generation from main Yazelix.
- Stop if the shared orchestrator change would make main Yazelix cycle into swap names that main does not ship.
- Stop if the implementation starts defining bottom-terminal pane role/cwd/focus policy; create a separate bead only if the user chooses it.

## Maintenance Notes

Current decision: sidebar-aware content modes are swap variants, not real layouts. Rejected for this slice: bottom-terminal layout, main Yazelix's broader layout family system, and raw swap-cycle UX.
acceptance_criteria:
- Work starts only if child .5 explicitly retains the tiled Yazi surface for stable v1; if Yazi is removed, close this bead as superseded without generalizing it to radar.
- One startup layout remains and columns are swap variants of the non-sidebar content area.
- Toggling the retained Yazi sidebar preserves stacked-versus-columns mode through semantic orchestration, not raw swap cycling.
- Every retained variant contains exactly one managed Yazi sidebar and coherent open or closed widths.
- Focused child, layout, flake, package, temporary-profile, and requested dogfood checks pass.
notes:
Stable-surface gate: this is intentionally a Yazi-sidebar feature, not a generic radar layout project. Child .5 must retain sidebar.surface = yazi before implementation. If child .5 chooses radar | none, close this bead; create no radar-columns replacement unless the user separately chooses that direction. Forest affects the evidence in child .5 but adds no scope here.

External UX reference at TUIOS revision 4cc64e58daee7faa872790d185e29d108e7dd461: its niri-style horizontal scrolling layout is summarized at https://github.com/Gaurav-Gosain/tuios/blob/4cc64e58daee7faa872790d185e29d108e7dd461/README.md#tiling. Use it only as comparison evidence during this already-approved slice, not as a dependency or authorization to reproduce its window manager. If Yazi survives v1, dogfood whether a fixed sidebar plus horizontally navigated work columns solves real narrow-width pressure better than the planned finite columns swap pair. The accepted implementation remains the smallest Zellij-native contract. Stop and keep the finite pair if an infinite strip requires broad fork work, new pane geometry ownership, or a second layout engine. TUIOS aggregate-window navigation belongs with the separate agent command-center investigation, not in the permanent rail or this layout bead.
close_reason: Nova v1 freezes the current tiled-Yazi layout and Nova v2 removes that rail. A new columns mode has no supported release window, so the user chose not to expand the v1 sidebar surface.

title: Evaluate remaining Starship integration improvements
description: Audit the open Starship request against Nova’s existing managed Starship config, live defaults, Nushell integration, and bar facts, then identify any remaining user-visible gap. Keep existing ownership intact and avoid a second prompt materializer.
acceptance_criteria: Inventory the behavior already delivered by Nova and the unmet request behind issue #640. Close as satisfied if no concrete gap remains; otherwise define one owner and one focused implementation bead with a user-visible verification path. Do not duplicate Starship configuration ownership.
notes: Reviewed classic issue #640 and Nova’s managed Starship chain. The classic issue is closed and contains no concrete requirement beyond investigating Starship. Nova already owns one Nu materializer and sparse starship.toml overrides; the remaining discoverability gap is satisfied by yazelix-5vl-core-all-config-discovery-lsw.6 without introducing another owner.
close_reason: Satisfied: no separate integration gap remains after the packaged-schema discovery slice; Nova keeps one Starship materializer and one sparse override owner.

title: Make doctor and status read-only
description:
## Accepted scope — 2026-09-07

DIAGNOSTICS-READ-ONLY-001: A user invoking yzx doctor (including --verbose) or yzx status (including --json) observes configuration and runtime state without Nova creating, overwriting or repairing files, initializing Rio, generating Zellij files or seeding plugin permissions. Missing runtime state remains missing and is reported with the existing launch action; invalid input fails without mutation. Preserve configured values, JSON schema 1 and existing validation/diagnostic ownership.

The user explicitly chose removal of preparation from diagnostics, with initialization retained in existing launch/run commands. No new public CLI action, repair mode or generic framework is selected. Correct the shared preparation boundary for doctor and both status formats. Configuration/sidecar validation keeps one owner; rendering may occur in memory without materialization.

This is shared Linux/Darwin behavior. Keep launch/run preparation intact, including native permissions, generated layouts, sidecar validation and new-session appearance policy. No ambient agent hooks or trust may be changed.

Verification: one packaged regression covers fresh roots, populated/custom config and invalid config/sidecars, compares the filesystem before/after diagnostics, and proves an existing execution command still prepares usable files. Adapt existing materialization checks to invoke execution instead of relying on status writes. Run relevant local checks, flake/package and isolated-install proof, exact Linux CI and Darwin Package Smoke; update documentation/changelog/LOC and the installed Edge runtime. No GUI or main/stable promotion.
acceptance_criteria: All doctor/status forms leave isolated config/state trees unchanged on fresh, configured and invalid inputs; outputs remain truthful and failures preserve recovery evidence. Existing run/launch paths retain preparation. JSON schema remains 1. Existing sidecar/key/layout/permission and package-variant contracts pass. Exact Linux and Darwin package gates and isolated installed command proof pass. README/runtime notes/CHANGELOG/LOC reflect the boundary; no new public command or automatic repair.
notes:
Implemented DIAGNOSTICS-READ-ONLY-001 in the shared Runtime resolver: diagnostics resolve and validate in memory; existing launch/run preparation owns writes. The internal Zellij scalar helper returns merged text and the runtime owns the final config write. No new public command or repair mode.

The packaged regression snapshots paths, contents and modification times for all four diagnostic forms on fresh, configured, invalid-root, invalid-sidecar and invalid-state cases, then proves yzx run still prepares files. It fails on the previously installed artifact and passes with the change. A state path occupied by a file retains its failure diagnostic through read-only metadata validation; removing mkdir alone was insufficient.

Local packaged contracts and launcher unit checks pass. Shared package, exact-revision Linux/Darwin, isolated installation and installed Edge refresh evidence remain pending. README, architecture, runtime notes, changelog and tracked-text scorecards describe the accepted behavior. No GUI launch or channel promotion is part of this change.

title: Remove legacy cursor JSONC configuration
description:
## Outcome

Complete in the current Yazelix Cursors child revision `f97d0e7`.

## Evidence

`rg -n 'settings\.jsonc|jsonc-parser|load_cursor_settings_jsonc|render_cursor_settings_jsonc' . --glob '!target/**'` returns no matches in `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/cursors` at `f97d0e7`.

The child therefore has no live JSONC cursor path, parser dependency, migration helper, or documented dual-owner surface matching this bead.

## Boundary

This closure proves absence only in the inspected child revision. It does not claim that unrelated historical changelogs or external released consumers have been rewritten.
acceptance_criteria:
[x] No live `settings.jsonc` cursor configuration path remains.
[x] No JSONC cursor parser/render/migration symbol remains.
[x] The current child uses TOML as its persisted cursor configuration format.
notes: Classic TOML migration and the Nova cursor bridge are complete.
